items.title: NEXUS RESORT & SPA KARAMBUNAI, COMBINING DISTINCT LUXURY WITH AUTHENTIC SABAHAN HOSPITALITY
items.content:
Photo Credit: Nexus Resort Karambunai

Nexus Resort & Spa Karambunai, nestled within its own 3,335-acre peninsula, pleasantly combines distinct luxury and authentic Sabahan hospitality. Take in the beauty of our tropical tree-lined driveway leading to the stunning, ethnic-inspired grand lobby as the gentle chimes of local musical instruments set the mood for the perfect beach getaway. Spacious and impeccable landscapes surround all 325 elegantly appointed guestrooms, while a vast range of dining options are available to cater to all. The choices to relax and pamper yourself are endless at Nexus Resort & Spa Karambunai. The award-winning 18-hole championship golf course and exclusive Borneo Spa complement the superb facilities of this magnificent resort which boasts eight restaurants and bars and an almost endless array of leisure and recreational activities for all. With its impressive banqueting and conference facilities, it is ideal for both leisure and business travellers.

Location: Off Jalan Sepangar Bay, Karambunai, Sabah

Distance to City Centre: ~28 km (about 45 minutes) from central Kota Kinabalu

Distance to Airport: ~35 km (about 60 minutes by car from Kota Kinabalu International Airport)


OUR ROOMS

Photo Credit: Nexus Resort Karambunai


Borneo Wing: 64 units of Borneo Garden, 22 units of Borneo Seaview, and 4 units of Executive Suite

Ocean Wing: 64 units of Ocean Deluxe, 38 units of Ocean Nexus Deluxe and 132 units of Ocean Premier

Luxury Villas: 1 unit Presidential Penthouse


Photo Credit: Nexus Resort Karambunai


18-Hole Championship Golf Course:

Nexus Golf Karambunai is one of the premier golf courses on the island of Borneo, specifically in Kota Kinabalu, Sabah. It is located within walking distance from Nexus Resort & Spa Karambunai. Designed by the world-renowned American golf course architect, Ronald Fream, Nexus Golf Karambunai is an international championship par 72, 18-hole golf course. It has established itself as one of the most popular golf courses in Sabah for its unique location and design which offers golfers a challenging and enjoyable experience. Nestled between the million-year-old rainforest and the South China Sea, golfers can enjoy the breathtaking views of Mount Kinabalu and the white sandy beach of Karambunai.  The tract’s key characteristics are its undulating fairways and its well-contoured greens across a series of small lakes, waterways, and hillocks — ingeniously crafted to add to its varying degree of difficulty.


Photo Credit: Nexus Resort Karambunai


Facilities & Activities

Pools - 3 outdoor lagoon-style swimming pools, including a kids' pool:

  • Kids Pool: Specifically designed for children below 7 years old, offering a safe, shallow, and highly family-friendly environment.
  • Activity & Adult Pool: Features a depth of 1.2 meters, making it safe for casual swimming and splashing while deep enough to lounge.
  • Design: The three pools connect into a single flowing complex, allowing parents to easily relax on a sunbed while keeping an eye on the children across the different sections.

Features & Amenities

  • Waterslides: The pools are equipped with a few gentle, mini-sized waterslides perfectly sized for younger children.
  • Swim-Up Bar: Features a swim-up bar (Splashes Pool Bar) where you can order tropical drinks and Ice-Cream
  • Floating Rentals: A kiosk is available by the pool where you can rent pool rings and inflatables for a small fee.
  • Towel Service: Complimentary towels are typically provided for hotel guests at the poolside.

Photo Credit: Nexus Resort Karambunai


Recreation: Kayaking, Surfing, Cycling, Nature walk, Batik painting and the Nexie Kids Club.

Nexus Resort & Spa Karambunai offers a host of activities for individuals, families, the young, and the old. Whether you are looking for an idyllic spot to relax, a place to discover the beauty of nature, an outdoor stage to enjoy a performance, or a scenic stretch for you to cycle along, you will be able to find these and more at Nexus Resort & Spa Karambunai.

On land or water, the choices are many and varied. The sprawling outdoor area allows the resort to infuse adventure into your stay, as there is never a dull moment at Nexus Resort & Spa Karambunai.

You can bask under the sun and enjoy the beauty of nature with Nexus Resort & Spa Karambunai’s menu of family-friendly water sports and recreational activities. Delight in the clear, turquoise blue waters of the South China Sea on a kayak, or just laze around in hammocks or bean bags.


Photo Credit: Nexus Resort Karambunai


Wellness: Borneo Spa for traditional massages and wellness treatments.

Borneo Spa inspires relaxation, rejuvenation, and a harmonious equilibrium of body, mind, and spirit through holistic treatments that combine time-tested therapies.

Drawn from age-old traditions of nature healing from both East and West, Borneo Spa strongly believes that by synergising the richness and wonders of nature with the highest standards of all-inclusive holistic therapy, a change of lifestyle for better health and well-being can be attained.

Embark on a healing journey through the wonders and richness of Mother Nature in Borneo with a selection of relaxing, rejuvenating, and soothing treatments available.


Photo Credit: Nexus Resort Karambunai

Dining Options: 8 distinct venues including the Penyu and Kingfisher Restaurants (serving daily buffets), Splashes Pool Bar, and the Sunset Bar & Grill for dining right on the beach.

items.title: THE RED BRICKS OF BUKIT NANAS: A JOURNEY THROUGH KUALA LUMPUR'S CATHOLIC HERITAGE
items.content:
The humid air of Bukit Nanas carries a certain weight, a blend of damp forest earth and the scent of old stone. 

Tucked away from the glass-and-steel glare of modern Kuala Lumpur, a row of weathered red bricks stands as a silent witness to a century of footsteps.

This is not just a street but also a corridor of memory where the echoes of school bells and choir hymns still linger in the heat.


Photo credit: KL The Guide

St. John’s Institution

The journey begins where the red-and-white arches of St. John’s Institution curve along the hillside. Built in 1904, the building feels less like a school and more like a fortress of knowledge. 

Sunlight filters through the corridors, catching the dust motes that dance where generations of "Johannians" once sprinted to class.

While historically a bastion for boys, there is a subtle shift in the rhythm here. 

In the higher forms, the sea of white and green uniforms welcomes girls into the fold, blending the school’s rigid tradition with a more inclusive present.

It is a place of sharp collars and even sharper heritage.


Photo credit: KL The Guide

St. John’s Cathedral

Just a stone’s throw away, the whitewashed walls of the Cathedral of St. John the Evangelist offer a stark, peaceful contrast to the fiery bricks of the school. 

Inside, the city's traffic noise dies away, replaced by the cool, hollow stillness of high ceilings. 

The Parisian stained glass casts fractured patterns of ruby and sapphire across the pews, looking like a vibrant, silent storytelling that has watched over the hill since the late 1800s.


Photo credit: KL The Guide

Further along the slope, the legacy branches out. St. John’s International School carries the same name but speaks a different language of education. 

Here, the halls are shared equally by boys and girls from the very start, a co-educational hum that brings a youthful energy to the ancient hill

It is the evolution of the Lasallian spirit, which means retaining the discipline of the past while looking toward a global horizon.

The Walk Behind the Greenery

To walk this path is to experience a specific kind of KL time travel. 

On one side, the primitive jungle of the forest reserve threatens to reclaim the pavement, while on the other, the Catholic heritage stands firm.

  • The Texture: Rough bricks, smooth marble, and the iron-wrought gates.

  • The Sound: The distant hum of the LRT mixed with the rustle of tropical leaves.

  • The Sight: The KL Tower peeks over the gothic spires, a reminder of how fast the world moves outside this sanctuary.

The red bricks of Bukit Nanas do not just hold up roofs but also hold a narrative. 

It is a story of faith, a story of scholars, and a story of a city that, despite its rush to the future, still keeps its heart tucked away on a quiet, emerald hill.

items.title: A SWEET ESCAPE FOR FAMILIES, FRIENDS AND WEEKEND FUN SEEKERS
items.content:
Some weekends call for something simple: sunshine, laughter, splashes of water and a full day away from the usual routine. Whether you are planning a family day out, a catch up session with friends, or a school holiday activity that keeps everyone entertained, a waterpark day always has a way of bringing out the fun side in people.

Located in Gamuda Cove, SplashMania Waterpark has become one of the most popular waterparks near Kuala Lumpur for families, young adults and groups looking for a refreshing day trip in Selangor. This season, the park feels even more cheerful as it celebrates SplashMania Birthday Bash 2026 with a playful Candyland Tea Party theme.


Photo credit: GL Play

Instead of walking into an ordinary waterpark setup, guests can expect colourful Birthday Bash decorations, sweet inspired props and photo worthy corners around the park. Think pastel colours, lollipop style displays, giant dessert elements and charming birthday touches that make the experience feel fun before you even get on a slide.

For families with children, this is the kind of outing that works well because the day can move at your own pace. Kids can enjoy water play areas, family friendly slides and splash zones, while parents get to join in the fun or take a breather between activities. It is a good option for parents searching for things to do with kids in KL, family activities in Selangor, or school holiday ideas near Kuala Lumpur.


Photo credit: GL Play

For those who prefer something more energetic, SplashMania also offers thrill-focused attractions such as Plunge, Monsta and Maniac Racer. These are the rides that turn a normal weekend outing into the kind of day where everyone compares who screamed the loudest. For friend groups, couples and young adults, it is an easy way to turn the usual cafe plan into something more memorable.

Photo credit: GL Play

Photo credit: GL Play

Of course, no lifestyle outing is complete without photos. With the Birthday Bash decorations adding a brighter and more whimsical look to the park, guests can capture plenty of cheerful moments between rides. From entrance displays to Candyland-inspired corners, the whole experience gives visitors more than just water slides. It gives them a reason to slow down, snap a few memories and enjoy the atmosphere.


Photo credit:  GL Play 

The celebration also comes with a limited-time online exclusive offer. From now until 31 July 2026, guests can enjoy Buy 1 Free 1 SplashMania tickets when they purchase online at glplay.com.my. For families, best friends or group outings, this makes it an even better time to plan a visit.

Whether you are looking for a waterpark near KL, a fun family day out in Selangor, or a weekend activity that everyone can enjoy together, SplashMania Birthday Bash offers a cheerful mix of thrills, water play, birthday-themed decorations and great value.


Photo credit:  GL Play

SplashMania Birthday Bash 2026 is happening now until 31 July 2026 at SplashMania, Gamuda Cove. Tickets are available online at glplay.com.my.

items.title: IS YOUR CHEAP LUGGAGE TOXIC? THE HIDDEN CONCERNS LURKING INSIDE YOUR SUITCASE
items.content:
There is a distinct moment when packing for a long-awaited holiday shifts from excitement to careful preparation.

Flights are booked, itineraries are finalized, and travelers invest in everything from comfortable footwear to premium skincare products. Yet one of the most important travel essentials often receives surprisingly little attention: the suitcase itself.

Photo credit: The Travel Store

According to travel specialists at The Travel Store, many consumers focus heavily on appearance and price while overlooking the materials used inside their luggage:

Why Does Some Luggage Smell So Strong?

If you have ever opened a newly purchased suitcase and noticed a sharp chemical smell, you are not alone.

These odors are often associated with manufacturing materials, including adhesives, coatings, dyes, and synthetic fabrics used during production. Heat can intensify these smells, especially when luggage is left inside a car boot, storage room, or poorly ventilated space.

While the presence of an odor does not automatically indicate a serious health risk, many travelers prefer luggage made with higher-quality materials that minimize unpleasant smells and provide a more comfortable travel experience.

For individuals who are particularly sensitive to strong scents or chemical odors, prolonged exposure in confined spaces may cause discomfort, making material quality an important factor to consider when selecting travel gear.

Photo credit: The Travel Store

More Than Just a Comfort Issue

Beyond material quality, cheaper luggage often faces another challenge: durability.

Frequent travelers know that a suitcase is subjected to considerable stress throughout its lifetime. Wheels encounter uneven surfaces, handles are repeatedly extended and retracted, and luggage shells endure constant impacts during transit.

Lower-quality bags may show signs of wear more quickly, leading many consumers to replace them sooner than expected. This cycle of frequent replacement contributes to unnecessary waste and increased long-term costs.

Brands that prioritize durability, repairability, and long-term performance offer a different approach. Replaceable wheels, serviceable handles, reinforced corners, and durable shell materials can significantly extend a suitcase's lifespan.

Photo credit: The Travel Store

Travel Smarter, Waste Less

As sustainability becomes increasingly important to modern travelers, longevity has become one of the most valuable features a suitcase can offer.

Choosing luggage designed to last for years rather than seasons helps reduce landfill waste while delivering better long-term value. Repairing worn components instead of replacing an entire suitcase can further extend its usefulness.

When a suitcase eventually reaches the end of its journey, recycling or repurposing its materials can help reduce environmental impact and support a more sustainable travel lifestyle.

The Bottom Line

A suitcase does far more than carry your belongings from one destination to another.

The materials inside, the durability of its construction, and its ability to withstand years of travel all play a roles in the overall experience.

Before choosing the cheapest option available, travelers may want to look beyond the price tag and consider what their luggage is made of, how long it is likely to last, and whether it is designed for the journeys still ahead.

items.title: EXPLORING AUTHENTIC ZAMBIAN FOOD: A CULTURAL LUNCH EXPERIENCE WITH OUR KLTHEGUIDE TEAM
items.content:
There’s a specific kind of magic that happens when an editorial team stops rushing.
Most days behind the KLTG desk, our workspace is a battleground of glowing laptop screens, half-edited drafts of city trails, and half-cold coffees. 

We are constantly chasing the city's pulse.

But today, the frantic rhythm of typing suddenly dissolved, replaced by something deeply grounding: the rich, aromatic steam of an authentic Zambian feast.

We didn’t just take a lunch break.

We flipped open a hidden palate passport and went on an unscripted, one-day culinary travel journey across the globe without leaving our chairs.

Breaking the Bread of Africa

At the absolute center of our table sat a massive, pristine mound of steaming Nshima.

In Zambian culture, Nshima isn't just a side dish; it is the literal and emotional anchor of life.

Made from ground maize white cornmeal that is vigorously whipped into a dense, smooth porridge-like, it holds a comforting heat.

There’s a beautiful, tactile intimacy to eating it. It gently demands that you abandon your cutlery and embrace a hands-on heritage.

We watched each other try it for the first time, taking a small piece, kneading it in the palm of our hand until it became a pliable little disc, and then shaping it into a scoop to catch the sauces.

Image Source : BGOC Internal

Right beside it was a golden platter of Egg Fried Rice.
While not traditionally Zambian, it sat there like a gentle, familiar bridge between cultures.
Flecked with soft egg and savory seasoning, it provided a welcoming, neutral baseline that made the bold, exotic flavors around it feel right at home.

Image Source : BGOC Internal

Stews That Tell a Story

The Oxtail was a masterclass in patience.

Slow-simmered for hours until the gelatinous meat literally dissolved off the bone at the touch of a finger, it was bathed in a rich, glossy, deeply savory reduction.

Pouring that luxurious gravy over the Nshima felt like a warm hug on a rainy afternoon.

Image Source : BGOC Internal

To balance the decadence of the meat, we passed around the bowl of Chilemba.

This hearty bean stew is a staple of Zambian home-cooking.

The sugar beans are boiled slowly with onions and tomatoes until they reach a velvety, melt-in-your-mouth texture, creating a thick, earthy broth that carries a subtle, natural sweetness. 

Image Source : BGOC Internal

The Green Canvas: Visashi and Rape

Zambian cuisine has a brilliant way of treating vegetables not as an afterthought, but as a highlight.

We fell in love with Visashi.

It’s a traditional dish where leafy green vegetables are stewed down in a rich, creamy sauce made from raw, pounded peanuts or groundnuts.

Image Source : BGOC Internal

Next to it was Rape, which is savory, sautéed mustard greens.
Kept simple and flash-fried with just a hint of oil, tomatoes, and onions, it preserved its bright, peppery bite.
It acted as the perfect, crisp palate cleanser between the richer, heavier stews.

Image Source : BGOC Internal

New Textures That Sparked the Room

As a part of publication, we live for the moments that surprise us.

The real magic of the afternoon happened when we ventured into the authentic delicacies, turning our lunch into a playful sensory lab.

First was Kapenta.

These tiny, sun-dried fish from Lake Tanganyika were shallow-fried with onions and tomatoes until they achieved an immaculate, golden crisp.

Each bite delivered an intense, smoky burst of umami and a satisfying crunch that had us reaching back into the bowl like we were eating gourmet chips.

Image Source : BGOC Internal

Next was Delele. This unique okra dish introduced us to a whole new texture.
Cooked with a touch of bicarbonate of soda to give it a wonderfully smooth, slippery, and viscous consistency, it is traditionally designed to help the dense Nshima slide down smoothly.
Image Source : BGOC Internal
Then came the true showstopper, the Vinkubala, which are sautéed mopane worms.
Seasoned perfectly and fried until crisp, they gave off a deeply earthy, nutty flavor with a distinct crunch.
Trying them became a beautiful test of shared courage for the team. 

Image Source : BGOC Internal

Why We Keep Exploring.

This lunch reminded us why we do what we do.

The best travel stories aren’t found by looking at a map from a distance.

Because, behind the KLTG desk, we are simply people who love the poetry of discovery. 

Until the next adventure,

From our family table to yours.

items.title: MY HERO ACADEMIA FINAL SEASON POP-UP STORE DEBUTS IN MALAYSIA AT SUNGEI WANG PLAZA
items.content:
Photo Credit: Sungei Wang Plaza

Fans of My Hero Academia can look forward to an exciting new experience as the My Hero Academia Final Season Pop-Up Store makes its official debut in Malaysia. Organized by Medialink Group Limited (Medialink Malaysia), the limited-time activation will take place at Sungei Wang Plaza from 27 May to 17 June 2026.

Held in conjunction with the Malaysian school holiday season, the pop-up store offers fans an immersive retail and experiential journey inspired by the Final Season of the globally acclaimed anime series.


Event Highlights

Photo Credit: Sungei Wang Plaza

Extensive Official Merchandise:

Explore over 100 SKUs of official merchandise, including newly released Final Season items and “Event Exclusive Only” items available in Malaysia for the first time. The collection caters to both dedicated collectors.

Explore over 100 officially licensed merchandise items on-site, including newly released Final Season collections and “event-exclusive” items making their debut in Malaysia. With a wide variety of products available, both dedicated collectors and casual anime fans will find something they love.

Photo Credit: Sungei Wang Plaza

Immersive Themed Zones & Photo Opportunities

 The pop-up features a series of curated environments designed to bring the anime to life, including:

●      Plus Ultra Backdrop

●      Villain Zone

●      Pro Hero Photo Area

●      Class 1-A Graduation Photo Area

●      Final Season Scene Gallery

Fan Engagement Activation – Message Wall

 A dedicated Sticky Note Wall allows fans to leave messages, thoughts, and appreciation for the series, creating a collective tribute to the Final Season and its creators.

Interactive Game – Quirk Assessment Spin-to-Win

 Visitors can participate in a themed game experience at RM50 per play, where they can discover their “Quirk” and win exclusive prizes valued at up to RM120.

Gacha Collectable Card Series

An on-site gacha experience introduces a collectable card series, encouraging fans to build and expand their own hero collection.

Limited Edition Redemption

Shoppers who spend RM150 and above will be eligible to redeem a Limited Edition Holographic Laser Ticket, featuring key visuals from the Final Season showdown between Deku and Shigaraki.


Photo Credit: Sungei Wang Plaza

Official Statement

“We’re excited to bring the Final Season experience of My Hero Academia to Malaysia for the very first time. Together with our venue partner, Sungai Wang Plaza, this pop-up is designed not just as a retail space, but as a place where fans can fully immerse themselves in the world of heroes, celebrate the series, and create memorable moments together,” said Vince Ng, Licensing Director of Medialink Malaysia.

Strengthening Malaysia's Anime Culture 

The debut of the My Hero Academia Final Season Pop-Up Store reflects the continued growth of anime fandom in Malaysia. It reinforces the country’s position as an emerging hub for anime & IP culture experiences. With its strategic timing during the school holidays, the event is expected to attract strong footfall from fans, families, and the wider public.


Photo Credit: Sungei Wang Plaza

Event Details

●               Event: My Hero Academia Final Season Pop-Up Store

●               Date: 27 May – 17 June 2026

●               Venue : Sungei Wang Plaza (Venue Partner)

●               Organiser: Medialink Group Limited (Medialink Malaysia)

●               Media Partner: 8TV

  

About MY Hero Academia

My Hero Academia is a globally acclaimed Japanese anime series produced by Bones Inc., set in a world where the majority of the population possesses superpowers known as “Quirks.” The story follows Izuku Midoriya (Deku), a boy born without powers who rises to become a hero after inheriting the legendary ability “One For All” from the Symbol of Peace, All Might.

The anime chronicles Midoriya’s journey at U.A. High School alongside Class 1-A, as they train to become professional heroes while facing increasingly powerful villains led by Tomura Shigaraki. The narrative evolves from school life into large-scale conflicts that explore themes of justice, responsibility, and heroism.

The series features many iconic arcs and scenes, including the U.A. Sports Festival, the Kamino Incident (All Might vs All For One), Endeavour’s battle against the High-End Nomu, and the Paranormal Liberation War.

Now entering its Final Season, the story reaches its climactic conclusion, focusing on the decisive battle between heroes and villains, including the long-anticipated showdown between Deku and Shigaraki.

Widely recognized for its dynamic animation and strong storytelling, My Hero Academia remains one of the most influential anime titles worldwide.


About Medialink

Medialink Group Limited (Stock Code: 2230.HK) is a leading intellectual property (IP) management company headquartered in Hong Kong, with operations spanning China, India, Japan, and Southeast Asia. The Group is committed to promoting cultural exchange across the region through a diverse portfolio of IPs, delivering high-quality entertainment content to the Asian market. Malaysia serves as one of the Group’s key subsidiaries in Southeast Asia.

Founded in 1994, its business mainly focuses on content distribution and brand licensing, and is also involved in content production, distribution arrangements and animation product development. The Group invests and cooperates closely with media content licensors to distribute media content related to animation, variety shows, TV dramas, animated and live-action movies. At the same time, it also obtains copyright licensing from various brand licensors in the Asia-Pacific region, including merchandising rights, location-based entertainment rights and promotion rights.

The Group has its own animation brand, its various Ani-One® YouTube channels (including Ani-One® Asia, which is Asia-focused, Ani-One® 中文官方頻道, which is run in Chinese, and other Southeast Asia channels – Ani-One® Thailand, Ani-One® Philippines and Ani-One® Vietnam) have more than 5 million subscribers and more than 980 million views. In addition, the Group also has its own e-commerce platform, Ani-Mall®, selling animation products and an exclusive anime boutique.


About Sungei Wang Plaza

Sungei Wang Plaza positions itself as a beauty and experiential shopping hub in the heart of Kuala Lumpur with a variety of choices in Optical Services & Products.

Boutique Fashion & Fashion Accessories, Hair Salon, Beauty Salon, Manicure & Pedicure, Beauty Products, Athleisure, Entertainment, Digital Lifestyle, Toys & Hobbies, Art & Craft and Speciality Stores. For nearly five decades, Sungei Wang has been more than a shopping destination; it's been a cultural and community landmark in Kuala Lumpur. The mall has an aggregate retail floor area of approximately 800,000 square feet (sq. ft.) and key anchor tenants include Cold Storage, JUMPA@Sungei Wang, Blastacars, Camp5, MR DIY and Mega Star Arena Kuala Lumpur. Mega Star Arena Kuala Lumpur is a 5,000-capacity concert hall seamlessly integrated into the mall, captivating audiences with exceptional world-class concerts and events, solidifying its position as a vibrant hub within Bukit Bintang.

 

Sungei Wang Plaza has received many local and international awards and accolades over the years, including the Gold Award for Best Experiential Marketing by the Malaysia Shopping Malls Association (PPKM) Awards 2024-2025, Most Number of Optical Shops in a Shopping Mall by The Malaysia Book of Records, TripAdvisor Travelers’ Choice Award 2024, Special Award for Best Shopping Mall by the Mayor of Kuala Lumpur for Outstanding Lightings Design 2024, Silver Award for Best Experiential Marketing by the Malaysia Shopping Malls Association (PPKM) Awards 2023-2024, Leading Brand in Strata Title Mall awarded by The ASEAN Master Class Award in December 2023, the winner of the Best Managed Sustainable Property in the Retail category (10 years and above) awarded by The Edge Malaysia in July 2023, The BrandLaureate BestBrands Awards 2021-2022, Nation's Pride Brand of the Year in Nation's Most ICONIC & Renowned Mall, Kuala Lumpur Mayor’s Tourism Awards 2011 Award for Excellence in Shopping Mall Category and the prestigious FIABCI Prix d'Excellence under the Special Award (Retail Properties Category) in 1996. items.title: LUNCH IN CHERAS, DINNER IN BANGKOK: THE ESCAPE TO A'HAN ORIENTAL
items.content:
Have you ever found yourself sitting in your car during the peak of the evening rush hour in Kuala Lumpur, watching the red taillights stretch out endlessly ahead of you, and felt an overwhelming urge to just escape?

Perhaps to a quiet mountain village or a tranquil waterfront sanctuary where the mind can finally rest. 

Luckily, you do not need a boarding pass to find this sanctuary. 

You only need to step across the hills of Cheras into Sungai Long and cross the threshold of A’Han Thai Seafood, a highly sought-after Pork-free Thai restaurant in Cheras located within the vibrant Monkeys Canopy resort.

PHOTO CREDIT: A'Han Thai Seafood

Architectural Craftsmanship Across the Water at Monkeys Canopy

Officially recognised as the region's first and largest pork-free Thai floating pavilion restaurant in ASEAN, this unique Thai seafood restaurant masterfully creates a profound sense of deep emotional intimacy rather than relying solely on overwhelming commercial grandeur. 

Every structural corner is softened through the thoughtful integration of warm, ambient lighting and intricate, hand-carved Thai woodwork. 

For those planning a meal, the layout is divided into distinct zones that offer a completely immersive floating pavilion dining experience:
  • Private Floating Pavilions: Sectioned off over the water, these spaces are perfect for those seeking solitary reflection or looking for a memorable place for family gatherings in Cheras. Surrounded by the gentle lap of the pond and the rustle of the hill breeze, the outside world ceases to exist.
PHOTO CREDIT: A'Han Thai Seafood
The Culinary Ritual: Authentic Pork-Free Thai Food in Selangor

As featured by KL The Guide, this lakeside retreat replaces the conventional formality of standard fine dining with a focus on shared presence and authentic connection.

This philosophy is best experienced through their traditional Khantoke-style dining. 

PHOTO CREDIT: A'Han Thai Seafood

Originating from the historic Lanna Kingdom of Northern Thailand, Khantoke is a style of service where an array of small, complementary dishes is served together on a traditional round wooden table.

The physical act of reaching across, passing dishes, and sampling different flavour profiles naturally sparks conversation and breaks down social walls, making A’Han Thai Seafood one of the most interactive choices for pork-free Thai food in Selangor.

The menu explores the bold, layered flavours of Thai cuisine through dishes rooted in regional traditions, overseen by a dedicated team of chefs from Thailand. 

A Ritual of Light: The Seasonal Krathong Experience

What elevates an evening from a simple dinner into a lasting memory is the invitation to become an active participant in a living cultural tradition. 

PHOTO CREDIT: A'Han Thai Seafood

During special seasonal events and cultural celebrations, A’Han Thai Seafood introduces guests to the quiet, beautiful tradition of the Krathong.

During these exclusive event periods, you can take a small, delicately handmade floating vessel constructed from natural elements, carefully light its small candle, whisper a private wish into the night air, and gently release it onto the water.

It provides a rare moment of absolute stillness, a physical manifestation of letting go of your daily worries, stress, and the chaotic speed of urban life. 

For anyone searching for an authentic Thai restaurant in Cheras or a scenic sunset dinner spot in Selangor, keeping an eye out for the seasonal cultural nights at Monkeys Canopy offers an escape that lingers long after the evening ends.

Location: Lot 683, Jalan Persiaran Sungai Long, Sungai Long, Cheras, Selangor, Malaysia

Reservations & Updates: To plan your visit, explore their full pork-free Thai menu, or check the availability of their next seasonal cultural event, you can browse updates directly on the official A'Han Oriental Website.

items.title: A DAY IN KL WITHOUT A CAR: HOW TO MAKE YOUR 10,000 STEPS WORTH IT
items.content:
Who says you need a Grab to see the best of Kuala Lumpur?

In a city known for its humidity and traffic jams, I decided to ditch the four-wheelers and explore three of KL’s most iconic spots, such as Petaling Street (Pasar Seni), KL Forest Eco Park (Bukit Nanas), and Pavilion Bukit Bintang, by using nothing but my feet and the rail system.

Here’s how it went.

Stop 1: The Soul of the Heritage District (Pasar Seni)

Arriving by the RapidKL Bus. The day begins as the bus pulls into the terminal, dropping you right into a pocket of the city where time moves a little slower. 

Stepping off, the air is immediately different; you can feel something thick with the scent of charcoal-toasted bread and the humid, lived-in history of Chinatown.

Walking through Pasar Seni, you meet the "real" KL. 

It’s in the way the morning light hits the turquoise facade of Central Market and how the vendors meticulously arrange their stalls of hand-painted batik and wood carvings.

It feels authentic. You are not just a tourist; you're part of a 130-year-old rhythm. 

Every step toward Petaling Street reveals a new texture.

A hidden mural, a red lantern swaying in the breeze, or a stall selling cooling herbal tea. 

By the time you’ve explored the alleys, you have easily clocked your first 3,000 steps without even trying.


Stop 2: The City’s Forest (KL Forest Eco Park / Bukit Nanas)

A transition via the KTM Komuter / LRT lines toward the city’s green lungs. To make a 10,000-step goal truly worth it, you have to find the shade. 

The transition from the concrete heat of the market to the lush gates of the KL Forest Eco Park is a literal breath of fresh air.

Standing at the entrance, you realise that KL is not just a concrete jungle. 

It is also a city built around nature. 

Even if you don't head deep into the trails, just being at the foot of this permanent forest reserve offers a sensory reset. 

The towering trees provide a massive natural canopy that gives you the second wind you need to finish the challenge.

Entrance Fees (Per Entry):

For Malaysians (MyKad Holders):

  • Adults: RM 10.00

  • Children (6–12 years): RM 1.00

  • Senior Citizens (60+): RM 1.00

  • Children (Under 6) & Persons with Disabilities: FREE

For International Visitors:

  • Adults: RM 40.00

  • Children (6–12 years): RM 5.00

  • Senior Citizens (60+): RM 40.00 (Standard Adult Rate)

  • Children (Under 6) & Persons with Disabilities: FREE


Stop 3: The Metropolitan Hub  (Pavilion Bukit Bintang)

Hopping on the Purple GoKL Bus for a free ride into the city's glittering centre. The final leg leads to the "Beating Heart" of modern Malaysia. 

As the bus weaves through the afternoon traffic, the scenery transforms. 

You leave behind the heritage bricks and forest vines for high-definition digital screens and towering glass.

Standing outside the Pavilion, the energy is infectious. 

You will encounter a whirlwind of cultures, such as locals rushing to dinner, tourists marvelling at the Crystal Fountain, and street performers adding a soundtrack to the hustle.

It feels vibrant, diverse, and endlessly alive. Crossing that street at Bukit Bintang is the ultimate reward. 

So there you go, you have navigated from a 19th-century market to a 21st-century landmark on your own two feet.

Are You Ready to Step Up?

Kuala Lumpur is a city that deserves to be felt, not just seen from a car window. 

You do not need a heavy budget or a private driver to experience the vibrant energy of Malaysia.

You just need a pair of comfortable shoes and a transit map.

  1. Grab a Touch 'n Go card and use the LRT or GoKL bus.

  2. Stop at that random kopitiam or take the long way through the forest entrance.

  3. Capture your journey and show the world that the best way to see KL is one step at a time.

Don't just commute through KL but also walk through its history. 

Take the 10,000 Step Challenge today! Your next adventure is just a bus stop away.

items.title: WELCOME TO BASECAMP - BUILT FOR CHALLENGE
items.content:
Most attractions give you fun.

BaseCamp gives you something different: pressure situations wrapped in fun.

It is designed around one core psychological trigger a competitive survival energy. The moment you step in, your brain stops treating it like “just a game” and shifts into instinct, coordination, and split-second decision-making.

It’s not about watching something happen.
It’s about being inside the moment where everything is happening at once.

Photo credit: Monkeys Canopy

Photo credit: Monkeys Canopy

The Games - Multiple Ways to Break Comfort Zones

Photo credit: Monkeys Canopy

BaseCamp isn’t a single experience. It’s a rotation of tactical, physical, and high-energy game modes designed to test different skills:

  • Paintball is a classic combat scenario where strategy, cover, and communication decide everything
Photo credit: Monkeys Canopy

  • Archery Tag makes you dodge, aim, and react in a fast-paced hybrid of archery and dodgeball
Photo credit: Monkeys Canopy

  • Water Tag will be chaotic, refreshing, and unpredictable, where movement matters as much as accuracy
Photo credit: Monkeys Canopy

  • Zorbing is a full-body fun where rolling, bumping, and balance turn into pure comedy and chaos
Photo credit: Monkeys Canopy

  • Team-Building Challenges are structured missions designed to test leadership, trust, and group coordination under pressure
Photo credit: Monkeys Canopy

Each game strips away routine thinking and replaces it with instinct, laughter, and adrenaline-driven decision-making.

More Than Just BaseCamp - It’s a Full Day at Monkeys Canopy

Photo credit: Monkeys Canopy

Photo credit: Monkeys Canopy

What makes BaseCamp even more powerful is its location inside Monkeys Canopy.

Because this isn’t a one-stop activity, but it’s part of a full experience ecosystem.

While squads are locked into battle at BaseCamp, family members and friends can turn the day into a shared destination with different energy levels for everyone, some compete, some relax, but everyone connects back over the same experience.

It’s rare to find a place where chaos and comfort coexist side by side.

For corporate groups, BaseCamp is also HRDC-approved, making it an ideal choice for structured, claimable team-building programs that combine real engagement with measurable team dynamics outcomes.

Photo credit: Monkeys Canopy

The Verdict

BaseCamp isn’t trying to be chill.
It’s not trying to be aesthetic.

It’s designed for something more primal:

Competition. Connection. Controlled chaos.

You don’t just leave saying you had fun.
You leave with a squad story that somehow gets more dramatic every time you retell it.

And usually, the last sentence is the same:

“Run it back.”

Experience: Paintball, Archery Tag, Water Tag, Zorbing, Team-Building Missions
Best for: Groups, enthusiasts, birthdays, competitive squads, corporate team-building (HRDC-approved)

items.title: GET SIDEWAYS: WHY BLASTACARS IS KUALA LUMPUR'S ULTIMATE INDOOR ADRENALINE RUSH
items.content:
If you’re hunting for a thrill in Kuala Lumpur that blends high-octane motorsport with pure, unadulterated fun, Blastacars Malaysia belongs at the top of your bucket list.

Tucked away on the 5th floor of Sungei Wang Plaza in the heart of Bukit Bintang, this isn't your typical go-karting track. Forget racing lines and grip; at Blastacars, the goal isn't just to be fast—it’s to be sideways.

Photo credit: Blastacars Malaysia

The Art of the Drift

Unlike traditional tracks that reward precision and traction, Blastacars utilizes a custom-designed, low-friction indoor surface. Paired with specialized karts imported from New Zealand, the experience is engineered for one thing: drifting.

The concept was born in 1987 by Peter Zyp and brought to Malaysian shores in 2015 by professional drift driver John Wong. Over the years, the track and karts have been fine-tuned to ensure the experience feels less like a toy and more like a genuine motorsport discipline.

Photo credit: Blastacars Malaysia

Power for Every Level

One of the best things about Blastacars is that it’s "easy to learn, difficult to master." You don't need a racing license to feel like a pro:


Kid's Speed: Perfect for kids to learn how to drive in a safe environment.

Standard: For first timer (adults) who want's to experience the drift.

Expert: For those who have found their rhythm and want more speed.

Pro (420cc): The heavy hitters. Powered by Honda engines, these are reserved for skilled drivers looking for a truly intense, high-torque experience.


Why It’s a "Must-Do" in KL

Weather-Proof Fun: KL’s tropical downpours won't ruin your plans. Being indoors means the drifting never stops, rain or shine.

Prime Location: Located in Sungei Wang Plaza, it’s the perfect adrenaline break during a day of shopping or exploring the Bukit Bintang district.

Inclusive Thrills: It’s a hit for corporate team-building, unique date nights, or family outings. They even accommodate younger thrill-seekers (ages 6+ and at least 1.2m tall).

Photo credit: Blastacars Malaysia

The Atmosphere

The moment those engines roar to life, the energy in the room shifts. There’s a certain infectious joy in watching friends laugh through a "spin-out" or seeing a competitive driver nail a perfectly clean sideways line through a hair-pin turn. It’s all the excitement of professional drifting without the high stakes or intimidation.

The Verdict: In a city famous for its cafes and malls, Blastacars Malaysia offers something refreshingly raw. It’s a blend of arcade-style fun and real-world driving skill that will leave you breathless and inevitably saying, "Just one more lap."

Photo credit: Blastacars Malaysia

Plan Your Visit

Location: 5th Floor, Sungei Wang Plaza, Bukit Bintang.

Who can join: Ages 6 and up (Min height 1.2m).

items.title: GET TO KNOW THE TRAVEL STORE
items.content:
How It All Began

Photo credit: The Travel Store

The Travel Store was founded in 2004 with an aim of making it easier for people to shop, travel, and move through everyday life. Since then, it has grown to become a leading and preferred travel goods provider in Malaysia, with a strong brand presence in Southeast Asia.

Photo credit: The Travel Store

With over 20 years of experience and a community of more than 150,000 loyal members, the brand has built a reputation grounded in trust, quality, and a deep understanding of modern mobility. Whether it’s a long-haul journey or a daily commute, The Travel Store continues to evolve alongside the needs of travellers.

A One-Stop Shop for All Your Travel Needs

Photo credit: The Travel Store

As a multi-brand retailer, The Travel Store offers a curated selection of international labels such as LOJEL, Echolac, Eminent, Verage, and Hush Puppies among many others. Several of these brands operate their own factories, where products are designed and tested to meet strict quality standards.

Photo credit: The Travel Store

At The Travel Store, customers can shop for everything under one roof, and choose from a wide range of thoughtfully designed products—suitcases, backpacks, travel accessories, outdoor apparel, and more—that cater to different needs.

Photo credit: The Travel Store

Besides being an expert in travel solutions, another thing that sets The Travel Store apart is its after-sales care. The brand continues to support its customers long after a purchase is made, even allowing them to bring in other luggage brands for repair. This reinforces the brand’s philosophy of putting people first: Your Journey, Our Promise.

Encouraging Sustainable Travel, One Repair at a Time

Photo credit: The Travel Store

Sustainability is an ongoing commitment for The Travel Store, which is evident through its Earth Day initiatives that are guided by three pillars: Respect, Restore, and Reimagine.

Photo credit: The Travel Store

Photo credit: The Travel Store

Each year, the brand actively promotes mindful consumption habits and encourages customers to repair instead of replace their luggage. During Earth week from 20th to 26th April 2026, The Travel Store’s community of 2,837 participants have successfully sent in 4,070 pieces of luggage for repair, thus fulfilling the brand’s goal of giving your luggage a second life.

Earning Customers’ Trust With a 100-Day Return Policy

Photo credit: The Travel Store

Featured Brand Stories

LOJEL

Photo credit: The Travel Store

items.content:

You leave the busy streets behind for a space that feels honest and uncomplicated. 

For the family traveller or the urban explorer, everything you need is exactly where it should be. 

Sunlight pours through floor-to-ceiling windows, illuminating a sanctuary of minimalist calm. 

It is a place that values your time as much as your comfort. 


Photo credit: Four Points

As the morning light fills The Mesh, families gather for a breakfast that feels like home but better. 

This is the social heart of the hotel, where local flavours and international comfort meet. 

The lobby hums with a quiet, social rhythm that invites you to linger. 

As the day unfolds, the dining story expands to the bold spices of Sichuan Kitchen or relaxed bites at the H2O Bar & Grill.

items.title: REDISCOVERING MADAM KWAN'S CULINARY GEMS IN KL
items.content:
When we talk about Madam Kwan’s, our minds often drift to the golden mounds of Nasi Lemak or the rich, aromatic layers of Nasi Bojari. 

Photo credit: Madam Kwan's

But this April, the "Truly Malaysian" legend is casting a wider net, inviting us to rediscover a side of their menu that is as deep and diverse as our local waters: The Seafood Collection.

For those residing in or visiting Kuala Lumpur, Madam Kwan’s remains the gold standard for "curative" dining, food that doesn't just fill you up but restores your soul through heritage and meticulous preparation.

Photo credit: Madam Kwan's

The April Spotlight: Masterpieces from the Sea

Madam Kwan’s has curated a selection of seafood dishes that bring the fresh, briny flavours of the ocean directly to your table in the heart of KL. If you haven't explored this section of the menu, you are missing out on some of the city's best-kept secrets:

  • The Sang Har Noodles (Fresh Water Prawn): A true showstopper. Large, succulent king prawns are perched atop a bed of silky noodles, all brought together by a rich, savoury egg gravy. It is a dish built for sharing and celebrating.
  • Claypot Sang Har Noodle Soup: Perfect for a rainy KL afternoon, this version swaps the wok-char for a deep, soul-warming broth. The essence of the prawns infuses every spoonful, creating a rich umami experience that hits the spot every time.
  • Claypot Soft Shell Crab Noodles: A modern favourite that highlights a beautiful contrast in textures. The delicate crunch of soft-shell crab nestled in aromatic noodles is a testament to Madam Kwan’s ability to innovate within the bounds of tradition.
Photo credit: Madam Kwan's
A Milestone of Inclusivity

Beyond the menu, Madam Kwan’s continues to grow with its community. We are thrilled to highlight that the brand is expanding its reach to ensure every Malaysian can enjoy these legendary recipes with peace of mind. 
While KL remains the heartbeat of the brand, recent Halal certifications at key locations (like Queensbay Mall and Gurney Plaza in the North) reflect a commitment to authenticity and trusted standards that resonate across all outlets.
From the kitchen to your table, every dish is made with care, ensuring that the "Truly Malaysian" experience is one that everyone can share.

Photo credit: Madam Kwan's

A Setting for Every Celebration

Whether you are dining under the iconic lights of Suria KLCC, enjoying a shopping break at Pavilion KL, or catching up with family at Mid Valley Megamall, the experience remains consistent. 

Madam Kwan’s isn't just about the food; it’s about the curated atmosphere of Malaysian hospitality.

This month, skip the usual and dive into the extraordinary. 

Whether it’s the snap of a king prawn or the richness of a lamb shank, discover why Madam Kwan’s continues to be the heartbeat of Kuala Lumpur’s dining scene.

Visit Madam Kwan’s across Kuala Lumpur:
Suria KLCC | Pavilion KL | Mid Valley Megamall | The Exchange TRX | 1 Utama | Bangsar Shopping Centre.

Are you planning to try the iconic Sang Har Noodles on your next visit, or does the new Rendang Lamb Shank sound more like your style?

Full menu details and online reservations are available directly on Madam Kwan’s official website.

items.title: GLOW UP RAYA MUSICAL SHOWCASE
items.content:
The energy at Sungei Wang Plaza reached a fever pitch this past weekend as the mall officially wrapped up its festive season with a bang. 

If you weren't at the Centre Court on Sunday, March 29, you missed what can only be described as the ultimate Raya "after-party."

The Glow Up Raya Musical Showcase turned the heart of Bukit Bintang into a literal concert hall, proving that Sungei Wang still knows exactly how to throw a party that resonates with every generation.

Photo credit: Sungei Wang Plaza

A Star-Studded Grand Finale

In a brilliant partnership with ERA FM, the showcase was led by the charismatic Shasha, who kept the vibes high and the crowd engaged from start to finish. But the real magic happened when the local powerhouses took the stage. 

We’re talking about a lineup that defines modern Malaysian music:

  • MimiFly brought her signature fieriness.

  • Aufa Hanie and Zubir Khan delivered soulful, catchy performances.

  • Naim Daniel captivated the audience with his undeniable stage presence.

From contemporary Raya hits like Serumpun and Si Dara Raya to fan favourites like Kan Dah Raya, the music had the entire mall singing along.

Photo credit: Sungei Wang Plaza

The Centre Court was transformed into a glowing neon oasis, blending traditional motifs with a sleek, "Glow Up" aesthetic that served as the perfect backdrop for the countless TikToks and Reels being filmed in the crowd. 

It wasn't just a concert; it was a fully immersive experience that proved Raya celebrations can be as trendy and high-octane as any major music festival.

Mascot Magic & Community Spirit

It wasn't just about the vocalists! 

The stage got an extra dose of adrenaline thanks to Wira and Manja, the official mascots of Visit Malaysia 2026. 

Their appearance added a playful, high-energy layer to the show, prompting kids and tourists alike to reach for their phones to capture the moment.

Photo credit: Sungei Wang Plaza

Beyond the flashing lights, the event felt like a massive family reunion. As Joseph Teo, General Manager of Sungei Wang Plaza, put it, the showcase was about creating a shared festive experience. 

Whether you were a youth there for the idols or a family doing some last-minute Raya browsing, the "Glow Up" theme truly lived up to its name by blending tradition with a modern, electrifying twist.

Did You Capture the Glow?

If you were part of the crowd, we want to see your perspective! Sungei Wang Plaza has once again solidified its spot as the go-to gathering point for Kuala Lumpur’s most vibrant celebrations.

Photo credit: Sungei Wang Plaza

As the final notes faded and the crowd began to drift away, you could still feel that lingering buzz in the air—the kind that only happens when people truly connect. 

Sungei Wang Plaza has always been more than just a place to shop; it’s the "People’s Mall," a spot where our shared love for pop culture and community spirit naturally collide. 

Ending the Raya season on such a high note feels like the start of something big. 

If you couldn't make it this time, don't worry—there’s always a seat for you at the next one. 

Keep an eye out so you don't miss the next big moment!

Stay updated on all their upcoming events by visiting www.sungeiwang.com or following their Facebook page.

items.title: GL PLAY MID-YEAR SALE
items.content:
A Different Kind of Getaway, Just 30 Minutes from KL

By the time you finish your first ride, you realise this is not a one-stop attraction. It is a full day that naturally turns into a night out.

That is exactly why more people are heading to Gamuda Cove right now.

Start with what makes the decision easy.

At SplashMania Waterpark, the Kids Play Free promotion (4 May to 7 June 2026, via online tickets) removes the usual hesitation for families. 

It turns the plan into a simple “YES!”.

Photo Credit Gamuda Cove

Once inside, the park opens up in scale. 

At the centre, the Amazonia Ship anchors everything, surrounded by a wide mix of rides that cater to different levels of thrill. 

If you are chasing adrenaline, this is where it delivers.

Photo Credit Gamuda Cove

The Plunge is the one everyone talks about. 

A near vertical drop that is over before you process it. 

Then come Monsta and Twista, where speed gives way to spins, turns and unpredictable movement that keeps every ride different.

Photo Credit Gamuda Cove

Photo Credit Gamuda Cove

For something slower, there are wide water zones and family friendly rides where you can ease off. 

Younger visitors tend to stay around the kids zone at Treasure Tower, where smaller slides and interactive play areas keep them occupied for hours.

Photo Credit Gamuda Cove

The rhythm is simple. Ride, rest, repeat. The day fills itself.

Then the experience shifts.

On Friday and Saturday nights from 3 April to 6 June 2026 (7PM to 11PM), SplashMania transforms into the Night Splash Water Festival, a high energy after dark experience that brings the feel of global water festivals right to Selangor. 

Inspired by internationally recognised celebrations, this is a festival you would usually travel for, reimagined with a distinctly Malaysian touch. 

The entire park shifts in mood. Slides stay open under the night sky, while the wave pool turns into the main stage, driven by DJs, live bands, fire and light performances, and an atmosphere that builds as the night goes on.

Photo Credit Gamuda Cove

Beyond the rides, the experience expands into a full festival ground. 

Expect interactive splash games, roaming performances, and pockets of activity across the park, alongside Thai inspired street food and quick recharge moments like express massage pop ups. 

It is not just about staying late at a waterpark. 

It is about stepping into a multi-sensory festival where water, music and movement come together, all within a single night.

 

Photo Credit Gamuda Cove

Photo Credit Gamuda Cove

If you want something more active in between, Discovery Park adds that contrast. 

The Goosebumps Rope Course is high, open and exposed, making every step feel rewarding without being overwhelming. 

It also holds a Malaysian Book of Records title for having the most rope course elements in the country, which gives a clear sense of its scale.

On the ground, archery and paintball target shooting keep things moving with short, repeatable bursts of activity. 

It is not designed to overwhelm, but to keep you engaged. 

On its own, it works well as a half day experience, or paired with SplashMania to round out the day.

Photo Credit Gamuda Cove

Photo Credit Gamuda Cove

If you prefer to take things at your own pace, the Unlimited Season Pass at RM50 per pax (valid until 31 July 2026) makes that possible. 

You are not locked into a single visit. 

Spend a few hours, leave, and come back again without pressure.

Photo Credit Gamuda Cove

If you are open to going a little further, FunPark at Gamuda Luge Gardens adds a different pace. About 30 minutes from Kuala Lumpur, it leans into familiar, easy going rides. 

The Eye of Gardens ferris wheel stands out, officially recognised by the Malaysian Book of Records as the biggest and tallest ferris wheel in a theme park. 

Around it, rides like the carousel and Vroomerang keep things light and relaxed, especially towards the evening when the lights come on and the atmosphere softens.

Photo Credit Gamuda Cove

Photo Credit Gamuda Cove

Within the same park, Big Bucket Splash offers a playful water element that complements the rides. 

It is designed for all ages, with interactive water play zones that make it easy to move between dry and wet activities without overplanning the visit.

Photo Credit Gamuda Cove

If you prefer flexibility, the Season Pass at RM50 per pax (valid until 31 July 2026) covers unlimited access to FunPark rides or Big Bucket Splash, allowing you to return and enjoy the park at your own pace. 

It works especially well if you are planning multiple visits or want a more relaxed experience without rushing through everything in one day.

Photo Credit Gamuda Cove

What makes this mid-year period worth acting on is how everything connects.

Spend the day at SplashMania, stay on for Night Splash, and still have a reason to return. The Kids Play Free offer gets you in, the RM50 passes let you come back, and the night festival delivers something you will not find elsewhere nearby.

This is not a one-time visit.
 And that is exactly why now is the right time to go.

Explore more at glplay.com.my.

items.title: A FRONT-ROW SEAT TO THE RENAISSANCE: WHY KL FAMILY STAYS ARE CHANGING
items.content:
We all know the struggle of the typical "city stay" with the family. 

It starts with logistics: how far is the hotel from the LRT? Is there a place nearby where they can run around that isn’t a busy road? By the time you’ve ticked off the convenience boxes, you often find yourself sacrificing the feeling of an actual getaway.

But as we look toward 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, there’s one landmark that has quietly solved that riddle, recently being honoured as Asia's Best Family City Hotel


Photo credit:Renaissance Kuala Lumpur

The Renaissance Kuala Lumpur Hotel & Convention Centre has managed to do something rare in downtown KL by creating a space that portrays itself not just as a hotel, but as a dual-branded urban resort where families can set up their "home base" right in the heart of the action.

                                                                              
Photo credit:Renaissance Kuala Lumpur

The Skyline View is Their Storyteller

When we talk about an "unforgettable stay" in 2026, the experience starts before you even unpack. For a child, seeing the city from the floor-to-ceiling windows of their room isn't just a view; it’s a fairy tale of scale.

The unique perspective here places you in a living conversation between KL’s iconic past and its soaring future. Waking up to the KL Tower on one side and the stunning geometry of the brand-new Merdeka 118 on the other frames their entire stay. 

In 2026, those specific rooms offer the best front-row seat to the changing city they will one day read about in history books.

                                                                

13,000 Square Feet of "Unforgettable"

The real portrait of a Renaissance family is painted on Level 4. You wouldn’t expect to find Paradise Trails tucked between skyscrapers—a 13,000-square-foot outdoor adventure zone dedicated entirely to play.

Photo credit:Renaissance Kuala Lumpur


Here, "unforgettable" looks like this:

  • The Canopy Walk: A chance to walk among the "tops" of the palms, right above the city.


Photo credit:Renaissance Kuala Lumpur

  • The Climbing Wall: Safe, outdoor challenges designed to help them find their confidence.


Photo credit:Renaissance Kuala Lumpur

  • The Massive Pool: One of the largest outdoor pools in the city, complete with water slides that turn a morning dip into a mini-theme park adventure.


Photo credit:Renaissance Kuala Lumpur

While the little ones explore their private sanctuary, parents can actually relax at the Mandara Spa or enjoy a "Bar Ritual" at R Bar, knowing their children are making memories just a few steps away.


Photo credit:Renaissance Kuala Lumpur

Festive Traditions, Reinvented for 2026

If you are planning your 2026 around the holidays, the Renaissance is offering a way to drop the holiday stress and keep the magic.

When you book your stay on Christmas Eve or New Year’s Eve, the portrait changes from adventure to celebration. 

It starts with the exclusive "wake up to the skyline" morning, followed by an Evolution breakfast where the authentic Italian coastal flavours meet the local festive spirit. 

For the Eve of the celebration, the family-friendly Holiday Buffet ensures that everyone—from the most adventurous eater to the pickiest toddler—finds a feast they love.


In 2026...

A family staying here isn't just about finding a room near the Twin Towers.

It’s about securing a place where your family can breathe, play, and watch the future rise right outside your window.

So, what are you waiting for? Book your stay now!

items.title: THE GLOW UP RAYA AT SUNGEI WANG PLAZA
items.content:
This Hari Raya season, Sungei Wang Plaza invites shoppers to celebrate with “The Glow Up Raya”, a vibrant festive campaign happening from 28 February to 29 March 2026. Held in support of Tourism Malaysia and the Visit Malaysia 2026, the celebration brings together culture, music, festive shopping and meaningful community initiatives.

Photo credit: Sungei Wang Plaza

A Kampung-Inspired Festive Experience

Visitors will be welcomed by a charming kampung-inspired festive décor at the mall’s Centre Court and Main Entrance. Featuring traditional village house elements, batik-inspired decorations and warm festive lighting, the installation blends Malaysian heritage with the vibrant energy of Kuala Lumpur, creating a perfect setting for festive photos and family moments.

Photo credit: Sungei Wang Plaza

Glow Up Raya Musical Showcase

The highlight of the campaign takes place on 29 March 2026 with the Glow Up Raya Musical Showcase, hosted by Sha Sha from ERA FM.

Photo credit: Sungei Wang Plaza


The showcase features performances by popular Malaysian artistes including:

  • MimiFly
  • Aufa Hanie
  • Zubir Khan
  • Ammar Haikal

Visitors can expect an exciting afternoon filled with music, festive energy and memorable Raya moments.


Festive Activities & Workshops


Throughout the campaign, visitors can enjoy various activities including cultural dance performances, the Festival Warisan Nusantara Fashion Show, live music showcases, and the Ketupat Mascot Walkabout.

Photo credit: Sungei Wang Plaza

Families can also join the Raya Miniature Workshop by MinNature Malaysia, held at JUMPA, where participants can create their own festive miniature scenes.


Raya Bazaar & Rewards


The Glow Up Raya Bazaar at Centre Court offers a lively marketplace filled with festive treats, Raya essentials and unique finds from local vendors.

Photo credit: Sungei Wang Plaza

Shoppers can also enjoy special redemptions, including Raya packets, tiffins and an exclusive cookie jar for members.


Giving Back This Raya


Through the Raya Give and Glow initiative, visitors can donate pre-loved clothing to support refugee communities in collaboration with United Arakan Institute Malaysia. The mall will also host a special Berbuka Puasa session with Pusat Gelendangan Anjung Kembara, spreading the spirit of generosity during the holy month of Ramadan.


Celebrate the joy of Raya with culture, entertainment and community spirit at Sungei Wang Plaza this festive season.

items.title: CHIC & UNIQUE SOUVENIRS: WELCOME TO TREASURE TROVE!
items.content:
Treasure Trove at Kuala Lumpur Central Walk feels like stumbling upon a tiny treasure box of Malaysian creativity, where every shelf is packed with colourful finds that celebrate local culture, craft, and design in a way that feels fun, meaningful, and actually worth bringing home instead of the usual generic souvenir-shop plastic trinkets.

Treasure Trove was created with the mission of giving Malaysian small businesses and artists the visibility they deserve, turning the boutique into a curated platform where passionate homegrown creators can showcase their work while visitors get to discover the richness of Malaysia’s arts, culture, and craftsmanship all in one place.

Photo Credit: Treasure Trove 

Being located right in the heart of Kuala Lumpur Central Walk gives the store a lively city-core atmosphere, with locals popping in during lunch breaks, office workers browsing after work, and travellers wandering in curious to see what unique Malaysian treasures they can find, creating a space that feels vibrant yet welcoming.

The overall vibe and aesthetic can best be described as modern Malaysian, where heritage motifs, traditional symbols, and cultural references are reimagined into contemporary lifestyle items that feel stylish, practical, and colourful while still staying deeply connected to Malaysian roots.

Photo Credit: Treasure Trove

Supporting local artisans is truly the heart of Treasure Trove, because every product in the store represents a real creator whose work carries their personal inspiration, cultural background, and craftsmanship, making each piece feel more like a story than just another item on a shelf.

If you only have a few minutes to browse but still want something memorable to bring home, the store’s signature picks include handcrafted ceramic mugs featuring Malaysian icons like the Bunga Raya, Rafflesia, hornbills, and traditional wau kites, handmade pop-up cards inspired by nostalgic local scenes and traditional kuih, and batik-inspired accessories such as keycaps or even pet bibs that cleverly mix heritage design with modern creativity.

What makes the shopping experience even more special is that the team actively shares the stories behind the makers, so customers often learn about the artists’ inspiration, creative process, and personal journeys through friendly conversations in-store, thoughtful product descriptions, and social media features that highlight the people behind each creation.

KL locals who visit Treasure Trove often gravitate toward nostalgic everyday items that remind them of familiar Malaysian moments, including ceramic mugs, decorative figurines, postcards, handmade greeting cards, magnets, and charming stationery featuring local slang, cultural references, and playful nods to Malaysian food and festivities.

When it comes to gift shopping, Treasure Trove stands out because every item carries a deeper meaning, with thoughtfully curated pieces that represent Malaysian creativity and craftsmanship, making the gifts feel far more personal and heartfelt than something mass-produced.

Photo Credit: Treasure Trove

Behind the scenes, the store also maintains strong relationships with its network of artists and creators, regularly collaborating with them, sharing feedback, and supporting their work through in-store features and promotional activities so the creative community can continue to grow together.

If you are planning to visit, Treasure Trove is open Monday to Saturday from 10am to 7pm, with lunchtime being the busiest period, so those who want a more relaxed browsing experience will probably enjoy coming right when the shop opens at 10am or later in the afternoon after 2pm.

Looking ahead, the team is also working on new ideas and collaborations for 2026, which means visitors can expect even more artisanal products and creative collections that showcase Malaysia’s diverse cultural influences and evolving creative scene.

Ultimately, the feeling Treasure Trove hopes customers take home with them is nostalgia, because every mug, card, or handcrafted piece is meant to become a warm reminder of Malaysia, its culture, and the memories and love people create while exploring Kuala Lumpur.

items.title: FARM IN THE CITY: KAMPUNG VIBES & FURRY SURPRISES
items.content:
If you’ve been craving something wholesome in Kuala Lumpur that isn’t another mall
or cafe, Farm in The City is the kind of place that resets your mood the second you step in.

It’s an award-winning Malaysian village-themed petting zoo that feels like a mini
kampung world tucked into the city, where nature and community vibes actually
show up in real life.

The best part is you’re not just “looking at animals,” you’re properly meeting them, the
kind of visit where a colourful bird might land on your shoulder and you suddenly feel
like you’re in a fairytale.

Photo Credit: Farm In The City

And yes, the Sunny Oasis Station is now home to capybaras , those famously
relaxed creatures that seem permanently unbothered by life and unbelievably
cute in person.

If you’re bringing kids along, the Junior Farm Ranger program is genuinely a flex
because they get hands-on animal care experience like grooming and feeding instead of
just walking around bored.

It’s also one of those rare attractions where the “included in your ticket” line actually
means something, because the animal interactions are a real highlight and not a hidden
extra charge situation.

You’ll want to time your visit around their Daily Feeding and Interaction Schedule
so you don’t miss the fun moments, from playful otters to the raccoon hugging
interaction that people talk about after like it’s a core memory.

What makes this spot tourist-friendly is how easy it is to reach now, because you can
literally MRT your way there and skip the traffic pain entirely.

It’s the kind of day trip that works whether you’re visiting KL for the first time, travelling
with family, or just want a break that feels outdoorsy without needing a full road trip plan.

If you’re building a KL itinerary, this is a clean “add it in” option because it’s cute,
different, interactive, and honestly just refreshing compared to the usual city loop.

Before you go: Online tickets must be purchased at least 24 hours before your visit, so plan it like a proper day out instead of last-minute winging it.

How to get there (MRT shortcut): Take the MRT Putrajaya Line to Putra Permai Station (PY37), then it’s about a 5-minute walk to the farm.

items.title: THE YELLOW LANDMARK OF CHINATOWN: WHY BUNN CHOON IS A MUST-VISIT AT KWAI CHAI HONG
items.content:
If you find yourself wandering through the hidden murals and pre-war charm of Kwai Chai Hong, your journey through the Straits of Malacca influence in KL isn't truly complete until you step into the vibrant yellow building on the corner.

Photo credit: Bunn Choon via Instagram

Bunn Choon 1893 isn’t just a bakery; it is a living piece of Kuala Lumpur’s history.

Standing as a golden landmark at the edge of the heritage trail, this iconic shop is the ultimate "must-visit" destination.

To visit Kwai Chai Hong and miss Bunn Choon is to miss the very soul of Chinatown.

Photo credit: Bunn Choon via Instagram

Step Into Authentic Nostalgia

While the murals outside tell the stories of the past, Bunn Choon allows you to taste it. As you move from the bustling streets into the heritage-style interior, the atmosphere shifts.

From the vintage memorabilia to the traditional wooden plaque hanging proudly in the dining area, every corner of this restaurant breathes authentic nostalgia.

Photo credit: Bunn Choon via Instagram

The Gold Standard of Specialty Bakes

You cannot visit Kwai Chai Hong without indulging in the legendary bakes that have defined this brand for over 130 years.

Photo credit: Bunn Choon via Instagram

Bunn Choon has earned its reputation as a trusted specialty bakehouse, famous for:

  • Signature Egg Tarts: Renowned for their impossibly flaky crust and silky custard.

  • Traditional Heritage Treats: Handcrafted recipes that have remained unchanged since 1893.

  • Century-Old Legacy: Every bite is a testament to the craftsmanship that has survived generations.

The Essential Kwai Chai Hong Pitstop

Whether you are a photography enthusiast capturing the teal windows against the yellow facade, or a foodie hunting for KL’s best tarts, Bunn Choon is your essential one-stop destination. It is the perfect place to soak in the old-world charm and experience the heritage of the area in its most delicious form.

Photo credit: Bunn Choon via Instagram

items.title: CAMP5: CLIMBING FOR EVERYONE, ADVENTURE FOR ALL
items.content:
From families to adventure seekers, Camp5’s goal is simple: get everyone climbing

Camp5 is synonymous with indoor climbing in Malaysia. With six gyms nationwide — five in Greater Kuala Lumpur and one in Johor Bahru — Camp5 has helped shape the country’s modern climbing culture. 

Walk into any outlet and you’ll instantly feel inspired. 

Beginners tackle their first wall, kids scramble up colourful holds, and experienced climbers project tough routes overhead.

Photo credit: Camp5

Each location has its own personality, but all share the same foundations — accessibility, safety, professional route setting, and a genuinely welcoming atmosphere.

No experience? Not necessary. 

Camp5 offers a full range of courses, from Bouldering to Lead Climbing and even Outdoor Lead Climbing. There’s a pathway for every comfort level.

Photo credit: Camp5

For families, the Family Friendly Courses are a fantastic introduction. 

You’ll learn safety basics and simple techniques together, then stay on to climb at your own pace. 

No pressure, no intimidation — just encouragement.

From families to adventure seekers and even professional athletes, climbing truly is for everyone.


CAMP5 ECO CITY: SOUTHEAST ASIA’S LARGEST BOULDERING GYM

Photo credit: Camp5

Camp5 Eco City is a true boulderer’s playground. 

Spanning 3,000sqm, it features nearly 1,000sqm of dedicated bouldering terrain, alongside 33 top-rope lines, autobelays, and two lead climbing lanes. 

Tension and Moon boards are available for those focused on building strength and refining technique.

Routes are reset regularly, so there’s always something new to challenge yourself with  whether you’re dropping in for a casual session or committing to serious training.

Families are well catered for too, with a dedicated kids’ area designed to help young climbers build confidence in a safe and structured environment. 

Add a barista café serving coffee and healthy meals, plus showers and locker rooms, and it’s easy to see why many climbers spend hours here.

Eco City isn’t just a gym — it’s a second home!

Photo credit: Camp5


CAMP5 KL EAST: FAMILY ADVENTURE MEETS FULL-SERVICE CLIMBING

Located at KL East Mall, just minutes from the iconic Batu Caves crags, Camp5 KL East blends indoor comfort with outdoor inspiration.

Split across two floors, Level G3 houses the Play Climb wall and gear shop. Upstairs — or via direct access from Carpark L1 — you’ll find the main climbing hall.

Here, climbers can enjoy bouldering, 12-metre top-rope routes with autobelays, and stunning 15-metre lead climbing. 

The fully air-conditioned space also offers training walls, functional fitness facilities, hot showers, locker rooms, and the Eat Well Café — everything you’d expect from a modern climbing gym.

Photo credit: Camp5

Play Climb: Perfect for Young Adventurers

What truly sets KL East apart is Play Climb. 

It’s a safe, structured and exciting way for little adventurers to discover climbing — and parents can join in too.

Designed especially for younger climbers, this colourful space turns climbing into a fun, confidence-building experience. 

Hour-long guided sessions run throughout the day, making it easy to plan a visit.

Children must be at least 4 years old and weigh a minimum of 10kg. 

The fee includes a harness and helmet, and kids can wear their own sport shoes or trainers (no flip-flops or slippers).

Photo credit: Camp5


Photo credit: Camp5


CAMP5 UTROPOLIS: A COMMUNITY FAVOURITE

Located in Glenmarie, Shah Alam, Camp5 Utropolis is popular with students and seasoned climbers alike.

Known for its spacious layout and strong bouldering focus, it offers everything from beginner-friendly routes to dynamic, parkour-style moves.

Utropolis balances performance and community beautifully. 

It remains welcoming to first-timers and families, with introductory courses and supportive staff ready to guide new climbers.

Photo credit: Camp5


CAMP5 1 UTAMA: SOUTHEAST ASIA’S TALLEST LEAD WALL

Camp5’s beloved flagship at 1 Utama recently celebrated 20 years of operation. 

Located inside one of Malaysia’s largest shopping malls, it makes climbing incredibly accessible — perfect for an after-work session or a weekend activity.

The gym offers a full climbing experience, including bouldering, roped climbing, and training facilities. 

Daily Try Climbing sessions make it easy for beginners to get started, while dedicated kids’ programmes cater to young climbers from as young as one year old.

Photo credit: Camp5

The Katak Club parent-and-child sessions are designed to nurture a lifelong love of climbing. 

After just a few sessions, many parents feel confident enough to bring their children climbing independently. 

Photo credit: Camp5
Photo credit: Camp5

A fun bonus: kids under eight climb free with a checked-in guardian at all Camp5 facilities.

And for those ready to dream big, Camp5 1 Utama houses the tallest indoor lead wall in Southeast Asia — a towering feature that inspires climbers to quite literally reach new heights.

Photo credit: Camp5


BEAST PARK AT CAMP5 JUMPA: FITNESS MEETS ADVENTURE

In the heart of Bukit Bintang, on the third floor of Jumpa at Sungei Wang Plaza, nestled within the walls of a full scale climbing gym in Camp5 Jumpa, you’lll also find Beast Park — a high-energy ninja course created by the Camp5 team.

Photo credit: Camp5

With the All-Access Beast Park Pass, visitors get 90 minutes to explore Ninja-style obstacle courses, interactive E-walls, the Fun Cave, Lil’ Beast zones, and the elevated Beast Net. 

It’s playful, active, and just challenging enough to keep things exciting.

Weekday passes are more budget-friendly, while weekends and public holidays are slightly higher. 

For even more action, the Combo Adventure + Climbing pass pairs Beast Park access with a guided climbing session.

Additional programs include Katak Club sessions, corporate bookings, birthday parties, and a full range of climbing courses.

Photo credit: Camp5


MORE THAN JUST CLIMBING

Across its six locations, Camp5 has built more than climbing gyms — it has built a thriving community. 

It’s where beginners gain confidence, families bond over shared challenges, and experienced climbers continue pushing their limits.

Whether you’re starting a new hobby, planning a family day out, or chasing your next fitness goal, Camp5 Climbing Gym might just become your new favourite place to hang out — and climb a little higher.

Photo credit: Camp5


Ready to start your adventure?

With six locations across Greater Kuala Lumpur and Johor Bahru, there is a Camp5 wall waiting for you. 

For specific addresses, contact details, and Operating Hours for each outlet, please visit the official website or follow Camp5 on social media for daily updates.
