items.title: WALLET-FRIENDLY WINGS: HOW SHOPLAH AND NEW PRICING RULES ARE TRANSFORMING KLIA
items.content:
Ever felt that distinct pinch in your wallet the moment you stepped into an airport terminal?

We have all been there, staring at a bottle of water or a simple meal that somehow costs twice as much as it does in the city.

With Visit Malaysia 2026 (VM2026) fast approaching, the government is stepping in to make sure your airport experience doesn't leave a sour taste in your mouth.

Photo credit: Asean Food Travel

The Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture (MOTAC) has officially urged Malaysia Airports Holdings Berhad (MAHB) to keep a closer eye on food and retail pricing.

This move comes after a wave of complaints regarding high prices at our main gateways, specifically KLIA Terminal 1 and KLIA Terminal 2.

The goal is to ensure that the first and last impression of Malaysia is one of hospitality, not overpricing, effectively reducing travel fatigue.

To balance the scales, MAHB has officially activated a new, enhanced phase of ShopLAH to make airport shopping more rewarding for the global traveller.

While ShopLAH originally debuted back in 2019, this 10 February 2026 relaunch marks its evolution into an "always-on" retail brand specifically for the VM2026 cycle.

If you are unfamiliar with it, ShopLAH is a fresh initiative that turns the terminal into a curated lifestyle destination rather than just a seamless transit point.

One of the biggest highlights for visitors is the brand-new Tourist Privilege Card, which offers instant discounts and perks through the MYAirports app.

The campaign also spotlights "Homegrown Heroes," featuring local brands like Kapten Batik and Royal Selangor to provide authentic keepsakes.

You can even look forward to limited-edition merchandise, such as foldable duty-free bags designed by local artists like Afi Sulaiman and Kideika.

Whether you are flying in from across the region or hopping between continents, the focus is now on fair value and high-quality local engagement.

Photo credit: Trip.com

Pro-Tip: The "Food Garden" Secret

For the most "local" prices in KLIA Terminal 1, skip the departure hall chains and head to the Food Garden on Level 2 (Main Terminal Building).

Recently revamped, this food court is the primary dining spot for airport staff, meaning you’ll find authentic Nasi Kandar and Chicken Rice at prices much closer to downtown KL.

Quick Summary

  • The Focus: Curbing high food and retail prices at MAHB managed airports.
  • The Evolution: ShopLAH was enhanced on 10 February 2026 with the new Tourist Privilege Card.
  • The Goal: Preparing for the Visit Malaysia 2026 influx with fair pricing and local brand spotlights.
  • Primary Locations: KLIA Terminal 1, KLIA Terminal 2, and regional hubs.
  • Digital Perk: Download the MYAirports app to access exclusive ShopLAHrewards.

items.title: SWEET DEALS AND GOLDEN BLESSINGS: WHY MANDARIN ORANGES ARE CHEAPER THIS CNY 2026
items.content:
If you’ve been walking through the aisles of Village Grocer or your local Bukit Bintang fruit stalls lately, you might have noticed something refreshing and it isn’t just the citrus scent.

Photo credit: The Star

Mandarin orange prices have seen a significant drop across Malaysia this year, just in time for the Year of the Horse celebrations starting 17 February 2026.

While initial reports centred on Melaka, we’ve verified that this "citrus surplus" is nationwide, including right here in Kuala Lumpur and the Klang Valley.

The festive price cut is largely thanks to a strengthening Malaysian Ringgit, which hit a seven-year high against the US dollar recently, and a massive bumper harvest from orchards in China.

But as any savvy local knows, we don’t just buy these oranges because they are a bargain; we buy them because they are literal "gold."

In Cantonese, the word for mandarin orange is kam, which sounds exactly like the word for "gold."

This linguistic coincidence is why the act of gifting oranges, known as song gam, is essentially like wishing someone a year filled with actual riches.

It is also why you’ll always see them served in pairs; in Chinese culture, good things come in twos, and a single orange is considered a bit "lonely" for a house full of blessings.

Beyond the wealth factor, the round, vibrant shape of the orange is said to resemble the sun, aligning with the yang (positive) principle to bring abundance and happiness into the home.

Whether you are stuffing them into a gift basket or placing them on your office desk, these fruits are the ultimate "low-cost, high-reward" way to manifest a prosperous year.

So, while the prices are down, it’s the perfect time to stock up, because in 2026, we’re all about sharing the "gold" without breaking the bank.

Just remember to keep an eye on the stems; a fresh green leaf still attached is the ultimate sign that your "gold" is as fresh as it gets.

2026 CNY Citrus Guide

  • The Price Trend: Prices are down approximately 10% to 30% nationwide compared to last year.
  • Trending Varieties: Look for the "Yellow Beauty" (sweet and firm) or the "Jelly Mandarin" (seedless and fiber-free), which are the top premium picks in KL malls this season.
  • Estimated Costs: Value boxes of Yongchun Lokam are retailing between RM14 – RM23, while premium gift sets (like Yellow Beauty) are ranging from RM35 – RM48.

items.title: FROM THE PENANG HILL FIRE TO PORTUGUESE ROOTS: WHY DO WE ACTUALLY SAY ‘BOMBA’?
items.content:
If you saw the smoke rising over Jalan Kebun Bunga yesterday, you weren't alone in feeling a bit of a heart-flutter for our beloved Penang Botanic Gardens.

Photo credit: The Star

Initial reports had everyone worried that the gardens themselves were ablaze, but the Penang Hill Corporation (PHC) has since clarified that the five-hectare fire was actually at KM1.9 along the Penang Hill jeep track.

Thanks to the rapid response from the Penang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) and the Air Itam Bukit Bendera Volunteer Fire Brigade, the fire was brought under control before it could do any major damage to our historic trees.

It’s during these intense moments, when the heat is on and the sirens are wailing, that we realise just how lucky we are to have the Bomba on speed dial.

Photo credit: Jabatan Bomba & Penyelamat Malaysia (Fire & Rescue Department of Malaysia)

But here’s a quick "pro-tip" for your next trivia night: have you ever wondered why we actually call them the "Bomba"?

You might have heard the popular theory that it's an acronym for Badan Operasi Mencegah Bencana Alam.

While that sounds incredibly official, Melaka Fire and Rescue director Mohd Zaidi Ma'at recently set the record straight: the term actually has Portuguese roots.

The word is derived from the Portuguese bombeiros, which literally means "firefighters."

According to historical records, the term entered local usage during the Portuguese era in Melaka and was later adopted officially in 1961.

Many people assume it has something to do with "bombs" or explosions, but it actually refers back to the Portuguese word bomba, meaning "pump": the essential tool for moving water to fight fires.

While other neighbours might use direct translations like "api dan penyelamat," Malaysia stuck with this unique linguistic souvenir from our colonial past in the Straits of Malacca.

The department itself has evolved through many names since it started as a Volunteer Fire Brigade in 1883.

Today, the team is even pushing a new aspiration called "Kita Bomba," focusing on values like bravery, integrity, and shared identity.

So, the next time you see those iconic red trucks racing toward Penang Hill or through the streets of Kuala Lumpur, you’ll know you’re looking at a legacy that's centuries in the making.

With the current dry season making things a bit crispy, let’s do our part to keep our green spaces safe because even the best "pumpsters" in the world prefer a quiet shift.

Quick Summary:

  • The News: A 5-hectare bushfire was controlled at KM1.9 along the Penang Hill jeep track on 4 February 2026.
  • The Myth: It is not an acronym for Badan Operasi Mencegah Bencana Alam, despite what many believe.
  • The Origin: "Bomba" comes from the Portuguese bombeiros (firefighters) and bomba (pump).
  • Historical Fact: The term was officially adopted in 1961, though the department’s roots go back to 1883.
  • Pro-Tip: During this dry spell, avoid any open burning near forest reserves like Penang Hill to prevent accidental reignition!

items.title: WAVE GOODBYE TO AIRPORT QUEUES: QR CODES ARE COMING!
items.content:
If you’ve ever felt that post-flight travel fatigue hit a wall while standing in a never-ending immigration line, I have some brilliant news for you.

Kuala Lumpur is about to get a lot more high-tech, and your smartphone is officially becoming your best travel buddy.

Photo credit: Bernama

Starting 1 March 2026, Malaysia Airports (MAHB) is rolling out QR code clearance across our major international gateways to make your arrival smoother than ever.

This is all part of the massive National Integrated Immigration System (MyNIISe), a digital upgrade designed to handle the millions of visitors we’re expecting for Visit Malaysia 2026 (VM2026).

The days of fumbling for your passport at the eGate are numbered; soon, you’ll just scan a code on your phone and breeze right through.

We’ve already seen this tech working wonders at the Johor-Singapore Causeway, and now it’s finally landing at KLIA Terminal 1 and Terminal 2.

The Home Ministry is installing 46 new pedestrian eGates across five airports to ensure a seamless transit experience, moving you from the plane to a taxi in record time.

Because a seamless transit only works if the hardware is actually there, here is exactly how the new eGate rollout looks across the country:

In our home base at KLIA Terminal 1, they are installing 18 units, split evenly between departures and arrivals to keep the flow moving.

Over at KLIA Terminal 2, you’ll see nine departure units ready to go, followed by an additional 10 arrival units coming in April 2026.

If you’re flying into the Pearl of the Orient, Bayan Lepas International Airport in Penang is getting five departure units and six arrival units.

And for our friends in East Malaysia, both Kota Kinabalu International Airport and Kuching International Airport are getting four units each to speed up your entry.

It’s a massive logistical upgrade for Malaysia Airports (MAHB), ensuring that no matter where you land, you aren’t stuck in a bottleneck.

items.title: MORE THAN A BACKDROP: STEP INSIDE THE ICONIC BANGUNAN SULTAN ABDUL SAMAD
items.content:
If you’ve ever stood at Dataran Merdeka, you’ve definitely looked up at the Bangunan Sultan Abdul Samad and wondered what was behind those heavy wooden doors.

Photo credit: The Star

For over a century, those doors remained largely closed to the public, marking a boundary between the "official" world and the rest of us.

Originally built in the late 1890s to house the British colonial administration, this building was designed to be the ultimate symbol of power and governance in the Straits of Malacca.

Later, it served as the heartbeat of the Malaysian legal system, housing the High Court and the Supreme Court, where some of the nation’s most pivotal legal battles were fought.

Photo credit: The Star

But as of 2 February 2026, the Bangunan Sultan Abdul Samad is no longer just a distant backdrop for your holiday photos.

It has officially transitioned from a restricted government office into a living heritage museum for the people.

You might see the tagline "Six Buildings. Six Roles. One National Story" during your visit, and it’s the key to understanding this massive site.

The BSAS Complex is actually part of a massive RM600 million Warisan KL initiative by Khazanah Nasional to rejuvenate eight of KL's most historic landmarks.

This includes the Sultan Abdul Samad Building, the Pejabat Pos Lama, the former High Court, Panggung Bandaraya, the old FMS Survey Office, and the National Textile Museum.

As this is a Phase 1 opening, you’ll be exploring Block 1 (the main building), while restoration continues on the other blocks to bring the full "National Story" to life in the coming years.

Photo credit: The Star

But there is so much more than just history here; it’s a full lifestyle destination.

Visitors can now enjoy immersive exhibition spaces, a one-stop visitor centre, and even experiential retail and craft-making spaces to get hands-on with local culture.

If you’re a foodie, you’re in for a treat with a lineup that includes BakeHouse by KLCG, The Café by Royal Selangor, Courthouse Cafe, Kaw Kaw Malaya, and Gula Camca.

The new Kuala Lumpur City Gallery within the building chronicles three centuries of our evolution, and for a limited time, entry to these galleries is completely complimentary.

Looking ahead, the Warisan KL project will even include a pedestrian bridge by the end of this year, linking the historic Seri Negara and Carcosa directly to the Perdana Botanical Gardens.

Whether you are a local history buff or a curious traveller, this is your chance to reclaim a piece of the city that was "off-limits" for far too long.

Photo credit: The Star

For a peek at the stunning interiors and the latest "story-worthy" moments, follow them on Instagram at @bsas.kl or check out bsas.com.my.

It’s grand, it’s deeply significant, and it’s finally open for you to experience from within.

Photo credit: BSAS via Instagram

Quick Summary:

The Big News: Bangunan Sultan Abdul Samad (Block 1) is officially open to the public as of 2 February 2026.

  • One Destination: The complex unifies 6 landmarks (including the Old Post Office and National Textile Museum) into a single cultural hub.
  • Limited Time Offer: Entry to the KL City Gallery is complimentary for the first month!
  • Eat & Explore: Home to BakeHouse by KLCG, Courthouse Cafe, and new craft-making spaces.
  • Visiting Info: Open daily from 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM at Dataran Merdeka.

Now that the doors are open, what part of the building’s 100-year history are you most curious to discover?

items.title: NIPAH VIRUS: WHAT’S HAPPENING AT THE BORDERS?
items.content:
Planning your next food hunt in KL or a weekend getaway to the highlands?

You might have seen some headlines floating around about the Nipah virus recently.

Since we’re your savvy local friend, we want to make sure you have the full picture; no panic, just the facts.

Photo credit: New York Post

So, what exactly is the deal with this virus?

In simple terms, Nipah is a virus that usually hangs out with fruit bats and can sometimes jump to other animals or people.

Interestingly, it was actually first discovered right here in Malaysia, specifically in Kampung Sungai Nipah, Negeri Sembilan, back in 1998.

Because of that history, Malaysia is widely considered one of the most prepared countries in the world when it comes to handling this.

Right now, our Health Minister, Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad, has confirmed that the Ministry of Health (MOH) is proactively monitoring reports from West Bengal, India.

But here is the part you’ll actually notice: "gatekeepers" at our borders are on high alert.

Whether you are arriving via KLIA Terminal 1 or 2, seaports, or land crossings, there is increased health surveillance and risk-based screening in place.

This doesn't mean travel is blocked or delayed; it just means our medical teams are being extra vigilant to keep everyone safe.

Think of it like a VIP security check: it’s a quiet, professional layer of protection ensuring your holiday remains uninterrupted.

The MOH has already put emergency medical teams on standby and established clear referral pathways just in case anyone feels under the weather.

As a traveller, your job is simple: practice basic hygiene, wash your hands often, and avoid raw date palm sap or fruit that looks like a bat might have had a snack first.

We’ll keep an eye on the situation for you, but for now, the city is wide open and ready for you to explore.

Stay smart, stay healthy, and enjoy VM2026!

Quick Summary:

  • Border Update: Expect upped health screenings at all international airports, seaports, and land borders.

  • The Situation: MOH is verifying reports from West Bengal, India, and has emergency teams on standby.

  • Local History: Since the virus was first found in Negeri Sembilan (1998), Malaysia’s response protocols are world-class.

  • Action Plan: No travel bans are in place; just keep up with basic hygiene and stay informed.

items.title: SKIP THE TRAFFIC: FREE TRAIN RIDES TO BATU CAVES FOR THAIPUSAM 2026!
items.content:
Getting to Batu Caves for Thaipusam just got a whole lot easier (and cheaper) this year.

Photo credit: CK Travels

In a move that’ll have your wallet doing a happy dance, KTMB has announced free train rides for the KTM Komuter Klang Valley sector.

This isn’t just for locals; whether you’re a traveller from abroad or a domestic tourist, you can ride the rails for RM0.00.

The free rides are valid for two full days, specifically from midnight on January 31 until 11:59 PM on February 1, 2026.

Photo credit: KTMB

If you’ve ever tried to drive toward Batu Caves during this festival, you’ll know that "traffic jam" is an understatement, it’s more like a permanent parking lot.

Taking the train is the ultimate pro-move to reach the world-famous golden Lord Murugan statue without the headache of finding a parking spot that doesn't exist.

Photo credit: The Star

The free travel covers the entire Klang Valley sector, including the Batu Caves–Pulau Sebang, Batu Caves–Port Klang, and Tanjung Malim–KL Sentral routes.

To make things even smoother, 28 stations will operate 24 hours a day for four days straight, from January 30 to February 2.

Photo credit: KTMB via Facebook

For those coming from further away, KTMB is also adding eight extra Electric Train Service (ETS) trips from January 29 to February 3.

These extra ETS trains cover high-demand routes like JB Sentral–Butterworth and KL Sentral–Ipoh, with over 10,000 extra tickets up for grabs.

Whether you're taking the Komuter or the ETS, you still need to tap your Touch ‘n Go card or use the KITS mobile app at the gantry.

Don't worry about the fare as for those two golden days, the amount deducted will be exactly zero.

Just make sure your card has the minimum balance (usually RM5) to trigger the gate, and you're good to go.

It’s the perfect excuse to experience the raw, spiritual energy of one of Malaysia’s most iconic cultural events without the logistical nightmare.

The Quick Summary:

  • What: Free KTM Komuter rides (Klang Valley sector) and 8 extra ETS trips.

  • When: Free rides on Jan 31 & Feb 1; 24-hour service from Jan 30 to Feb 2.

  • Where: Best for reaching Batu Caves; extra ETS for intercity travel.

  • How: Use Touch ‘n Go, KITS app, or debit/credit cards at the gates.

  • Pro-Tip: Wear comfortable shoes and stay hydrated; with 2.5 million people expected, it's going to be a lively one!

items.title: KL 2026 IS THE NEW 2016: WHY WE’RE TRADING BEIGE CAFES FOR UNFILTERED NIGHTS
items.content:
If you’ve been scrolling through TikTok lately, you’ve probably seen the viral "2026 is the new 2016" trend flooding your feed with grainy, high-flash photos and nostalgic throwbacks.

It turns out, the internet has collectively decided that ten years is enough time to miss the chaos of Puppy Dog filters and the simpler joy of the pre-AI era.

Photo credit: Free Malaysia Today

In Kuala Lumpur, this isn’t just a digital trend; it’s a full-blown lifestyle shift that is changing how we eat, play, and explore our concrete jungle.

We are officially entering our "Unfiltered Era," where the curated perfection of 2025 is being traded for the raw, vibrant energy of the mid-2010s.

Forget the quiet, minimalist cafes with white walls; 2026 is about the loud, neon-soaked nights and the thrill of a spontaneous squad photo.

Visit Malaysia 2026 is leaning hard into this vibe, focusing on "Surreal Experiences" that prioritise how a place feels over how it looks on a grid.

Think of it as a return to "Main Character Energy," where you aren’t just a spectator of the city, but the star of your own messy, colourful adventure.

Photo credit: Instagram @turbulency

The heart of this movement is a collective longing for authenticity in a world that has become a bit too "polished" and digitally distant.

We want to touch the textures of the city, taste the smoky heat of street food at Jalan Alor, and laugh until our faces hurt without worrying about the lighting.

Photo credit: Instagram @avostay_my

In 2016, we chased virtual monsters at the KLCC Park and Batu Caves during the Pokémon GO craze; in 2026, we are chasing that same sense of community and wonder.

Photo credit: Vulcan Post

Pro-Tip: When hunting for that 2016 vibe, ditch the DSLR and use your phone’s high-flash—the grainier and "vibier," the better.

You’ll notice the city’s newest hotspots, like the rooftop city park and bars in TRX, are trading "minimalist chic" for bold, spice-themed interiors and panoramic neon views.

Photo credit: Pentago Malaysia

Even our infrastructure is getting a glow-up, with permanent light installations in Bukit Bintang designed to make the streets feel like a 24/7 festival.

Photo credit: The Star

So, put down the editing apps, grab your most comfortable "athleisure" gear, and get ready to live like it’s 2016 all over again.

Because in Kuala Lumpur, the best memories aren't the ones that are perfectly edited, they’re the ones that are a little blurry and a lot of fun.

The Cultural Cheat Sheet

  • DO embrace the "High Flash" aesthetic for your night-out photos; it’s the unofficial uniform of the 2026 trend.

  • DO revisit the city’s "OG" landmarks like KLCC Park and Batu Caves; they are the heart of the nostalgia wave.

  • DON'T over-edit your experiences; the goal of 2026 is to capture the raw, "potato-quality" joy of the moment.

  • DON'T forget to lepak (hang out) without your phone for at least an hour. Ttrue 2016 energy is about being "presently" chaotic.

  • DO use local slang like Huat Ah! when celebrating a win; it’s timeless, high-energy, and always in style.

What was your favourite memory from 2016, and have you found that same "vibe" anywhere in KL lately?

items.title: EVERYTHING YOU NEED TO KNOW ABOUT THE PONGGAL FESTIVAL
items.content:
If you’re wandering through Brickfields or Batu Caves today and hear joyful shouting alongside the smell of sweet, boiling milk, you’ve just found Ponggal!

Photo credit: Malay Mail

The Malaysia Hindu Sangam has officially confirmed that the peak of this vibrant harvest festival falls on January 15, 2026.

For travellers and locals alike, this is Malaysia’s version of "Thanksgiving": a four-day tribute to the Sun God, nature, and the cattle that help put food on our tables.

The name "Ponggal" literally means "to boil over," which is why the main ritual involves cooking a pot of rice, milk, and jaggery until it spills over the rim.

When that milk overflows, everyone shouts "Ponggalo Ponggal!" because a messy stove today means a life overflowing with prosperity and wealth all year round.

Photo credit: The Star

The festival is a four-day journey of renewal, starting with Bhogi on January 14, where homes are scrubbed clean and old belongings are discarded to make way for fresh starts.

Today, January 15, is the main event (Thai Ponggal), where families set up clay pots outdoors and decorate their entrances with stunning Kolams (intricate floor art made of colored rice).

But for those who just got hitched, this year is even more significant because of a tradition called Thala Ponggal.

Thala Ponggal is the very first harvest festival for a newly wedded couple, and it’s a massive milestone celebrated with the bride’s family.

The newlyweds are often gifted new clothes and brass utensils, and they work together to tend the fire, symbolising their first joint effort to bring "sweetness" into their new home.

The celebration continues on January 16 with Mattu Ponggal, a day dedicated entirely to honouring cattle.

You’ll see cows and bulls bathed, their horns painted in bright colours, and draped in garlands as a massive "thank you" for their hard work in the fields.

Finally, the festival wraps up on January 17 with Kaanum Ponggal, which is all about family reunions and younger generations seeking blessings from their elders.

If you’re a traveller in KL, head over to Little India in Brickfields. It’s the best place to soak in the atmosphere, snap photos of the sugarcane-lined streets, and try a bowl of that delicious sweet rice.

It’s a beautiful, noisy, and heartwarming celebration that perfectly captures the "Truly Asia" spirit of our city.

Quick Summary

  • The Main Event: January 15, 2026 is the official peak day for Thai Ponggal.

  • Thala Ponggal: A special "First Ponggal" for newlyweds, traditionally celebrated at the bride's family home.

  • The Ritual: Boiling sweet rice until it overflows to symbolise future abundance.

  • Four Days of Fun: Runs from January 14 (Cleaning) to January 17 (Family Reunions).

  • Best Spot for Tourists: Little India (Brickfields) or the Batu Caves temple grounds for the best visuals and festive food.

Have you ever tried the sweet "Ponggal" rice, or are you planning to visit Brickfields to see the colorful Kolams this weekend?

items.title: MCMC TO TAKE LEGAL ACTION AGAINST X AND XAI OVER USER SAFETY CONCERNS
items.content:
If you’ve noticed your X (formerly Twitter) feed acting a bit differently lately, there is a very big legal reason why.

Photo credit: Astro Awani

The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has officially announced it is pursuing legal action against X Corp. and xAI LLC.

This move comes after the platform reportedly failed to address serious concerns regarding its AI chatbot, Grok, and its ability to generate harmful content.

Authorities have identified that the tool was being misused to create obscene, indecent, and non-consensual manipulated images, which is a massive no-go under Malaysian law.

The government is particularly worried about content involving women and minors, stating that the tech giants haven't done enough to stop it.

Even though Grok has already been temporarily restricted for users in Malaysia as of 11 January 2026, the MCMC is now taking things a step further in the courtroom.

While the X platform itself is still accessible, this legal battle marks a significant crackdown on how AI tools are regulated within our borders.

The Ministry of Communications has made it clear: if you want to operate in Malaysia, you have to follow the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.

For the average traveller or local, this doesn't mean you need to stop tweeting your favourite laksa spots, but it does show that the digital landscape is tightening up.

Expect to see stricter moderation and perhaps more restrictions on AI features as the government pushes for a "safer internet" for everyone.

As always, keep your apps updated and stay mindful of what you're sharing in the digital sphere!

To know more about staying safe online, check out MCMC IG @skmm_mcmc

Quick Summary

  • The News: MCMC is suing X Corp. and xAI over safety failures.

  • The Reason: Misuse of the Grok AI to generate harmful and explicit images.

  • Current Status: Grok is currently restricted in Malaysia while legal proceedings begin.

  • The Law: Authorities are enforcing the Communications and Multimedia Act to protect users, especially women and children.

items.title: 5 SECRET SPOTS IN KL YOU PROBABLY HAVEN'T VISITED YET
items.content:
Photo credit: KL The Guide

Think you’ve seen all of KL? Think again! Whether you’re a local or just visiting, the city is packed with "hidden gems" that go way beyond the standard tourist trails.

From world-record pewter tanks to miniature worlds and deep dives into police history, here are five spots you need to add to your weekend itinerary.

Photo credit: KL The Guide

1. Royal Selangor Visitor Centre: Snap a Pic with a Giant!

Did you know the world’s largest pewter tankard is right here in KL? Standing tall at the Royal Selangor Visitor Centre, this iconic landmark is an absolute must-see.

While you're there, you can take a free guided tour to learn about Malaysia's rich tin mining history and watch master craftsmen at work. If you're feeling creative, sign up for a "School of Hard Knocks" workshop and hammer out your very own pewter masterpiece to take home!

  • 📍 Location: 4, Jalan Usahawan 6, Setapak Jaya, 53300 Kuala Lumpur.

  • ⏰ Hours: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM daily.

  • 🎟️ Admission: FREE entry.

Photo credit: KL The Guide

2. Bank Negara Malaysia Museum and Art Gallery: Cash, Coins, and Culture

If you ever wondered what early currency looked like or how our economy actually works, this is the place to be. Located at Sasana Kijang, this museum features six galleries, including a massive Numismatics (money) collection and a stunning Art Gallery showcasing Southeast Asian works.

The "Nautilus" staircase is also one of the most Instagrammable architectural spots in the city!

  • 📍 Location: Sasana Kijang, 2 Jalan Dato' Onn, 50480 Kuala Lumpur.

  • ⏰ Hours: 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM (Closed on Mondays).

  • 🎟️ Admission: FREE entry.

Photo credit: KL The Guide

3. MinNature Malaysia: Malaysia, But Way Smaller

Experience Malaysia from a completely different perspective—literally! MinNature Malaysia is Asia’s largest indoor miniature exhibition, featuring incredibly detailed 1:87 scale models of our most famous landmarks.

From the busy streets of Bukit Bintang to the heritage buildings of Ipoh, the detail is mind-blowing. Keep an eye out for the interactive elements where you can trigger lights and movement with the push of a button.

  • 📍 Location: JUMPA @ Sungei Wang Plaza, Level 1, Bukit Bintang.

  • ⏰ Hours: 10:00 AM – 10:00 PM daily.

  • 🎟️ Admission: RM30 (Adults), RM20-25 (Seniors/Youth).

Photo credit: KL The Guide

4. Royal Malaysian Police Museum: A Hero’s Journey

For a change of pace, head over to the Royal Malaysian Police Museum in the lush Lake Gardens area. This museum houses an impressive collection of police uniforms, weapons, and vehicles, including actual armored cars and a vintage police plane parked right outside!

It offers a fascinating look at the evolution of law enforcement in Malaysia, from the Melaka Sultanate era right up to the modern day.

  • 📍 Location: 5, Jalan Perdana, Tasik Perdana, 50480 Kuala Lumpur.

  • ⏰ Hours: 10:00 AM – 6:00 PM (Closed on Mondays).

  • 🎟️ Admission: FREE entry.

Photo credit: KL The Guide

5. Art House Gallery Museum of Ethnic Arts: A Hidden Attic of Treasures

Tucked away on the second floor of the Central Market Annexe, this gallery feels like stepping into "Aladdin’s Cave." It’s a specialised museum and antique shop that showcases an incredible range of native artwork, carvings, and textiles, particularly from the ethnic groups of Borneo.

If you're lucky, you'll catch the curator, Leonard, who can give you a personalised tour and share the fascinating stories behind each artifact.

  • 📍 Location: Lot 3.04 & 3.05, Level 2, Annexe Building, Central Market.

  • ⏰ Hours: 11:00 AM – 7:00 PM daily.

  • 🎟️ Admission: FREE (though some special tours may carry a small fee).

 Quick Summary

  • Best for Families: MinNature Malaysia and Royal Selangor Visitor Centre.

  • Best for History Buffs: Royal Malaysian Police Museum and Bank Negara Museum.

  • Best for Art Lovers: Art House Gallery and Bank Negara Art Gallery.

  • Budget Friendly: 4 out of 5 of these spots offer FREE admission!

Which of these hidden gems are you hitting up first this weekend? Let us know in the comments!

The Minister was very clear: your current passport and MyKad are still perfectly valid until they reach their official expiry date.

There is absolutely no need to panic or join a 4 AM queue just to get the "new version" before your old one is done.

The government plans to give everyone a six-month heads-up before the full rollout, so you’ll have plenty of time to plan your visit to the immigration office.

This timing is actually perfect because 2026 is Visit Malaysia Year, and the government is busy beefing up border security and installing more autogates at major entry points like KLIA 1, KLIA 2, and the Johor-Singapore border.

So, whether you’re a local planning a holiday or a frequent traveller to KL, expect smoother moves and tighter security starting next year.

For now, just keep an eye on those expiry dates and enjoy your travels!

Quick Summary

  • What’s New: A high-tech redesign of the Malaysian Passport and MyKad.

items.title: REMBAYUNG SCAM ALERT: DON’T LET A FAKE BOOKING RUIN YOUR DINNER PLANS!
items.content:
If you’ve been scrolling through TikTok lately, chances are you’ve seen the stunning sunset views and lush greenery of Rembayung in Kampung Baru.

Photo credit: Business Today

It is easily one of the most talked-about spots in KL right now, especially since it’s the brainchild of celebrity creator Khairul Aming, but scammers are officially trying to gatecrash the party.

A Malaysian diner recently went viral for almost losing RM300 after trying to book a table through a fake social media account posing as the restaurant.

Photo credit: World of Buzz

The scammer was so convincing that they even sent "official-looking" bank details to collect a hefty reservation fee before the diner caught on.

Between us, while we all want to try that Dendeng Nyet Berapi, no dinner is worth getting your bank account drained by a "ghost" host!

Here is the real tea: if you’re trying to snag a table, you should know that Rembayung is currently fully booked until next Monday (12 January).

Khairul Aming and his team only reopen the reservation system at the end of each week, so anything claiming to have "immediate slots" for a fee is a massive red flag.

The actual restaurant operates strictly on a reservation-only basis through the Umai platform, requiring a minimum of two guests and a maximum of eight per booking.

The official rules are very clear: there is a small deposit required, and they only hold your table for a 15-minute grace period before releasing it to other hungry guests.

Scammers are currently creating "clone" profiles that look nearly identical to the original, but the real management will never ask you for a direct bank transfer to a personal account.

To stay safe, only use the official channels listed below and ensure you are clicking through verified links.

The city centre is beautiful at night, but it's much more enjoyable when you aren't fighting to get your money back from a viral fake-out!

Stay sharp, keep your deposits in your pocket, and always verify before you "pay to play."

The Need-to-Know

  • Official Website: rembayung.com
  • Official Booking Link (Umai): reservation.umai.io/en/widget/rembayung
  • Instagram Handle: @rembayungmy
  • TikTok Handle: @rembayungmy
  • Booking Status: Fully booked until 12 January; new slots open weekly.
  • The "Real" Cost: A small, official deposit of RM10 per person via the Umai system.

items.title: MyNIISe LOGIN UPDATE: THE BIG SWITCH TO MYDIGITAL ID IS HERE!
items.content:
If your phone is currently a graveyard of forgotten passwords and government app logins, we have some news that might actually make you breathe a sigh of relief.

Malaysia is officially doubling down on the "one ID to rule them all" strategy, and the next big shift is happening in just a few days.

Photo credit: The Edge Malaysia

Starting 15 January 2026, the Home Ministry (KDN) is making MyDigital ID the mandatory way to log into the MyNIISe app.

For those who haven't used it yet, MyNIISe is the National Integrated Immigration System, the go-to platform for managing passport renewals and visa-related services.

Think of this update as your digital VIP pass: you can no longer use a separate username or password for immigration-related services on the app.

Now, before our international friends start panicking, take a deep breath: this update is strictly for Malaysian citizens (aged 18 and above) only.

If you are a tourist or an expat currently exploring the sights of KL, you can carry on as usual, as you are currently exempt from this specific requirement.

For the locals, this is the government’s big push for a "passwordless" Malaysia, aiming for a seamless Single Sign-On (SSO) experience across all platforms.

The idea is to have one secure digital identity that works for JPJ, MyNIISe, and eventually every other government portal you can think of.

Between us, the real magic here is security; your identity is verified directly against the JPN database without storing your private data in every single app.

But here is the "savvy friend" advice you really need: don't wait until the night before the deadline to set this up.

We all know how apps love to get "cranky" and congested when everyone tries to log in at the exact same time!

If you haven't registered your MyDigital ID yet, do it now so you aren't stuck staring at a loading screen on January 15.

Quick Summary

  • The Big Change: MyDigital ID becomes the mandatory login for the MyNIISe app.

  • What is MyNIISe?: Malaysia’s National Integrated Immigration System for passports and visas.

  • The Deadline: 15 January 2026.

  • Who Needs It: Malaysian citizens (18+); Tourists and expats are exempt.

  • The Benefit: A secure, Single Sign-On (SSO) experience; no more separate passwords!

items.title: STEP BACK 500 YEARS: WATCH 'AFROT', THE EXCLUSIVE ANCIENT MYSTERY PERFORMANCE!

Photo credit: Jabatan Kebudayaan dan Kesenian Negara (JKKN)

The Story of a Lost Prince

The performance is titled 'Afrot', and it’s a modern take on Mek Mulung, a traditional dance-drama from Kedah that’s so ancient, it’s practically a time machine.

Imagine a performance where the air is thick with the sound of traditional drums and the glow of vibrant costumes, all while actors tell the haunting story of Afrot, the prince of Tok Raja Besar.

Afrot, who has never met his father, was separated from him when the King was kidnapped by Raja Gergasi (Giant King) before Afrot was even born.

Now, he’s embarking on a daring quest to Kota Sarang Semut to find the truth about his lineage and save his family's legacy.

An Authentic Heritage Experience

The show runs for approximately 100 minutes, which is the perfect length to get lost in a world of myth without needing a marathon runner's stamina.

Since this is an authentic heritage piece, the entire performance is conducted in Bahasa Melayu (specifically with that charming Northern Kedah lilt), but the storytelling is so visual you'll feel the emotion regardless.

This isn't just a play; it’s an immersive experience that combines ritualistic dance, rhythmic music, and a heavy dose of Northern Malaysian mystery.

Where and How to Watch

The best part? Admission is absolutely FREE, making this the most budget-friendly, high-culture date night you can find for your weekend itinerary.

Photo credit: Rumah Seni JKKN

The show starts at 8:30 PM at the Dewan Tuanku Canselor (DTC) at UPSI, located in the charming "Education Town" of Tanjung Malim.

While it is located just across the border in Perak, it's a straightforward 1-hour drive from KL via the North-South Expressway, or a breezy KTM Komuter/ETS ride if you want to skip the traffic.

Trust us, witnessing an "Intangible Cultural Heritage" come to life in such an atmospheric setting is worth every minute of the journey.

items.title: THE PROSPERITY TOSS: WHY MALAYSIANS PLAY WITH THEIR FOOD AND HOW TO JOIN THE YEE SANG CHAOS WITHOUT LOOKING LOST
items.content:
If you find yourself in a Kuala Lumpur restaurant during Chinese New Year, you might witness something that looks like a high-stakes food fight.

Don’t call the manager just yet; you’ve just walked into the middle of a Yee Sang session.

To the uninitiated, it looks like a group of adults intentionally making a massive mess with a colourful salad.

But in Malaysia, we call this the "Prosperity Toss," and it is the most energetic social glue you’ll ever experience.

Photo credit: foodforthought.com.my

Yee Sang is essentially a vibrant platter of shredded vegetables, crackers, sweet plum sauce, and the star of the show: strips of raw fish.

The word for fish, phonetically ‘yu’, in Mandarin sounds like "abundance," so eating this is basically like downloading a year’s worth of good vibes directly into your life.

This tradition actually has local roots, having been popularised by a chef in Seremban in the 1940s to drum up business after the war.

Now, it is a mandatory ritual for any gathering between January and March, especially as we head into the Year of the Fire Horse in February 2026.

Pro-Tip: You aren't just eating a meal; you are participating in a collective wish for a "huat" (prosperous) year ahead.

The real magic happens when everyone at the table stands up and grabs their extra-long chopsticks.

One person usually leads the ceremony, pouring the oil and spices while reciting auspicious blessings for health and wealth.

Once the signal is given, you must dive in and begin to toss the ingredients as high into the air as possible.

The rule is simple: The higher you toss the ingredients, the higher your growth and luck will be for the coming year.

Photo credit: Monash University Malaysia

This is not the time to be shy or worry about your table manners; it’s the time to let your inner extrovert shine.

You should be shouting phrases like "Huat ah!" or "Gong Xi Fa Cai" as loudly as you can while the salad flies.

If you are a traveller, don't just watch from the sidelines; most locals will be more than happy to hand you a pair of chopsticks.

It’s a uniquely Malaysian experience. You won’t even find this specific, high-energy version in mainland China!

Pro-Tip: If you're wearing expensive clothes, maybe stand back a few inches, because that plum sauce has a mind of its own.

By the end of the toss, the table will likely look like a colourful disaster zone.

In Malaysia, a messy table after Yee Sang is actually a sign of a very successful and abundant year to come.

So, grab those sticks, find your voice, and get ready to toss your way to greatness.

Photo credit: KL Foodie

The Cultural Cheat Sheet

  • DO: Use your chopsticks to lift the food as high as possible. The "high toss" is the most important part of the ritual.

  • DO: Shout along! Even if you don't know the Mandarin phrases, a loud "Happy New Year!" or "Huat Ah!" works perfectly.

  • DON’T: Worry about the mess. It is expected (and encouraged) for the table to be covered in ingredients by the end.

  • DO: Start with the fish. It represents the "abundance" that sets the tone for the entire year.

  • DON'T: Be a "lepak" (lazy) participant. Stand up and get involved; it’s a group effort!

items.title: NEW YEAR, NEW FLOW: KLIA TERMINAL 1 UPDATES YOUR DEPARTURE ROUTINE!
items.content:
If you’re jetting off from KLIA Terminal 1 this New Year, take note of a small change that makes a big difference to your airport stroll.

Photo credit: Malaysia Airports' FB

Starting 1 January 2026, the Royal Malaysian Customs Department is moving its baggage inspections directly to the departure gates.

Previously, you might have hit a bottleneck at the scanners right after Immigration, but that’s officially a thing of the past.

By moving these checks to the individual gates, the airport aims to reduce congestion and give you a much smoother walk to your flight.

This "consolidated" approach means less standing around in the main departure zone and more time to enjoy your pre-flight coffee.

While the location has changed, the rules haven't: Customs is still on the lookout for prohibited items and unreported currency.

Remember, if you’re carrying cash exceeding USD 10,000 (or the equivalent), you must declare it to keep things legal and stress-free.

Because these checks now happen right before you board, we recommend heading to your boarding gate early to avoid any last-minute huffing and puffing.

The Ministry of Transport ensures that while the process is faster for you, security remains top-notch and fully reinforced.

It’s all part of making KLIA T1 a more efficient, world-class hub that respects your precious vacation time.

So, pack smart, arrive with time to spare, and enjoy a breezy start to your 2026 adventures!

The Quick Summary:


  • Effective Date: 1 January 2026.

  • The Change: Customs checks moved from after Immigration to the Boarding Gates.

Imagine a countdown where the air vibrates not just with music, but with the cool rush of water. From 7:00 PM until 12:30 AM,  SplashMania sheds its daytime charm for a spectacle of light, colour, and raw, endless energy. Photo credit Fastbridge Gamuda

items.title: ZOO NEGARA WELCOMES NEW PANDA DUO FOR 10-YEAR STAY
items.content:
Welcome to Malaysia, dear Chen Xing and Xiao Yue! 

Photo credit Utusan Malaysia 

On 18 November 2025, Malaysia joyfully welcomed Giant Pandas Chen Xing (male) and Xiao Yue (female), who arrived from the People’s Republic of China (PRC). Their presence highlighted the close diplomatic ties between the two nations. After arriving, they spent a month in quarantine under the care of dedicated veterinarians and keepers before meeting the public. 

The pair had been confirmed by Deputy Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Huang Tiong Si, as reported by The Star. They arrived under a 10-year agreement, giving Malaysians plenty of time to get to know them.

Their arrival followed the farewell to beloved Xing Xing and Liang Liang in May 2025, after 11 memorable years and three cubs. That earlier pair first came in 2014 to mark 40 years of Malaysia–China diplomatic ties.

Photo credit Zoo Negara

Chen Xing and Xiao Yue, being a younger duo, were part of a new panda loan initiative signed on 16 April during Chinese President Xi Jinping’s state visit. With them settling into their new home, the next decade of panda joy at Zoo Negara had officially begun.

Heartfelt thanks went to everyone who made their arrival a success. Malaysians looked forward to showering them with love and continuing efforts to protect this iconic species. 

Come visit Zoo Negara to welcome Chen Xing and Xiao Yue, learn more about giant panda conservation, and be part of Malaysia’s next decade of panda love.

items.title: HAIKU KL'S "SUNSET KALYANAM" SETS RECORD FOR LARGEST INDIAN MOCK WEDDING IN MALAYSIA
items.content:
Photo credit Haiku KL

Haiku KL’s Sunset Kalyanam has officially entered the Malaysia Book of Records, attracting 601 attendees and surpassing the previous benchmark of 480 participants to claim the title for “Most Turnouts in an Indian Mock Wedding.” Held at Glasshouse at Seputeh, the event offered a modern twist on a South Indian wedding, emphasizing culture, community, and shared joy.

The evening recreated traditional Tamil kalyanam elements — from dhol rhythms and thematic décor to communal banana leaf dining — but presented them in a social, interactive format, allowing guests to enjoy the festive atmosphere without formal wedding rituals.

Photo credit Haiku KL

Music was a highlight, with DJs Jay, Moski, MOONCUE, D, Slick Vick, Tva, Vind, Kashy Kash, and Buzzarmstrong keeping the energy high for nine hours, complemented by dhol performances from Rsquare and Amanda, and live acts by Amos Paul, Arvind Raj, and Elcfer. Official Emcees Jayshree & Puvanan, along with Good Tapes Music’s live band, elevated the experience further.

The event also showcased collaborations with local SMEs, including Bali Euphoria Tour & Travel, Jharee, Ministry of Cakes, Mandali Concept, Ipoh Ambulance, High Society Events, Saaro Events, False Prophets, Vdesignsz, Vdrapes, and Pani Puri Klang, whose contributions shaped the vibrant cultural and sensory experience.

Photo credit Haiku KL

Haiku KL noted that the record turnout reflects a growing appreciation for cultural expression in contemporary social spaces. “This achievement was made possible by the people who attended,” they said. “It’s inspiring to see a cultural concept embraced so wholeheartedly and recognised nationally.”

Sunset Kalyanam now stands as Haiku KL’s most significant cultural showcase, blending tradition with modern social culture and marking a milestone in Malaysia’s lifestyle and entertainment scene.

items.title: CELEBRATING LIGHT AND CULTURE: THE GRAND DEEPAVALI CELEBRATION AT SUNWAY LAGOON AND SUNWAY LOST WORLD OF TAMBUN
items.content:
Photo credit: Sunway Theme Parks

Sunway City Kuala Lumpur & Sunway City Ipoh, 20 October 2025 - This Deepavali, Sunway Lagoon and Sunway Lost World of Tambun shone brighter than ever as both parks lit up the night skies with a spectacular three-minute fireworks display.

The dazzling show marked the highlight of the Grand Deepavali Celebration, one of Malaysia’s biggest festive events celebrating light, culture, and togetherness.

Running from 15 to 22 October 2025, the week-long celebration transformed both theme parks into vibrant cultural destinations filled with music, colour, and festive cheer - drawing thousands of visitors, from local families and tourists to international travellers seeking an authentic Malaysian experience.

Photo credit: Sunway Theme Parks

A Festival of Light and Joy

Deepavali, known as the Festival of Lights, celebrates the triumph of good over evil and light over darkness.

This year, Sunway Theme Parks brought that spirit to life through captivating performances, interactive experiences, and cultural unity.

Guests enjoyed an array of lively shows, including Melodies of Deepavali, the vibrant Colours of Bhangra, and an energetic Dhol Parade that had everyone dancing along.

The evening ended with a musical fireworks spectacle, painting the sky in bursts of colour - a symbol of joy, unity, and new beginnings.

The parks also featured meet-and-greet sessions with the beloved Captain Quack and Family, alongside colourful kolam displays and festive photo zones, offering picture-perfect memories for all ages.

The atmosphere was one of laughter, music, and celebration - a true reflection of Malaysia’s multicultural harmony.

Photo credit: Sunway Theme Parks

A Celebration of Togetherness

“Deepavali is a celebration of light, culture, and togetherness - and at Sunway Theme Parks, we’re proud to honour that spirit,” said Professor Calvin Ho, Chief Executive Officer of Sunway Theme Parks.

“Our goal is to create inclusive spaces where people from all walks of life can come together to experience Malaysia’s multicultural heritage.”

This year’s Deepavali celebration continues Sunway Theme Parks’ tradition of promoting unity through culture, following the success of previous festive events such as Hari Raya, Chinese New Year, and Christmas.

These initiatives highlight Sunway’s role in bringing communities together through shared experiences that go beyond entertainment - fostering understanding, inclusivity, and joy.

Photo credit: Sunway Theme Parks

Shining the Way to Visit Malaysia Year 2026

As Malaysia prepares for Visit Malaysia Year 2026, cultural events like The Grand Deepavali Celebration are essential in showcasing the nation’s living heritage and attracting global travellers.

By blending cultural performances, local artistry, and community spirit, Sunway Lagoon and Sunway Lost World of Tambun are not only creating memorable guest experiences but also contributing to the growth of Malaysia’s tourism sector.

These festivals help drive economic benefits to surrounding communities, strengthen tourism partnerships, and reinforce Malaysia’s image as a welcoming and diverse destination.

More than just a theme park celebration, Deepavali at Sunway represents Malaysia’s strength in unity - where people from different backgrounds come together to celebrate light, joy, and hope.

Photo credit: Sunway Theme Parks

Festivities Continue

The Grand Deepavali Celebration continues until 22 October 2025, featuring ongoing performances, festive treats, and fun family-friendly activities across both Sunway Lagoon and Sunway Lost World of Tambun.

Visitors are encouraged to join the festivities and capture the magic of Deepavali - whether by watching cultural dances, enjoying festive delicacies, or simply basking in the glow of lights that illuminate both parks.

Stay updated with upcoming events, collaborations, and immersive experiences by following Sunway Lagoon Studios on Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, and RedNote.

Photo credit: Sunway Theme Parks

About Sunway Lagoon

Located in Sunway City Kuala Lumpur, Sunway Lagoon is Malaysia’s premier multi-park destination, spanning 88 acres of fun and adventure. Recognised as Asia’s Best Attraction, it features seven unique experiences:

  • Water Park
  • Amusement Park
  • Wildlife Park
  • X Park
  • Scream Park
  • Sunway Lost Lagoon
  • Sunway Lagoon Night Park, home to Captain Quack Land

With thrilling rides, wildlife encounters, and world-class entertainment, the park is home to record-breaking attractions like the World’s Largest Surf Pool and Vuvuzela, the world’s largest vortex ride.

Operating Hours: Wednesday to Monday, 10:00 A.M. – 11:00 P.M.


About Sunway Lost World of Tambun

Nestled within Sunway City Ipoh, Sunway Lost World of Tambun offers a one-of-a-kind eco-adventure surrounded by lush jungles and 400-million-year-old limestone formations.

The park features seven attraction zones - Water Park, Amusement Park, Petting Zoo, Tin Valley, Adventure Park, Tiger Valley, and the Night Park.

Highlights include the enchanting Luminous Forest, the fiery Flaming Percussion performance, and relaxing natural hot springs.

Guests can also enjoy local delights at Ipoh Street and get up close with friendly animals at the Petting Zoo.

Operating Hours:

  • Day Park: 11:00 A.M. – 6:00 P.M.
  • Night Park & Hot Springs: 6:00 P.M. – 11:00 P.M.

(Closed every Tuesday, except Public Holidays and School Holidays.)


Join the Celebration of Light

As Malaysia’s top family destinations, Sunway Lagoon and Sunway Lost World of Tambun invite everyone to experience Deepavali in grand style.

Beyond the fireworks and festivities, the celebration is a reminder of what truly matters - love, unity, and the light that shines brightest when shared.

Because at Sunway Theme Parks, every celebration isn’t just an event - it’s a meaningful experience that brings people together under one radiant sky.


Issued by Sunway Theme Parks

Date: 20 October 2025

items.title: NIGHT SPLASH RETURNS THIS NOVEMBER - K-POP ENERGY LIGHTS UP SELANGOR
items.content:
If you think you’ve seen everything a waterpark can offer, think again.


When the sun dips below the horizon, SplashMania Waterpark@ Gamuda Cove transforms into a glowing dreamscape - where neon lights ripple across the water, the air hums with bass, and laughter echoes beneath a star-drenched sky.


This November, Night Splash: Amazonia K-Wave makes its dazzling return - an after-dark takeover infused with K-Pop rhythm, dazzling fire shows, and slides that gleam like liquid light.


Forget your usual weekend plans; this is where night energy meets splash-soaked fun.


Credits to GL Play by Gamuda Land


The Scene: Where Water Meets Rhythm


Picture this: you’re standing beneath the colossal Amazonia Ship - a landmark by day, but at night, it morphs into a glowing rooftop deck pulsing with bass and K-Pop beats.


Fire bursts paint the night sky, slides shimmer like light trails, and a sea of people moves in rhythm as DJs drop remix after remix.


You take a sip of your drink, feel the cool night breeze, and realise something magical - you’re not just watching the night unfold; you’re part of it.


And the best part? You can still jump on the slides, float through illuminated pools, or just chill with your crew while soaking up the festival atmosphere.


Whether you’re a die-hard K-Pop stan or simply chasing something new to do after dark, this one’s for you.

Every Friday and Saturday in November, SplashMania turns into a livewire spectacle of music, light, and water.

items.title: KL HOP-ON HOP-OFF: YOUR FRONT ROW SEAT TO KUALA LUMPUR'S BEST VIEW
items.content:
The KL Hop-On Hop-Off Bus Tour offers one of the easiest and most enjoyable ways to explore Kuala Lumpur. This open-top double-decker bus takes you past iconic landmarks like the Petronas Twin Towers, KL Tower, and Merdeka Square, with the freedom to hop on and off at any stop. Explore at your own pace by shopping in Bukit Bintang, visiting cultural sites, or sampling local street food. Perfect for first-time visitors and locals alike, it’s a hassle-free way to experience the vibrant sights and sounds of Malaysia’s capital. 

 
Picture Credit: TripAdvisor

Picture Credit: TripAdvisor

The KL Hop-On Hop-Off Bus has been upgraded to deliver an even more enjoyable and convenient sightseeing experience in Kuala Lumpur. Now featuring six brand-new open-top buses, passengers can soak in panoramic city views in comfort and style. Each bus offers free Wi-Fi and USB charging ports, keeping travellers connected on the go. To enhance the experience for international visitors, audio commentary in 11 languages provides engaging insights into the city’s landmarks and culture. With these upgrades, the KL Hop-On Hop-Off Bus is a modern, comfortable, and informative way to explore Malaysia’s vibrant capital.

Picture Credit: TripAdvisor

The KL Hop-On Hop-Off Day Tour is a fun and flexible way to explore Kuala Lumpur’s top attractions at your own pace. Operating daily from 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM, the double-decker bus follows a loop with over 20 strategic stops, including the Petronas Twin Towers, KL Tower, Bukit Bintang, Chinatown, Central Market, and Merdeka Square. Choose between 1-day or 2-day passes, starting from RM45 for Malaysians and RM55 for international visitors, and enjoy unlimited rides within your chosen period. Hop off to explore any attraction, then hop back on when you’re ready, all while taking in panoramic views from the comfort of your seat. Whether sightseeing, shopping, or simply soaking up the city’s lively atmosphere, the KL Hop-On Hop-Off Day Tour offers a convenient, affordable, and enjoyable way to experience Kuala Lumpur.

Picture Credit: Agoda.com

If you can’t explore during the day, don’t worry, the KL Hop-On Hop-Off Bus also offers a Night Tour. Operating daily from 8:00 PM to 10:00 PM, this guided evening ride takes you past Kuala Lumpur’s most iconic landmarks, including the Petronas Twin Towers, KL Tower, Merdeka Square, Saloma Link Bridge, and Bukit Bintang. Unlike the day tour, the night route is non-stop, letting you sit back and enjoy the illuminated skyline with live commentary from an onboard guide. Tickets start from RM40 for Malaysians and RM80 for international visitors, making it an affordable yet memorable way to experience the city’s glittering nightlife. Perfect for photographers, couples, or anyone seeking a unique evening adventure, the KL Hop-On Hop-Off Night Tour reveals Kuala Lumpur at its most captivating.

Picture Credit: Hop On Hop Off by Headout
Picture Credit: KL Hop On Hop Off Online

In the end, the KL Hop-On Hop-Off Bus Tour is more than just a ride; it’s a complete Kuala Lumpur experience. Combining convenience, comfort, and flexibility, it allows you to explore the city’s top attractions without the hassle of navigating traffic or public transport. Whether you’re discovering the sights by day or admiring the skyline by night, the tour offers a unique perspective on Kuala Lumpur’s vibrant culture, striking architecture, and lively energy. With its affordable passes and scenic routes, it’s the perfect way to make the most of your visit and truly experience what makes Malaysia’s capital so dynamic and unforgettable.

Picture Credit: KKday

items.title: DARE TO ENTER? SUNWAY LAGOON NIGHTS OF FRIGHT 11 PROMISES TERRORS BEYOND IMAGINATION!
items.content:
More than just jump scares, Nights of Fright 11 fuses Malaysian folklore (pontianak, pocong) with global horror culture, conjuring a unique and terrifying experience unlike any other.

On 25 September, the festival opened in an unforgettable fashion. The Puppetmaker, Hantutu, Hantu Kum Kum, and Poh Kong emerged from a striking pink hearse, as the night unfolded with a spine-chilling ballerina performance that set the tone for the horrors ahead.

Image provided to KL The Guide

Malaysia's most chilling Halloween event, Nights of Fright at Sunway Lagoon, returns for its 11th edition - darker, deadlier and more terrifying than ever. From 26 September to 2 November 2025, every Friday-Sunday, witness the Puppetmaker take the stage in the nation's ultimate fright fest.

Image Credits: Klook

Nights of Fright has risen into a legendary attraction, luring over one million visitors from near and far. And with their collaboration with creative partners such as Poh Kong, Pop Mart, and Libresse, this year's Nights of Fright unleashes seven terrifying new haunted houses. Among them is the world's first life-size Blind Box Haunted House, a scream-worthy experience you won't find elsewhere. 

Image provided to KL The Guide


A New Era of Fear


Step inside the Puppetmaker's twisted workshop, a place where puppets move on their own, shadows whisper in the dark, and nightmares are strung together by fear itself. 


Expect terrifying fun attractions at Nights of Fright 11, including: 
  • 8 Haunted Houses: Karak - The Kampong Killers, Tiki Terror, The Puppetmaker, The Blind Box, Fortunes and Freaks, Horrorwood Studios, Legends of Horror, and The Freezer 2: High Voltage
  • 1 Haunted Theatre: Scary Tales Theatre featuring Malaysian star Nadia Brian as PotianAxe 
  • 3 Scare Zones: Hantu Hell, Pontianak X Pocong, and Horrorwood Boulevard: Slashers & Dolls
  • 11 Thrill Rides & 3 Live Show Stages
Image provided to KL The Guide

There are also some interesting partner collaborations to look forward to:
  • Libresse: Escape of Hantu Kum Kum - an immersive escape experience
  • Poh Kong: Villain Hitting - a sinister cultural ritual reimagined for the festival of fear
  • Pop Mart: Eerie Photo Ops, marking the brand's first-ever collaboration with a theme park
Image provided to KL The Guide

Naturally, no fright fest is complete without eerie street eats, hauntingly themed merchandise, and carnival-like entertainment that brings the entire park to life.




Since its debut in 2013, Nights of Fright has terrified over one million visitors and become Malaysia's largest and longest-running Halloween festival.

Image provided to KL The Guide


The darkness has risen. The Puppetmaker awaits. The question is... will you survive Nights of Fright 11? Dare to find out, only at Sunway Lagoon from September 26th to November 2nd, 2025.


Tickets are now available for purchase on the Sunway Super App, OTAs, and the official Sunway Lagoon website.

Image via Sunway Lagoon Studios (Facebook)

Ticket rates for Nights of Fright 11 are:
  • RM128 - One (1) admission ticket + mystery flavoured popcorn voucher
  • RM228 - One (1) admission ticket + express pass + mystery flavoured popcorn voucher
The night is dark, the scares are waiting! So gather your courage, rally your friends, and step into the terror of Nights of Fright 11!

Find out more at the official website, or follow Sunway Lagoon Studios on Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, TikTok and RedNote.

items.title: TUAH 1895 @ BUKIT BINTANG: WHERE CRAVINGS MEET COMFORT

Pak Tok Signature delivers the bold flavours of Malaysia’s food capital straight to Bukit Bintang.

One of Asia’s most celebrated seafood restaurants, Ministry of Crab, finds a home at TUAH 1895.

Photo credit: TUAH 1895 @ BBCC

Must-try dishes:

items.title: REACH FOR THE SKIES: THE ALL-NEW PETRONAS TWIN TOWERS SKY XPERIENCE
items.content:
Photo credit: Petronas Twin Towers

Welcome to the PETRONAS Twin Towers Sky Xperience — or PeTT SkyX — a reimagined journey that will take you higher, further, and deeper into the spirit of Malaysia. 


Heart of a Nation. Peak of Your Journey.

Rising majestically above the city, the PETRONAS Twin Towers are more than just a must-visit attraction — they are the heartbeat of Malaysia. 

The towers stand as a proud symbol of Malaysia’s rich heritage, architectural mastery, and unyielding drive for innovation. 

With PeTT SkyX, your visit transforms from a simple sightseeing trip into an immersive exploration of history, culture, and engineering brilliance.

Photo credit: Petronas Twin Towers

A Sky-High Journey Like Never Before

The new PETRONAS Twin Towers Sky Xperience invites you to explore a series of curated attractions designed to immerse you in both the beauty of the towers and the vibrancy of Malaysia:

Photo credit: Petronas Twin Towers

  • Sky Lobby – Where your elevated adventure begins, blending architectural elegance with warm Malaysian hospitality.

  • Skybridge @ Level 41 – Begin your journey at the world’s tallest double-decked bridge, linking the two towers. Here, you’ll be greeted with sweeping aerial views of Kuala Lumpur’s skyline, KLCC Park, and the bustling city below.

Photo credit: Petronas Twin Towers

  • Sky Café @ Level 83 (coming soon) – Sip and savour as you float above the city.

  • Sky Deck @ Level 86 – Continue upward to where panoramic vistas of Kuala Lumpur unfold before your eyes. Informational displays and interactive digital exhibits reveal the design, construction, and symbolism behind these architectural wonders.

Photo credit: Petronas Twin Towers

  • Sky Shop – Before you leave, explore the PETRONAS Twin Towers Gift Shop on Level 83 or the Concourse for exclusive souvenirs that capture the spirit of your journey.

  • Skywalk 360 – Experience a new, virtual perspective with a unique skyline walk.

Photo credit: Petronas Twin Towers

Guided for a Deeper Experience

All tours are conducted in small, guided groups, ensuring an intimate and enriching visit. 

Knowledgeable guides bring the towers’ story to life, offering fascinating insights into their place in Malaysia’s cultural and economic landscape.

Photo credit: Petronas Twin Towers

More Than Just a View

PeTT SkyX is more than an upgrade — it’s a bold transformation. 

It combines world-class facilities with immersive storytelling, connecting visitors to Malaysia’s identity as a nation that values knowledge, creativity, and diversity.

It’s an experience that bridges education and adventure, making it perfect for families, solo travellers, and curious minds from around the globe.

Photo credit: Petronas Twin Towers

Plan Your Visit

The PETRONAS Twin Towers Sky Xperience is open to all who are ready to see Malaysia from a new perspective.


Tickets: Available online at www.petronastwintowers.com.my 

Tip: Tickets are limited — book early to secure your preferred time slot.

items.title: PETROSAINS, THE DISCOVERY CENTRE: IGNITING CURIOSITY, INSPIRING DISCOVERY
items.content:
Photo credit: Petrosains

Discover a World of Curiosity

Situated in the heart of Kuala Lumpur, Petrosains, The Discovery Centre stands as one of the city’s most captivating attractions, inspiring learning through the wonders of science and innovation.

Housed within the iconic PETRONAS Twin Towers, the centre spans approximately 7,000 square metres — a sprawling playground of knowledge and discovery. 

With over 300 exhibits and programmes, Petrosains seamlessly blends cutting-edge science and technology into an interactive, hands-on journey. 

Here, you can explore everything from the tiniest microscopic marvels to the vastness of the cosmos; from fearsome prehistoric dinosaurs to futuristic robotics and artificial intelligence.

This is more than a science centre — it’s a space where excitement soars, curiosity is nurtured, and minds of all ages are inspired. 

Now is the perfect time to immerse yourself in this one-of-a-kind educational realm. 

Ready to plan your visit? Here’s a glimpse at the must-see highlights.

Embark on a Journey of Wonder

Science here is far from rigid or textbook-bound. 

Petrosains takes a hands-on, immersive, and innovative approach, ensuring every visitor gets to experience science from fresh perspectives.

Photo credit: Petrosains

Energy Capsule

Right at the main entrance, you’ll spot the Energy Capsule — a revolutionary ride introduced in 2022. 

Far from an ordinary roller coaster, it takes you on a thrilling narrative of human civilisation and our ever-growing thirst for energy, ending with thought-provoking ideas for a sustainable future.

Photo credit: Petrosains

SPARKZ

From a Wind Tube launching paper helicopters to an interactive Grain Pit and digital Interactive Art walls, SPARKZ combines science with creativity. 

Challenge friends and family to a Robo Soccer match, or catch one of the centre’s lively science shows scheduled throughout the day.

Photo credit: Petrosains

The Platform

Ever wondered what life is like in the middle of the ocean? 

Step into a realistic oil platform model right in the heart of Kuala Lumpur and see for yourself how offshore operations work.

Photo credit: Petrosains

SPEED!

For motorsport fans, SPEED! offers adrenaline-charged fun. 

Race in a Formula 1 simulator, test your reflexes with the Batak Pro, or try the Mind Ball challenge — where telekinesis is your only weapon against an opponent.

Photo credit: Petrosains

Café Mesra

Exploring science works up an appetite. 

Refuel at the first Café Mesra in KLCC, open since 2023, with a menu of tasty bites and refreshing beverages.

Photo credit: Petrosains

Sustainability Gallery

Launched in 2023, this 2,760-square-foot gallery focuses on climate change, environmental impact, and ways to live greener. 

Interactive displays encourage visitors to embrace sustainability as a lifelong habit.

Photo credit: Petrosains

3D Theatre

Sit back, put on your 3D glasses, and enjoy a cinematic journey that focuses on sustainability — supporting PETRONAS’ mission to achieve Net Zero Carbon Emissions by 2050.

Photo credit: Petrosains

Tech Lab

Step into the future: meet robots, simulate flight, explore big data, and even learn to Code.

Photo credit: Petrosains

Space

Get a taste of life beyond Earth in the SPACE exhibit. 

Discover astronaut training, spacecraft technology, and even try programming a Mars Rover replica.

Photo credit: Petrosains

Geotime Diorama

Travel back 200 million years to walk among the dinosaurs — including T-Rex and Spinosaurus — while learning about Earth’s geological history.

Photo credit: Petrosains

Maker Studio

This is where innovation begins. 

Learn to build drones, operate robotic arms, construct wind turbines, and more through hands-on workshops.

Photo credit: Petrosains

XPLORASI – Petrosains Gift Shop

Before you leave, stop by for unique souvenirs, science kits, and educational toys — perfect mementoes of your visit.

Photo credit: Petrosains

Your Journey Starts Here

Since its opening, Petrosains has remained committed to making science engaging, emotional, and intellectually satisfying. 

Every corner of the centre is designed to spark curiosity and inspire innovation. 

Who knows? Your visit might just lead to the next big idea that changes the world.


Get your tickets today! https://eticket.petrosains.com.my/

items.title: WORLD SINGING DAY KUALA LUMPUR 2025: SING TOGETHER, UNITE THE WORLD
items.content:
Photo credit: World Singing Day

No singing experience needed, just bring your joy! 🎶

The stage is set, but this isn’t a concert.

There are no auditions, no competitions, and no judges.

Instead, World Singing Day Kuala Lumpur 2025 invites everyone!

Yes, even you shower singers and car karaoke champions, join in to raise your voices and celebrate life through song.

This year, the event promises to be more special than ever as World Singing Day (WSD) Malaysia partners with KL The Guide in support of Visit Malaysia 2026.

Together, we’re turning the city into a stage where locals and visitors can experience the unifying power of music.

📅 Date: Saturday, 18 October 2025
🕓 Time: 4:00–6:00 pm (singing begins at 4:30 pm)
📍 Venue: Rooftop Garden, Lalaport BBCC Kuala Lumpur (Monorail/LRT Hang Tuah Station)
🎟 Admission: Free – just bring yourself!
👉 Register now: https://bit.ly/WSDKL2025

Photo credit: World Singing Day

Why You Should Join (No Matter How You Sing)

At World Singing Day Kuala Lumpur, it’s not about being good at singing; it’s about feeling good while singing.

Whether you’ve not sung since your school days or belt out tunes daily, you’ll feel right at home here.

✨Zero Pressure – Sing for joy, not perfection.
✨All Lyrics Provided – Songbooks and e-songbooks will keep you in tune.
✨Familiar Tunes – From local favourites to international classics, you’ll know the songs.
✨Inclusive Atmosphere – From kids to seniors, everyone belongs.

As one participant put it:

“There’s something uplifting about singing with others. It creates this sense of connection that’s hard to put into words.” 

Photo credit: World Singing Day

Special Highlights for 2025

🌟First-timers Welcome – Around half of our participants each year are newcomers, so don’t be shy!
🌟Heartwarming Guests – Youths from BINA Malaysia NGO and children from HiiChiiKok Foundation will join in the celebration.
🌟“Why I Sing” e-Wall – Share your story about how music lifts you up.
🌟Central & Accessible – Just 5 minutes from Bukit Bintang MRT—no excuses not to come!

Photo credit: World Singing Day

The People Behind the Magic

World Singing Day Kuala Lumpur is powered by amazing volunteers—teachers, sports coaches, engineers, and students in fields from psychology to food science.

None of them is a professional musician, but together, they make the music happen.

Guiding us once again is our beloved host, Ms. Lee Yong Yong (Shareen), World Singing Day ambassador and polytechnic English lecturer, who has been the heart of WSD Malaysia since 2018.

As one young participant once said:

“I love World Singing Day. Music heals my soul.”

Photo credit: World Singing Day

About World Singing Day

Founded in 2012 by Scott Johnson, World Singing Day is a global movement celebrating how singing together breaks down barriers and builds community.

With the motto “Sing Together, Unite the World”, WSD is celebrated in more than 50 cities worldwide.

Since its start in Kuala Lumpur in 2018, the event has shown Malaysians that you don’t need talent—just enthusiasm.

🌍 Learn more: https://worldsingingday.org/
📸 Follow: Instagram – @worldsingingdaymalaysia

Photo credit: World Singing Day

Final Note

The World Singing Day Kuala Lumpur 2025 isn’t just an event—it’s a reminder that music has the power to unite us, heal us, and bring joy.

So, bring your friends, family, or just yourself, and get ready to sing your heart out under the city sky.

Because here, every voice matters. 💜

items.title: KEYS TO FREEDOM: MY MALAYSIAN ROAD TRIP WITH AVIS
items.content:
Photo credit: Avis Malaysia

When I landed in Kuala Lumpur for a long-awaited holiday, I had one goal in mind: to see as much of Malaysia as possible. 

The food, the culture, the beaches, the mountains…I wanted it all. 

But as I stood in the taxi queue outside the airport, I realised that relying on public transport or ride-hailing would mean I would be limited by schedules, routes, and waiting times.

That’s when I remembered Avis Malaysia. 

A quick online booking later, I found myself standing inside their Kuala Lumpur city outlet, where a friendly staff member handed me the keys to a fresh-looking Proton X50. 

My journey was about to begin.

From City Streets to Sacred Caves

The first stop on my self-made itinerary was Batu Caves, just a short drive from the city. 

I left at dawn, watching KL’s skyline fade in the rear-view mirror. 

By the time the tourist buses arrived, I’d already climbed the colourful steps and stood inside the limestone cavern, marvelling at the temple’s beauty. 

Freedom to move on my own terms—it was exactly what I wanted.

Photo credit: Avis Malaysia

The Scenic Route to Ipoh

After breakfast, I headed back to the city and pointed the car north toward Ipoh. 

With no rush, I cruised through green hills and roadside towns, windows down, letting the warm breeze fill the car. 

In Ipoh, I sipped its famous white coffee in a heritage café and wandered through colonial streets. 

A roadside sign for Kellie’s Castle caught my eye, and without hesitation, I turned off to explore - something I could never have done without my own wheels.

Photo credit: Avis Malaysia

Tranquillity by the lake in Taiping

Taiping’s Lake Gardens mirrored the rain-heavy skies and ancient angsana trees, their branches bowing like calligraphy. 

In nearby Kuala Sepetang, I boarded a boat through mangroves, learned how charcoal kilns breathe, and lunched on prawns still tasting of the sea. 

With the weather on our side, we found a quaint little spot for dinner, where we basked in a bit of that local Taiping life. 

A friendly passerby then suggested we check out the night safari adventure at the Taiping zoo, which turned out to be another unplanned surprise that added some memorable experiences to our road trip.

Photo credit: Avis Malaysia

Coastal Roads and Penang Vibes

The next morning, I set out for Penang, crossing the famous Penang Bridge as the sun dipped low. 

Gurney Drive was alive with hawker stalls, and the aroma of char kway teow filled the night air. 

My Avis rental handled the winding hills of Penang Island with ease, making sightseeing from Kek Lok Si Temple to hidden beaches effortless. 

In the end, we filled our bellies and called it a day.

Photo credit: Avis Malaysia

Back to KL, Full of Memories

By the time I returned the car in Kuala Lumpur, I’d covered hundreds of kilometres and dozens of unforgettable moments. 

My road trip wasn’t just about getting from point A to B—it was about the freedom to take detours, linger longer, and discover places I didn’t even know I wanted to see.

Photo credit: Avis Malaysia
