items.title: FARM IN THE CITY: A MUST VISIT VILLAGE-THEMED PETTING ZOO NEAR KUALA LUMPUR
items.content:
Photo credit: Farm in The City

If you’re visiting Kuala Lumpur and want to experience a side of Malaysia beyond skyscrapers and shopping malls, take a short 30-minute trip to Farm in The City in Seri Kembangan.

This award-winning attraction is more than just a place to see animals — it’s a living, breathing Malaysian kampung (village) where wildlife, culture, and community come together.

Perfect for families, couples, and curious travellers, Farm in The City has been delighting visitors for years with its intimate wildlife encounters and rustic charm.

Now, in 2025, it’s unveiling a fresh lineup of activities and attractions that make it an even more exciting destination.

Photo credit: Farm in The City

A Malaysian Village Brought to Life

From the moment you enter, you’re greeted by shady paths and traditional wooden huts surrounded by free-ranging animals.

This is a petting zoo designed to slow you down — to let you wander, breathe in fresh air, and enjoy the simple pleasures of rural Malaysia.

Photo credit: Farm in The City

Every corner offers an Instagram-worthy moment: tropical plants framing tranquil ponds, rustic wooden bridges, and adorable animals just waiting to meet you.

It’s a peaceful escape from the city, where you can truly immerse yourself in nature.

Photo credit: Farm in The City

Up-Close with Unique Wildlife

One of 2025’s highlights is the Sunny Oasis, a lush tropical enclosure where you can take part in our Squirrel Monkey and Dusky Wallaby Interaction Sessions.

These playful, curious creatures move freely in their naturalistic habitat, and visitors can observe and, at times, interact directly under the guidance of trained rangers.

Another crowd favourite is the new Raccoon Hugging Sessions, held daily at 3:30pm in the Exhibition Hall.

Photo credit: Farm in The City

Fully supervised, this gentle close-up experience lets you hold and connect with these inquisitive animals — a rare opportunity in Malaysia. (Tip: Arrive early to secure your spot for this activity.)

Throughout the day, wildlife interaction and free feeding sessions take place every 15 minutes across different stations.

From feeding gentle pigeons and meeting playful lemurs to greeting exotic birds and watching cheeky otters, each session is led by friendly rangers who share fascinating facts while you enjoy the moment.

Photo credit: Farm in The City

Ranger Outpost – A Learning Adventure for All Ages

For those who love to learn while exploring, the Ranger Outpost is a must-visit.

This indoor education centre features a Mini Museum with real wildlife skeletons, preserved specimens, and interactive displays that bring Malaysia’s biodiversity to life.

It’s also home to the Junior Farm Rangers (JFR) programme, held every other Saturday.

In this hands-on class, children aged 5–12 are guided by enthusiastic rangers to explore topics about the natural world, enjoy close-up encounters with real animals, and get creative in fun craft sessions.

It’s a memorable way to inspire young explorers with a passion for nature.

Photo credit: Farm in The City

DIY Culture & Creative Fun

Add a splash of culture to your visit with the DIY Batik Painting & Button Badge Crafting Session.

Open to all ages, you can try the traditional Malaysian craft of batik painting and create your own colourful design.

Or personalise a unique button badge to take home — the perfect keepsake from your Malaysian adventure.

Photo credit: Farm in The City

Why Tourists Love Farm in The City

For international travellers, Farm in The City offers something truly special — the chance to interact closely with wildlife while also experiencing the warmth and authenticity of Malaysian village life.

Photo credit: Farm in The City

Here’s why it’s a must-visit:

  • Authenticity: A rare blend of tropical wildlife encounters and kampung charm.

  • Accessibility: Located between Kuala Lumpur and KLIA — just 30 minutes from the city and about 40 minutes from the airport, making it perfect for a day trip or layover.

  • Cultural Connection: Workshops like batik painting offer a taste of local heritage.

  • Ease of Visit: Wheelchair and stroller-friendly, with English-speaking staff.

  • Great for Content Creators: Picture-perfect spots at every turn.

Photo credit: Farm in The City

Plan Your Visit

📍 Location: Seri Kembangan, Selangor (Between Kuala Lumpur and KLIA)
🚉 Nearest MRT: Putra Permai Station (short ride from the zoo)
⏰ Opening Hours: Daily, 10:00am – 6:00pm (Closed on Tuesdays)
🎟️ Tickets: Book online at www.farminthecity.my or via OTA partners
💳 Payment: Cash, card, and QR code accepted
🅿️ Parking: Free limited on-site parking
📲 Follow: Instagram @farminthecitymalaysia | TikTok @farminthecity

items.title: DRIVING IN MALAYSIA: 10 TIPS FOR TOURISTS
items.content:
Photo credit: Hertz Malaysia

Malaysia is a beautiful and diverse country, offering stunning landscapes, vibrant cities, and a rich cultural heritage.

The best way to fully experience its beauty is by driving in Malaysia, as it provides the flexibility to explore both popular destinations and hidden gems at your own pace.

For tourists planning to drive in Malaysia, this guide provides key insights, friendly advice, and practical tips to ensure a smooth and enjoyable driving experience.

1. Driving Laws in Malaysia

Malaysia is a welcoming country for tourists, and driving in Malaysia is straightforward if you follow the rules.

  • Left-hand driving: Like the UK and other Commonwealth nations, Malaysians drive on the left side of the road, and the steering wheel is on the right side of the car. If you're unfamiliar with this setup, don’t worry—you’ll get the hang of it in no time!

  • Speed limits: Speed limits are clearly marked. On highways, you can drive up to 110 km/h, on main roads up to 90 km/h, and within city limits around 60 km/h.

  • Seatbelt laws: To ensure everyone’s safety, wearing seatbelts is mandatory for both front-seat and back-seat passengers.

  • Mobile phone usage: To keep roads safe, it’s illegal to use mobile phones while driving unless you use a hands-free device.

Photo credit: Unsplash

2. Licence Requirements for Tourists

Tourists with a valid international driving permit (IDP) or a driver’s licence in English can enjoy driving in Malaysia without any issues.

If you're visiting from an ASEAN country, you can simply use your national licence.

This means you can rent a car and explore Malaysia with ease, whether it's a quick drive to Kuala Lumpur’s vibrant markets or a scenic coastal trip in Penang.

3. Road Tax and Car Insurance—All Covered for You

When driving in Malaysia, all vehicles are required to have road tax and car insurance.

Fortunately, when you rent a car from trusted companies like Hertz, both road tax and insurance are included in your rental package.

You won’t have to worry about these details—just pick up the car and start exploring Malaysia’s beautiful landscapes.

Photo credit: Flickr

4. Types of Cars Available in Malaysia

Malaysia offers a wide selection of cars, catering to every kind of traveller.

You’ll find local brands like Proton and Perodua, perfect for city driving in Malaysia, as well as international brands like Toyota, Honda, and BMW for those who want a bit more luxury.

If you’re planning to explore Malaysia’s mountainous regions or go off the beaten path, an SUV would be an excellent choice.

Whether you prefer a compact car for zipping around town or a larger vehicle for a family road trip, Hertz Malaysia offers a variety of well-maintained cars to suit your needs.

5. Flexible Driver Arrangements for Tourists

Driving in Malaysia can sometimes feel daunting, but Malaysia makes it easy.

If you're not comfortable driving or just want to sit back and relax, many rental services, including Hertz, offer chauffeur-driven vehicles.

This allows you to enjoy the journey without worrying about navigation or traffic, making it an ideal option for tourists new to Malaysian roads.

Photo credit: Unsplash

6. Types of Fuel—What You Need to Know

  • RON 95 and RON 97 petrol: Malaysia offers two types of petrol: RON 95 and RON 97. However, RON 95 is subsidised for Malaysian citizens only, so tourists and foreign-registered vehicles will need to use RON 97, which is slightly higher in price but still widely available.

  • EV charging: Malaysia is embracing green energy, and electric vehicles (EVs) are becoming more popular. Tourists driving in Malaysia can easily find EV charging stations at most major shopping malls, hotels, and along highways. Simply use apps like PlugShare or ChargeEV to locate the nearest charging station. Hertz Malaysia even offers EV rentals, making it easier for eco-conscious travellers to get around.

7. Road Conditions—Enjoy a Comfortable Drive

Driving in Malaysia is generally a smooth experience, thanks to the well-maintained road network.

The country’s North-South Expressway (PLUS) is the main highway running through Peninsular Malaysia, offering travellers an easy way to journey between key destinations.

Even rural roads are accessible, although they can be narrower, so cautious driving is recommended when exploring more remote areas.

You’ll also find plenty of rest stops along the highways, equipped with food courts, petrol stations, and shops—perfect for taking a break during longer drives.

Photo credit: Unsplash

8. Friendly Driving Etiquette

Malaysians are known for being warm and courteous, and this extends to their driving as well.

  • Flashing headlights: If someone flashes their headlights at you while driving in Malaysia, it usually means "I’m coming through" rather than "go ahead." Keep an eye out for this common signal, especially on highways.

  • Using indicators: While most drivers use their indicators, you might occasionally encounter someone who doesn’t. It’s always a good idea to stay alert and give other drivers some space.

  • Polite gestures: You might see drivers give a friendly wave to thank others for letting them into a lane. It’s always nice to reciprocate the courtesy!

9. Types of Roads and How Tolls Work

Malaysia has an extensive road network, including modern highways, scenic coastal roads, and rural routes. Toll highways are common, especially for long-distance travel. Here’s what you need to know:

  • Touch ‘n Go card: This is the most common way to pay for tolls when driving in Malaysia. You can purchase and reload the card at petrol stations, convenience stores, or at the toll booths themselves. Tolls vary, typically ranging from RM1 to RM50 depending on the distance you travel.

  • Highways: Malaysia’s highways, like the North-South Expressway, are some of the best in Southeast Asia, offering smooth, well-signposted routes.

Photo credit: Loncar Lyon Jenkins

10. Unwritten Driving Customs in Malaysia

Like any country, Malaysia has its own set of unwritten rules that make driving in Malaysia a unique experience.

  • Motorcycles: Be cautious of motorcycles, especially in urban areas. They often weave between cars in traffic and can appear unexpectedly, so always check your blind spots.

  • Tailgating: You might notice some drivers following closely behind you, especially on highways. It’s a common habit, but it’s still best to maintain a safe distance between vehicles.

  • Stopping at zebra crossings: While it’s the law to stop for pedestrians at zebra crossings, not every driver strictly follows this rule. It’s a good idea to be extra cautious at these crossings.

Why Renting a Car from Hertz is Your Best Bet

If you're planning to explore Malaysia by car, Hertz is an excellent choice for car rentals. Here’s why:

  • No worries about maintenance: Hertz offers well-maintained vehicles, so you won’t need to worry about mechanical issues while driving in Malaysia.

  • Insurance included: With Hertz, comprehensive insurance is included in your rental package, giving you peace of mind throughout your journey.

  • Flexible car options: Hertz offers everything from compact city cars to larger SUVs, making it easy to choose the perfect vehicle for your trip while driving in Malaysia.

Photo credit: Hertz Malaysia

Final Thoughts: Drive and Explore Malaysia with Confidence

Driving in Malaysia is a wonderful way to see everything the country has to offer.

With well-maintained roads, friendly locals, and a reliable car rental service like Hertz at https://www.hertzmalaysia.com/en/, you’ll have everything you need for an unforgettable road trip.

Just remember to follow the rules of the road, enjoy the scenic views, and take in the warm hospitality that Malaysia is known for. Safe travels!

items.title: KELANA JAYA LRT SERVICE ADJUSTMENTS: WHAT TO EXPECT AND WHY IT MATTERS
items.content:
Photo credit: Lowyat

Prasarana Malaysia has announced phased service adjustments on the Kelana Jaya LRT line from August 9 to November 22, as it upgrades its signalling system to SelTrac Generation 8.

Here's a polished breakdown of what to expect and why it's ultimately a move worth your patience.

What’s Going On?

Between August 9 and September 14 (Phase 2), 10 stations from KLCC to Gombak will launch service at 9:00 a.m. instead of the usual 6:00 a.m. on weekends and public holidays.

Phase 3, from October 11 to November 22, will affect 17 stations from Lembah Subang to Ampang Park, with similar later openings.

Why the Delay?

The Kelana Jaya line has been operating on a legacy automatic train control (ATC) system since 1998.

Prasarana is upgrading both software and hardware to the SelTrac Gen 8 system, incorporating real‑time data analytics, cybersecurity enhancements, and improved train scheduling.

The upgrade is expected to add another two decades of reliable service and significantly reduce future disruptions.

Photo credit: KLIA

Scope & Impact

  • Phase 2 affects 10 stations: KLCC, Ampang Park, Damai, Dato’ Keramat, Jelatek (Aug) and Setiawangsa, Sri Rampai, Wangsa Maju, Taman Melati, Gombak (Sept).

  • Phase 3 includes 17 stations: Such as KL Sentral, Pasar Seni, Masjid Jamek, Dang Wangi, Kampung Baru, and others.

  • An estimated 7,000 passengers were affected during Phase 2, rising to about 20,000 during Phase 3.

Stations not in the upgrade zone will continue operating as usual.

Photo credit: Carz Automedia Malaysia

What Prasarana Is Doing to Help

To ease commuter inconvenience:

  • Free shuttle trains will operate between Pasar Seni and Kampung Baru at 10–20-minute intervals.

  • Bus Route 2 stops at all affected stations between Dang Wangi and Gombak.

  • Bus Route 3 offers a limited-stop option for quicker travel.

  • Intermediate vans operate nonstop from 6 a.m. to 9 a.m. between Kampung Baru and KLCC, no booking needed.

On-site support includes station staff, auxiliary police, and Prasarana Troopers to assist with transfers and queries.

Timeline & Key Dates

Phase

Check official channels for precise weekends and dates.

Photo credit: Newswav

Why It Matters

  • Enhances long-term reliability and reduces the frequency of breakdowns.

  • Improves passenger safety, system security, and future scalability.

  • Avoids larger, more disruptive failures in future years.

What You Can Do

  • Visit myrapid.com.my or monitor Rapid KL's social media for updates and detailed schedules.

  • Plan ahead if travelling on affected weekends. Arrive early, explore shuttle routes.

  • Ask station staff or look for signage if unsure. They’re there to guide your journey.

Photo credit: Tunnel time

In Summary

These weekend and public holiday service adjustments are a temporary inconvenience for long-term enhancement.

This strategic move not only modernises the Kelana Jaya line but it ensures that Malaysia’s busiest LRT system remains safe, efficient, and future-ready for years to come.

items.title: A TEMPORARY FIX OR TURNING POINT? MALAYSIA’S COST-OF-LIVING CRISIS HITS CENTRE STAGE
items.content:
Photo credit: Malay Mail

A Nation at the Tipping Point

Malaysia stands at a crossroads.

In the thick of economic stress, where prices pinch and paycheques stretch thin, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s latest announcement comes not just as a response, but as a test: is this a genuine pivot, or a pause button on deeper unrest?

On 23 July 2025, Anwar addressed the nation with a series of relief measures aimed at cushioning the rakyat from the escalating cost-of-living crisis.

Timely, yes. But is it timely enough?

Photo credit: Asia News Network

RM100 Handouts: Symbol or Solution?

The headline measure: a one-off RM100 cash aid to all Malaysians aged 18 and above under the Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) programme.

It’s easy to dismiss RM100 as a drop in the ocean, but for many, it’s the difference between choice and compromise.

Highlights:

  • Eligibility: All Malaysians 18+

  • Amount: RM100 per person

  • Redemption period: 31 August to 31 December 2025

  • Outlets: 4,000+ across the country

  • Unused funds: Reallocated to low-income households in 2026

Photo credit: Pexel


Petrol Relief & Toll Freeze: Easing the Everyday

Two of the most visible wins for Malaysians came in the form of fuel and toll relief:

  • RON95 fuel price cut to RM1.99/litre (from RM2.05)

  • Foreign drivers to pay market rate, protecting subsidies

  • Toll hike suspensions across 10 major highways

  • No burden to drivers. Concessionaires to be compensated

For daily commuters and weekend hometown goers alike, these changes bring tangible breathing room.

Photo credit: Pexel

Rahmah Sales and a Surprise Holiday

  • Rahmah Sales funding doubled: From RM300M to RM600M

  • One sale per district minimum. Focused on essentials

  • New public holiday on 15 September, ahead of Malaysia Day

This blend of relief and morale-boosting speaks to a government trying to reach both the wallet and the heart.

Photo credit: Wikimedia

The Cost Behind the Care

Total aid under the Madani government now climbs from RM13 billion to RM15 billion this year.

But with Malaysia’s public debt at 76.5% of GDP, and a deficit target of 3% by 2028, critics warn: these are not waters we can paddle in for long.

Subsidy rationalisation and targeted tax reforms are expected by September 2025, and how they unfold may determine whether this aid is a short-term sedative or a long-term strategy.

Photo credit: Pexel

The Pulse on the Ground

This announcement came on the eve of a large-scale protest in Kuala Lumpur.

Tens of thousands are prepared to demand action on living costs.

Anwar’s address defused tensions but didn’t erase them. The rakyat is awake, alert, and asking: “What comes next?”

Cabinet members praised the move as proactive and compassionate.

Fahmi Fadzil, the Communications Minister, remarked:

“It shows the Prime Minister’s empathy and attentiveness to people’s concerns.”

Still, empathy without reform risks becoming performance.

That’s the tightrope Anwar now walks.

Photo credit: Harian Metro

What Happens After the Applause?

Key upcoming dates to watch:

  • 31 July: Launch of the 13th Malaysia Plan

  • By September: Fuel subsidy and tax reform blueprint

  • October: Budget 2026 revealed

Each step carries the weight of expectation.

Malaysians don’t just want relief, they want reassurance, reform, and results.

Photo credit: Wikimedia

A Temporary Fix or Turning Point?

The true test of leadership isn’t in how you respond to pressure but in how you follow through when the applause fades.

This relief package is welcome.

It’s needed. But if left as-is, it risks being just that: a temporary fix.

What Malaysia needs next is a turning point.

The rakyat doesn’t expect magic, but they do expect motion.

The next few months will reveal whether this government chooses courage over convenience, structure over sentiment, and, above all, sustainable action over short-term applause.

items.title: PD OSTRICH SHOW FARM: A MUST-VISIT GEM IN PORT DICKSON FOR ANIMAL LOVERS, THRILL SEEKERS & HERITAGE BUFFS
items.content:
Photo credit: PD Ostrich Farm

When in Port Dickson, don’t just hit the beach and call it a day. 

Just a few minutes inland from Teluk Kemang lies a truly unforgettable stop: the PD Ostrich Show Farm. 

A place where wild meets whimsical, and nature meets nostalgia.

Endorsed by Tourism Malaysia, Lembaga Pelancongan Negeri Sembilan, and MPPD, this family-run farm is more than just an animal park; it is an experiential wonderland bursting with quirky characters, photo-worthy moments, and heartwarming community values.

Race an Ostrich? Meet Kuntum, Your Feathered Rival!

Racing against people is a normal occurrence, but how about racing an ostrich?

Meet Kuntum, the PD Ostrich Show Farm’s pride and speed. 

This long-legged superstar is not just any bird; he is Malaysia’s only ostrich you can actually challenge in a race. 

Set foot on the farm’s sandy track and try to outpace him! 

Spoiler alert: You will probably lose, but to experience racing against an ostrich is priceless.

This one-of-a-kind activity is what truly sets PD Ostrich Show Farm apart, as no other farm in Malaysia offers this heart-pounding, feather-flying experience.

Photo credit: PD Ostrich Farm

Say Hello to Puteri, The Poser of the Poultry World

Forget influencers. 

Puteri the Ostrich is the queen of the camera. 

Elegant, poised, and ridiculously photogenic, Puteri knows her angles better than a fashion model. 

She’s trained, or maybe just naturally gifted, to strike a pose whenever you whip out your phone.

And yes, she always steals the spotlight.

Whether you’re a family on vacation, a couple on a quirky date, or a solo traveller collecting moments, Puteri makes sure your memories are picture-perfect.

Photo credit: PD Ostrich Farm

Beyond the Ostriches: What Makes This Farm So Special?

This is not just a show farm; it is a multi-sensory playground of nature, culture, and conscious living.

1. Herbal Oasis & ESG Goodness

Since 2024, PD Ostrich Show Farm has gone all-in on eco-conscious practices, from kenaf planting to bio-composting kitchen waste. 

There is even a Herbal Oasis showcasing traditional herbal remedies, local produce, and immersive cooking classes in collaboration with SEKUNTUM, their community tourism arm.

2. Pets, Paws & Planet Jurassic

Snuggle up to guinea pigs, rabbits, meerkats, goats, and even African soft fur animals. 

Explore the Cat Café, journey through Planet Jurassic, stroll in the Bamboo Garden, or go on a Night Farm Safari that feels like stepping into a magical animal kingdom.

3. Crocodile ‘Hunt’ & Farm Safari Train

Fancy something a little wilder? 

Book their river cruise, crocodile watch at a nearby sanctuary or hop on a farm train safari through lush greenery. 

The kids and the adults will love it.

4. Hutan Misteri

Feeling the heat? Step into the cool, curious world of Hutan Misteri, an indoor, glow-in-the-dark jungle where mystery meets modern magic.
Designed for the IG and TikTok generation, this 3D immersive experience is made to be explored, snapped, and shared.

5. SEKUNTUM

This is where you will feel Malaysia; soak in its spirit and, most deliciously, taste it.
At SEKUNTUM, dive into tradition: play classic games, relive timeless pastimes, and cook beloved dishes like nasi lemak, roti canai, steamed cassava, lempeng, and more.
But culture here isn’t all joy and snacks. It has a darker side too.
Dare to drive through Perkampungan Puaka, the Haunted Village where ghostly folklore comes alive.

Photo credit: PD Ostrich Farm

Taste the Wild Side: Ostrich Satay, Egg Dishes & Herbal Cuisine

You have not truly experienced the farm until you have tasted it. 

Yes, ostrich satay is on the menu; tender, lean, and high in protein. 

You will also find ostrich egg dishes, local Malay food, and herbal cuisine that brings tradition and wellness to your plate.

For Families, Schools, & Even Weddings!

This isn’t just a day-trip stop; it is a venue for team building, educational tours, family days, and even weddings.

With wheelchair-friendly facilities, kids' amusement zones, rest areas, and plenty of parking, it is designed to welcome everyone, young or old, able-bodied or mobility-challenged.

Photo credit: PD Ostrich Farm

Getting There

PD Ostrich Show Farm is just:

  • 3–15 mins from beaches like Teluk Kemang, Blue Lagoon & Pantai Cermin

  • 8–30 mins from 5-star hotels like Lexis Hibiscus, Avillion & Thistle

  • 3–30 mins from attractions like Marine Fish Centre & the PD Lighthouse

Address: Lot 1419, Jalan Kemang 13, Batu 9, Teluk Kemang, 71050 Port Dickson
Telephone: 018-207 8286
Email: pdostrichfarm@yahoo.com
Website: www.pdostrich.com
FB/IG: @pdostrich2011

Photo credit: PD Ostrich Farm

Why PD Ostrich Show Farm is a KL The Guide Top Pick

From Kuntum’s thunderous dash to Puteri’s red carpet strut, this charming farm is Port Dickson’s most delightful detour. 

It is educational, entertaining, and evolving, as well as rooted in local heritage while embracing a sustainable future.

So next time you are in PD, skip the usual tourist traps. Instead, race a bird, hug a goat, and let a posing ostrich upgrade your selfie game.

You will gain more than just photos. You will experience stories, laughs, and a reminder that sometimes, the best memories are made where you least expect them.

items.title: TEMASYA TARI MELAYU: TRADITION REIMAGINED AT PST2025 – CATCH IT ON 25 & 26 JULY!
items.content:
Photo credit: JKKN

Step into the rhythm of history this July with a performance that’s equal parts grace, heritage, and soul.

As part of the vibrant Panggung Seni Tradisional 2025 (PST2025) lineup, Temasya Tari Melayu: Lama Dalam Baharu is a must-see celebration of traditional Malay dance, reimagined for the present while honouring the past.

Mark your calendars for 25 and 26 July 2025 at 8:30 PM, as the stage at the Tunku Abdul Rahman Hall, Malaysia Tourism Centre (MaTiC), Kuala Lumpur, comes alive with an unforgettable journey through Malaysia’s rich dance heritage.

What is Panggung Seni Tradisional (PST2025)?

Since 2013, this annual cultural extravaganza has brought together the best of Malaysia’s traditional performing arts, from stirring ghazals and Chinese opera to classical Indian dance and Malay folk theatre.

Organised by the National Department of Culture and Arts (JKKN), PST2025 isn’t just a stage for performance, it’s a living cultural classroom, a creative lab, and a nationwide invitation to reconnect with Malaysia’s artistic soul.

Photo credit: JKKN

And this year, PST2025 is pulling out all the stops with five spectacular performances:

  • Irama Ghazal Johor by Ghazal Johor Network (23 & 24 May)

  • Irama Lingnan – Cantonese Chinese Opera by Pat Woh Association (28 & 29 June)

  • Temasya Tari Melayu: Lama Dalam Baharu by University of Malaya Arts Group (25 & 26 July)

  • Parampara – Indian Classical Dance by Angika Fine Arts (6 & 7 September)

  • Kembara Putera – Jikey Langkawi Theatre by Kedah Creative Artists Association (26 & 27 September)

Photo credit: JKKN

Spotlight on Temasya Tari Melayu: Lama Dalam Baharu

This isn’t just a performance, it’s a cultural awakening.

Temasya Tari Melayu: Lama Dalam Baharu, translated as "Malay Dance Festival: The Old in the New," is a masterful dance showcase that revives the beauty of classical and folk Malay dance through a contemporary lens.

It merges authentic tradition with innovative presentation, offering a performance that speaks to both the old soul and the curious newcomer.

Two Acts, One Cultural Heartbeat

Act I: Tari Klasik Melayu (Classic Malay Dance)

Reverent and refined, this segment showcases the regal elegance of traditional dance forms, including the Malay Gamelan repertoire and the rarely performed Terinai Perlis.

Once performed in royal courts and ancient ceremonies, these dances are given new breath and grace under the stage lights.

Act II: Tari Rakyat Melayu (Folk Malay Dance)

Lively, joyful, and deeply rooted in community, this act features folk dances originally developed in the 1970s at the Kompleks Budaya Negara.

Expect expressive movements, vibrant costumes, and rhythms that tell the everyday stories of the Malay people.

Photo credit: JKKN

Why You Should Catch This Performance

  • Rare Cultural Showcase – Many of the dances featured are vanishing art forms.

  • Part of PST2025 – One of five major cultural events celebrating Malaysia’s artistic identity.

  • Educational and Entertaining – A beautiful balance of performance and preservation.

  • For Everyone – From culture buffs to curious newcomers, there’s something here for all.

Photo credit: JKKN

Event Details – Temasya Tari Melayu: Lama Dalam Baharu

Dates: 25 & 26 July 2025
Time: 8:30 PM
Venue: Tunku Abdul Rahman Hall, Malaysia Tourism Centre (MaTiC), Kuala Lumpur
Ticket Prices:

  • VIP: RM55

  • Regular: RM40

  • Student: RM30

For reservations or more info:
Contact Khairi at 019-6101157 or AS at 014-2631344

Photo credit: JKKN

Final Thoughts: Where the Past Dances Into the Future

In a world spinning ever faster, Temasya Tari Melayu: Lama Dalam Baharu reminds us to pause, listen, and honour the rhythms that have carried our culture through centuries.

It’s more than a show, it’s a graceful, glowing ember of our collective heritage, passed into new hands with care and creativity.

So, this July, let tradition move you. Let the music guide you. And let the soul of Malay dance leave you breathless.

items.title: MY50 MONTHLY TRAVEL PASS NOW AVAILABLE DIGITALLY VIA TOUCH 'N GO E-WALLET
items.content:
Photo credit: SYOK
In a significant step toward digitalising Malaysia’s public transport ecosystem, Rapid KL’s popular My50 Monthly Travel Pass can now be activated and renewed digitally via the Touch ‘n Go (TNG) eWallet app.
This marks a major milestone in the country’s ongoing effort to streamline commuter experiences through digital innovation.

The digital option officially launched today and is now accessible to Malaysian citizens who own the Enhanced Touch ‘n Go NFC card and use NFC-enabled smartphones.

Photo credit: RinggitPlus

A Seamless Commuter Experience

Previously, My50 users were required to visit physical service counters to purchase or renew their passes, often resulting in long queues and time-consuming processes.

The new digital method eliminates this inconvenience by allowing users to complete the entire process through their mobile devices.

How it works:

  1. Download or update the Touch ‘n Go eWallet app.

  2. Complete the eKYC (electronic Know-Your-Customer) verification process.

  3. Link your Enhanced TNG card (equipped with NFC capability).

  4. Navigate to the “My50 Travel Pass” feature and choose your activation date.

  5. Make the payment and tap your card to your phone to write the pass into the card.

Once the process is complete, the card is immediately ready to be used across Rapid KL’s network of buses, MRT, LRT, monorail, and BRT lines.

Photo credit: SoyaCincau

Who Is Eligible?

This service is currently available to Malaysian citizens only, in line with the My50 pass’s original eligibility requirements.

To prevent misuse or duplication, the system restricts the issuance of only one My50 pass per user through the eWallet, linked to a verified identity via eKYC.

Users must also ensure they possess the Enhanced Touch ‘n Go card, which supports NFC functionality.

Standard TNG cards and MyKad-based passes remain incompatible with this digital renewal method and must still be managed at physical locations.

A Step Toward Digital Mobility

Transport Minister Anthony Loke stated that the digitalisation of the My50 pass is part of a broader vision to modernise Malaysia’s public transport infrastructure.

"This is an important move to encourage the use of public transport through improved convenience and efficiency," he said during the launch event.

He also added that similar digital integration is planned for other travel products such as the MyCity pass and MyTourist pass, both expected to be rolled out by the end of the year.

Photo credit: Carz Automedia Malaysia

Public Reception and Future Outlook

The update has been well-received by the public, with many commuters praising the ease of use and the elimination of long queues.

However, some concerns have been raised regarding card sharing, as the enhanced cards can still be passed between users, potentially circumventing the single-user restriction.

Despite this, the digital rollout is seen as a progressive move, especially as the government explores long-term mobility solutions such as cardless fare systems, QR code ticketing, and integrated Mobility-as-a-Service (MaaS) platforms.

The digitisation of the My50 Monthly Travel Pass represents more than just a convenience upgrade; it is a symbol of Malaysia’s commitment to transforming public transport into a user-friendly, accessible, and future-ready system.

As digital adoption continues to expand across sectors, this move brings the nation one step closer to a fully integrated, smart mobility ecosystem.

For daily commuters across the Klang Valley, the ability to renew and activate their travel pass anytime, anywhere is not only practical, it’s empowering.

items.title: ALL ABOARD: KLIA AEROTRAIN SET TO RESUME SERVICE THIS JULY 1
items.content:
Photo credit: Astro Awani

Good news for travellers flying through Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA): the long-awaited Aerotrain service is officially returning on July 1, 2025, after over two years of upgrades, testing, and fine-tuning.

If you’ve been navigating KLIA’s shuttle buses and tight transfer windows, rejoice. 

The sleek new people mover is finally ready to roll, bringing back seamless, efficient connectivity between the Main Terminal and Satellite Building A, just in time for Malaysia’s push towards Visit Malaysia Year 2026.

Photo credit: Lowyat.net

What Is the KLIA Aerotrain?

For the uninitiated or long-haul-dazed: the KLIA Aerotrain is an automated airside train that connects the Main Terminal Building (MTB) to Satellite Terminal A, the latter serving most international departures and arrivals.

Since March 2023, the system has been shut down for a full revamp.

Travellers were instead transported via shuttle buses, which, while functional, were never quite the same as zipping silently above the tarmac on dedicated rails.

Photo credit: Straits Times

What’s New?

According to Transport Minister Anthony Loke, the reintroduced service is not just a reboot, it’s a major modernisation. 

Here’s what’s on board:

  • Brand-new trains by global rail giant Alstom, using the Innovia APM 300R platform.

  • Three-car configurations with a 270-passenger capacity per train.

  • Two trains, running during peak hours, with a 3-minute frequency.

  • A single-train operation from midnight to 5AM, ensuring night-time maintenance without total shutdown.

  • Shuttle buses will still be available as backup during the transition phase.

The Aerotrain system has already undergone extensive testing, including emergency response simulations and system stress trials. 

Officials say it’s ready for prime time.

Photo credit: Malay

What Happens on July 1?

Starting at 10AM, the Aerotrain service will once again ferry passengers between the terminals at KLIA. 

The full rollout will continue alongside the existing shuttle buses during the initial re-launch period to ensure operational stability.

This means faster transfers, less crowding, and a cooler way to travel.

Photo credit: NH Online

Why You Should Care

Let’s cut to the chase: whether you’re a casual traveller, a frequent flyer, or an aviation geek, here’s why this matters to you:

1. Save Time

No more waiting for shuttle buses or bracing for last-minute gate changes. 

The Aerotrain slashes transfer time between terminals to under 2.5 minutes.

2. Travel Smarter

Better transit equals less stress, especially during layovers or tight international connections.

3. Malaysia Means Business

With Visit Malaysia Year 2026 around the corner and Malaysia chairing ASEAN 2025, this upgrade sends a message: we’re ready to welcome the world.

4. Boosting Airport Cred

KLIA’s global ranking took a hit after repeated Aerotrain breakdowns in recent years. 

A successful relaunch helps restore confidence for travellers, airlines, and investors alike.

5. Modern & Sustainable

The new system is driverless, efficient, and eco-conscious, representing a step forward in smart airport infrastructure.

Photo credit: Soya cincau

What’s Next?

KLIA is positioning itself as a regional aviation hub, and the Aerotrain is just one piece of a larger puzzle. 

With digital boarding, biometric security trials, and terminal upgrades on the horizon, KLIA is clearly gearing up for a future-ready transformation.

Final Boarding Call

The return of the KLIA Aerotrain marks more than just the end of a construction period; it signals a fresh chapter in Malaysia’s airport experience. 

Whether you’re flying in, out, or through, this streamlined, stress-free transit option is one upgrade you’ll feel the moment your feet hit the platform.

So if you’re flying through KLIA after July 1, keep an eye out. The Aerotrain is back, and it’s better, faster, and finally on track.

There’s something undeniably therapeutic about a road trip—the wind in your hair, the open road stretching ahead, and the freedom to explore at your own pace.

Why Malaysian Road Trips Heal the Soul

Malaysia’s diverse terrain makes it a paradise for road trippers.

1. Cameron Highlands – A Cool Escape

Winding roads through emerald tea plantations, strawberry farms, and crisp mountain air—Cameron Highlands is the perfect antidote to city fatigue.

2. East Coast Peninsula, Malaysia – Beaches & Serenity

The drive along Malaysia’s East Coast, stretching from Terengganu to Kelantan, is a journey through serene landscapes and cultural richness.

Pristine beaches line the coastline, dotted with charming fishing villages where time seems to slow down.

Along the way, you'll encounter some of the country’s finest seafood, fresh from the boat to your plate.

Stop by Cherating for its golden sands and laid-back surf culture, or venture farther to Perhentian Island, where turquoise waters and untouched coral reefs offer a slice of paradise that feels worlds away.

Photo credit: AVIS Car Rental

It’s a beloved Malaysian food trail on wheels.

For those exploring East Malaysia by car, this is an unforgettable experience.

items.title: 15 HIDDEN GEMS IN MALAYSIA TO EXPLORE BY CAR – YOUR ULTIMATE ROAD TRIP WITH HERTZ AWAITS!
items.content:
Photo credit: Unsplash

 

There’s nothing quite like the open road calling your name, a playlist queued up, and a reliable ride from Hertz Malaysia waiting to whisk you away.

If you're craving adventure beyond the usual tourist trails, buckle up — these hidden gems in Malaysia are the perfect reason to hit the highway.

Whether you're dreaming of misty mountains, secret beaches, or serene kampung life, your next epic escape starts with the right car rental in Malaysia.

With Hertz, exploring Malaysia’s lesser-known marvels is not just easy — it’s extraordinary.

Let’s rev up your wanderlust. Here are 15 unforgettable hidden gems in Malaysia you can explore on your next road trip:


Photo Credit: Hertz


1. Balik Pulau, Penang – For Durians and Sunsets

Trade Georgetown’s bustle for the peaceful vibes of Balik Pulau.

This countryside haven is perfect for scenic drives past paddy fields, village life, and mouth-watering durians.

Bonus: it’s a short hop to the beaches of Batu Feringghi for that golden-hour glow.

🚗 Distance from Kuala Lumpur: 350 km (~4 hours)
🛣️ Toll: RM45 (one way)
💸 Fuel: RM46–60
🕐 Best time: Nov–Feb


2. Pulau Pangkor, Perak – The Laid-Back Island Life

Drive to Lumut, park your Hertz car, and ferry off to this tranquil tropical island.

Before that, stretch your legs at Teluk Batik — a gorgeous, underrated mainland beach.

🚗 250 km (~3.5 hours)

🛣️ RM28 toll

💸 RM33–42 fuel

🕐 Best time: Feb–Oct



3. Belum Rainforest, Perak – The Ancient Wilderness

Feel the call of the wild at Belum-Temenggor, one of the oldest rainforests on Earth.

It’s a sanctuary for wildlife, waterfalls, and eco-adventures.

🚗 300 km (~4 hours)

🛣️ RM35 toll

💸 RM39–51 fuel

🕐 Best time: Feb–Oct


4. Gua Tempurung, Perak – Into the Depths

Love caves and a bit of thrill? Explore Malaysia’s largest limestone cave, followed by a food-fueled detour to Ipoh’s heritage streets.

🚗 160 km (~2 hours)

🛣️ RM20 toll

💸 RM21–27 fuel

🕐 Best time: Mar–Nov


5. Kuala Sepetang, Perak – Fireflies & Fishermen

Savour seafood fresh off the boat, visit charcoal kilns, and witness magical firefly tours at night. A peaceful coastal gem that’s full of charm.

🚗 250 km (~3 hours)

🛣️ RM28 toll

💸 RM33–42 fuel

🕐 Best time: Feb–Oct


Photo credit: Unsplash


6. Bukit Tinggi, Pahang – Bonjour, Malaysia!

A French village in the hills? Oui! Stroll cobblestone streets, visit the Japanese garden, and soak in the cool mountain air.

🚗 50 km (~1 hour)

🛣️ RM6 toll

💸 RM7–9 fuel

🕐 Best time: Mar–Aug


7. Janda Baik, Pahang – A Forest Retreat

Hidden in the highlands, this peaceful village offers riverside stays, hiking trails, and an escape into nature, just a short drive from Kuala Lumpur.

🚗 45 km (~1 hour)

🛣️ RM5 toll

💸 RM6–8 fuel

🕐 Best time: Mar–Aug



8. Fraser’s Hill, Pahang – Colonial Cool

Birdwatching, British cottages, and misty trails — Fraser’s Hill is a slice of old-school charm. Great for a quiet weekend getaway.

🚗 100 km (~2 hours)

🛣️ No toll

💸 RM13–17 fuel

🕐 Best time: Mar–Sep


9. Tasik Kenyir, Terengganu – Into the Blue

Malaysia’s largest man-made lake is a hidden aquatic paradise for kayaking, fishing, and jungle trekking.

🚗 450 km (~6 hours)

🛣️ RM45 toll

💸 RM58–73 fuel

🕐 Best time: Mar–Sep


Photo credit: Unsplash

10. Pantai Irama, Kelantan – Melodies of the Sea

Its name means “Melody Beach,” and true to form, this serene spot near Bachok hums with peace and gentle waves.

🚗 400 km (~6 hours)

🛣️ RM35 toll

💸 RM52–66 fuel

🕐 Best time: Feb–Oct


11. Kuala Selangor, Selangor – A Glow in the Dark

One of the easiest day trips from Kuala Lumpur is to a place famous for fireflies, seafood, and sunset views over the estuary.

🚗 65 km (~1 hour)

🛣️ RM5 toll

💸 RM8–10 fuel

🕐 Best time: Mar–Oct


12. Sekinchan, Selangor – Where Green Meets the Sea

A photogenic patchwork of paddy fields meets a coastal breeze. Don’t miss the seafood or the paddy museum.

🚗 100 km (~1.5 hours)

🛣️ RM5 toll

💸 RM13–17 fuel

🕐 Best time: Mar–Sep


Photo credit: Pexels


13. Sasaran Sky Mirror, Selangor – A Natural Illusion

Catch this magic only during low tide when the seabed becomes a mirror to the sky. It’s surreal, dreamy, and Instagram gold.

🚗 70 km (~1.5 hours)

🛣️ RM6 toll

💸 RM9–12 fuel

🕐 Best time: Mar–Oct


14. Batu Feringghi, Penang – Buzzing Beach Bliss

Vibrant night markets, beach activities, and fresh seafood galore. Pair this with a visit to the hidden nooks of Georgetown for a full island experience.

🚗 360 km (~4.5 hours)

🛣️ RM45 toll

💸 RM48–63 fuel

🕐 Best time: Nov–Feb


15. Tanjung Sepat, Selangor – Seafood by the Sea

Coffee, seafood, and small-town vibes. Explore the boardwalk, visit a mushroom farm, and wrap up your day at Morib Beach nearby.

🚗 100 km (~1.5 hours)

🛣️ No toll

💸 RM13–17 fuel

🕐 Best time: Feb–Oct



Photo Credit: Hertz


Why Choose Hertz Malaysia for Your Road Trip?

When it comes to car rental in Malaysia, Hertz leads the way with comfort, convenience, and reliable vehicles perfect for every kind of adventure — from solo escapes to family road trips.

Whether you're cruising through Kuala Lumpur or venturing deep into rainforest reserves, Hertz Malaysia ensures a smooth ride with:

  • Wide range of vehicles (sedans, SUVs, MPVs & more)

  • Convenient locations across Malaysia, including major airports

  • Easy online booking at hertzmalaysia.com

  • Trusted international service with local expertise

Quick Tips Before You Go:

  • Top up your Touch ‘n Go card for tolls.

  • Dry season (Feb–Sep) is prime time for exploring.

  • Don’t forget a good playlist — road trips are 80% music, 20% snacks.

Start your engine, grab your keys, and let Hertz Malaysia take you on a journey beyond the map. There’s a whole world of hidden gems out there — and they’re just a drive away.

Nestled in the upscale neighbourhood of Mont Kiara, Kuala Lumpur, Global Doctors Hospital (GDH) shines as a leading beacon of patient-centred healthcare.

Strategically located to serve the diverse communities of Mont Kiara, Hartamas, and Bukit Damansara, this esteemed medical facility is known for delivering comprehensive, world-class care with a personal touch.

Whether you're a resident, an expatriate, or a traveller in need of quality healthcare in Kuala Lumpur, GDH offers trusted expertise across the medical spectrum.


Photo Credit: Global Doctors Hospital

Comprehensive Medical Services Under One Roof

Global Doctors Hospital provides a full suite of medical services, making it a one-stop destination for both primary care and specialised treatments.

Patients benefit from a seamless experience, supported by a team of experienced professionals and cutting-edge medical technology. Key services include:

  • Specialist Consultations: Connect with top-tier specialists across more than 20 medical disciplines, including cardiology, orthopaedics, paediatrics, and internal medicine.

  • Diagnostic Services: Accurate diagnoses begin with advanced tools—MRI, CT scans, ultrasounds, and laboratory testing are all available onsite.

  • Minimally Invasive Surgeries: Benefit from the latest surgical techniques that minimise discomfort, reduce hospital stays, and accelerate recovery.

  • Emergency Medical Services: GDH operates 24/7 to address urgent healthcare needs promptly, ensuring peace of mind at any hour.

  • Rehabilitation Services: Customised physiotherapy and rehabilitation programs are designed to support patients through recovery and help them regain strength post-treatment.

  • Dental and Aesthetic Services: From routine cleanings to cosmetic enhancements, GDH provides comprehensive oral and aesthetic care in a comfortable environment.

Additionally, GDH champions preventive medicine, offering extensive health screening packages that promote early detection and long-term wellness, an essential service for busy professionals and families alike in Kuala Lumpur.



Photo Credit: Global Doctors Hospital


A Human-Centred Healthcare Experience

At Global Doctors Hospital, healthcare goes beyond treatment—it's about building relationships, understanding individual needs, and providing tailored care.

The hospital’s multidisciplinary approach ensures that each patient receives a personalised treatment plan crafted with compassion and clinical excellence.

GDH adheres to international healthcare standards and continuously evolves to enhance patient experience through innovative care models and quality improvements.



Photo Credit: Global Doctors Hospital


Convenient and Accessible Healthcare in Kuala Lumpur

Recognising the demands of urban life, GDH extends its outpatient clinic hours to accommodate a wide range of schedules:

  • Monday – Friday: 8:00 AM – 9:00 PM

  • Saturday: 8:00 AM – 6:00 PM

  • Sunday & Public Holidays: Closed

Meanwhile, its 24-hour medical clinic ensures that emergency care is always within reach—yet another reason GDH stands out in the landscape of private hospitals in Kuala Lumpur.


Photo Credit: Global Doctors Hospital


Malaysia: A Global Leader in Medical Tourism

Malaysia has been recognised as the top destination for medical tourism by Nomad Capitalist, thanks to its combination of high-quality healthcare services and affordability.

The country's modern medical facilities, many of which are internationally accredited, offer treatments ranging from routine check-ups to complex surgeries at a fraction of the cost compared to Western countries.

English-speaking medical professionals and a well-developed infrastructure further enhance the appeal for international patients seeking care in Malaysia.

In 2019, Malaysia attracted over 1.2 million medical tourists, generating more than $500 million in revenue.

The Malaysia Healthcare Travel Council (MHTC) anticipates these numbers to rise, projecting revenues to surpass RM2.4 billion (approximately US$558 million) by 2024.

This growth underscores Malaysia's commitment to providing exceptional healthcare services to both domestic and international patients



Photo Credit: Global Doctors Hospital


A Hub for Medical Tourism in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia

Kuala Lumpur has rapidly emerged as a global destination for medical tourism, attracting thousands of international patients seeking high-quality, affordable healthcare.

Global Doctors Hospital plays a significant role in this growing sector, offering treatments that combine Western medical standards with Malaysian hospitality.

With English-speaking staff, transparent pricing, and international patient services, GDH is an ideal choice for those travelling to Malaysia for medical care, whether it’s for surgery, chronic disease management, or wellness check-ups.

The hospital’s prime location in Mont Kiara, a favourite among expats, adds to its appeal for overseas patients.


Photo Credit: Global Doctors Hospital


Community Commitment and Global Impact

Global Doctors Hospital isn’t just a healthcare provider—it’s a community pillar.

GDH actively engages in public health initiatives, education campaigns, and charitable outreach.

A notable example is its partnership with the United Nations High Commission for Refugees (UNHCR), through which GDH provides vital medical care to refugees living in Malaysia.

This reflects a deep commitment to healthcare equity, social responsibility, and meaningful global impact.


Photo Credit: Global Doctors Hospital


Visit Global Doctors Hospital Today

Whether you're managing a chronic condition, planning a health screening, or seeking urgent care, Global Doctors Hospital in Kuala Lumpur delivers reliable, compassionate, and comprehensive medical services.

Experience a healthcare institution where cutting-edge technology meets heartfelt human care.

📍 Address: No. 18, Jalan Kiara 3, Mont Kiara, 50480 Kuala Lumpur
📞 Phone: +603 2303 9911
🌐 Website: www.globaldoctorshospital.com

Your health journey deserves the best care—choose Global Doctors Hospital, where Kuala Lumpur’s healthcare excellence meets global standards and local warmth.

items.title: PANGGUNG SENI TRADISIONAL 2025: A LIVING TAPESTRY OF MALAYSIA'S CULTURAL SOUL
items.content:
Photo Credit: JKKN


Step aside, Netflix. The real drama, music, and magic are taking centre stage at Panggung Seni Tradisional 2025—affectionately known as PST2025.

This isn’t just a cultural show. PST2025 is a full-blown celebration of Malaysia’s heart and heritage, set to dazzle your senses and stir your soul.

From ghazals to opera, from classical dance to comedic folk theatre, PST2025 is ready to light up the Tunku Abdul Rahman Hall at the Malaysia Tourism Centre (MaTiC), Kuala Lumpur.

And guess what? Everyone’s invited. Whether you’re a lifelong art lover or someone who thinks TikTok is the pinnacle of performance, PST2025 promises something unforgettable.


Photo Credit: JKKN

Why PST2025 Matters

Since its inception in 2013, Panggung Seni Tradisional has grown into a treasured annual program, showcasing the dazzling diversity of Malaysia’s traditional performing arts.

But PST2025 isn't just a series of shows—it's a living classroom, a cultural bridge, and a soulful showcase rolled into one.

Spearheaded by the National Department of Culture and Arts (JKKN), PST2025 reflects their vision to make cultural arts more accessible while enriching the lives of Malaysians.

It also serves as a learning platform for performing groups to hone their craft and perfect the intricate art of production.

And in 2025, PST is pulling out all the stops, in May, June, July, and September, with five mesmerising showcases, each representing a different thread in Malaysia’s vibrant cultural tapestry:

  1. Ghazal Music Titled “Irama Ghazal Johor” By Ghazal Johor Network On 23 & 24 May 2025
  2. Cantonese Chinese Opera Titled “Irama Lingnan” By Pat Woh Association Of Malaysia On 28 & 29 June 2025
  3. University Of Malaya Arts Group With Malay Dance Titled “Temasya Tari Malayu: Lama Dalam Baharu” On 25 & 26 July 2025
  4. Indian Classical Dance Titled “Parampara” By Angika Fine Arts On 6 & 7 September 2025
  5. The Last Performance Of The Work Of The Kedah Creative Artists Association, Bringing The Jikey Langkawi Theatre “Kembara Putera” On 26 & 27 September 2025


Photo Credit: JKKN

The Grand Kickoff: Irama Ghazal Johor (23 & 24 May 2025)

The excitement begins with the soul-stirring beauty of Irama Ghazal Johor, presented by the Ghazal Johor Network—and you won’t want to miss this one.

This special performance marks the grand opening of PST2025, set for 23 May 2025 at 8:30 PM, and a prestigious Launching Ceremony, on the 24th May 2025 at 8:30 PM, attended by none other than YBhg. Dato’ Shaharuddin bin Abu Sohot, Secretary-General of the Ministry of Tourism, Arts, and Culture Malaysia.

But the real magic begins once the harmoniums start humming.

Ghazal, one of Johor’s proudest musical traditions, is a rich fusion of poetry and music that stretches back through generations.

Founded by the legendary Colonel Musa Yusoff, better known as Pak Lomak (regarded as the 'Father of Johor Ghazal'), this genre has long been a vessel of cultural expression and soulful storytelling.


Photo Credit: JKKN


Originally performed by a group of seven musicians playing the Harmonium, Gambus, Sitar, Violin, Tabla, Tambourine, and Maracas, alongside male and female vocalists, ghazal performances are known for their lyrical depth, singing praises of the divine, the wonders of nature, and the glory of heritage.

Unlike the romantic pop tunes we hear on the radio, ghazal speaks to something more eternal.

For PST2025, “Irama Ghazal Johor” comes to life in a powerful mini orchestra format presented in three enthralling segments:

  • Traditional Ghazal: A nostalgic return to the roots, showcasing the essence of Johorean musical heritage.

  • Contemporary Ghazal: A reimagining of ghazal infused with modern influences—proving that tradition evolves, but never fades.

  • Diverse Ghazal: A cross-cultural twist featuring multilingual expressions of ghazal art, embracing Malaysia’s melting pot of traditions.


Photo Credit: JKKN


Expect to be mesmerised by the poetic depth, rhythmic intricacies, and hypnotic harmonies of this performance.

Whether you’re new to ghazal or grew up with its soothing sounds echoing through family gatherings, this is a must-see moment in PST2025’s lineup.

It’s not just a show—it’s a cultural homecoming. Bring your parents, your kids, your friends—heck, bring your whole kampung! Let them witness Johor’s musical soul on full display.

The entrance fee for premier seating is RM70, and regular seating is RM30. For more information or reservations, you can call:

  • Puan Aznina at 012-7926923

  • Or Cik Norihan at 014-7759281 


Photo Credit: JKKN

Stay Tuned for More!

While Irama Ghazal Johor kicks off PST2025 with grace and grandeur, the journey doesn't end there—it's only the beginning.

With four more spectacular showcases on the horizon, from the dramatic elegance of Cantonese opera to the hypnotic rhythm of classical Indian dance and the cheeky charm of Jikey theatre, each performance promises a cultural adventure you won’t want to miss.

So, mark your calendars and keep your eyes on the stage—PST2025 is just getting warmed up!

Want more info?

  • Visit www.jkkn.gov.my
  • Or follow JKKN on Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, and TikTok at @mysenibudaya



Photo Credit: JKKN


Let’s Keep the Flame Burning

Our heritage isn’t just a relic of the past—it’s the rhythm of who we are. As globalisation zips us into the future, PST2025 lovingly reminds us of our roots, our stories, and our shared identity.

Let’s not let our traditional arts fade into whispers. Let’s dance, sing, laugh, and learn together. Let’s make sure that future generations don’t just remember the arts—they live them.

Join us at PST2025. Feel the pulse of Malaysia.

Because culture, dear friends, never goes out of style.

items.title: MERDEKA 118: A NEW ICON OF MALAYSIA'S SKYLINE AND SPIRIT
items.content:
As the vibrant nation of Malaysia strides confidently into a new era, the architectural wonder of Merdeka 118 serves as both a towering symbol of ambition and a heartfelt tribute to the past.

Rising majestically above the skyline of Kuala Lumpur, the tower represents more than just an architectural feat; it is an embodiment of national pride, cultural significance, and a beacon of unity for the diverse fabric of Malaysian society.

With its striking design and impressive height, Merdeka 118 stands as a testament to the spirit of resilience and progress that defines the nation.

Officially opened in 2024, Merdeka 118 was conceived to commemorate Malaysia's hard-won independence.

The name "Merdeka" translates to "freedom" in Malay, a word that echoes the fervent aspirations of a people who have journeyed through history to carve out their own identity.

At an astounding height of 679 meters, Merdeka 118 not only claims the title of the tallest building in Southeast Asia but also ranks as the second tallest in the world—a striking achievement that reflects the country's ambition to be a leader on the global stage.

The design of Merdeka 118 is laden with symbolic significance, intricately weaving together the values and history of Malaysia.

One of the core inspirations for its architectural form is the iconic gesture of Tunku Abdul Rahman, the nation’s first Prime Minister, when he declared independence on August 31, 1957.

In a moment that is forever etched in the hearts and minds of Malaysians, Tunku Abdul Rahman raised his hand and announced "Merdeka!" to a jubilant crowd.

This outstretched hand has been immortalized in the tower’s design, capturing an essence of freedom, hope, and unity.

The towering spire of Merdeka 118 mirrors this gesture, serving as a constant reminder of the momentous occasion and the collective spirit of a nation.

As a cultural and architectural landmark, Merdeka 118 is also poised to play a significant role in the storytelling of Malaysia's contemporary narratives.

Notably, the tower is set to make a noteworthy appearance in the upcoming Marvel Studios film "Thunderbolts."

This decision underscores its importance beyond mere functionality; by incorporating Merdeka 118 into cinematic narratives, filmmakers have the chance to showcase not only its stunning architectural grandeur but also its embodiment of Malaysia's identity.

"Thunderbolts" delves into themes of redemption, teamwork, and the complexities of heroism as a group of anti-heroes and reformed villains band together for a mission which may require them to confront their pasts and fight their own inner demons.

The film's incorporation of Merdeka 118 into its storyline serves as a backdrop for this journey of self-discovery and unity—a fitting parallel to the ideals represented by the tower itself.

By using such a culturally significant location, the film connects local and international audiences to the essence of Malaysia, enhancing the cinematic experience with a visual representation of the nation's past while also serving as a lens on its future.

In this modern age where globalization often challenges local identities, Merdeka 118 stands as an unwavering pillar of strength and pride.

It symbolizes the commitment of the Malaysian people to embrace diversity while remaining united in their pursuit of progress.

The tower embodies the essence of the nation's motto, "Unity is Strength," portraying a collective identity that transcends individual differences.

It is a place where various cultural narratives converge, fostering dialogue and interaction among the diverse populations that make up Malaysian society.

In conclusion, Merdeka 118 is far more than just a stunning structure that graces the skyline of Kuala Lumpur; it is a powerful narrative of a nation, intertwining history, culture, and aspirations into its very fabric.

As it towers proudly above the city, the building beckons Malaysians and the world alike to reflect on the values of freedom and unity that it so brilliantly embodies, while also inviting audiences to engage with its story through avenues like film.

The synergy between Merdeka 118 and "Thunderbolts" exemplifies how architecture and art can intertwine to communicate a broader trajectory of hope and resilience.

items.title: ART IN THE CITY: A ONE-DAY WALKING TOUR OF KUALA LUMPUR'S HIDDEN GEMS FOR ART LOVERS
items.content:
Kuala Lumpur, the vibrant capital of Malaysia, is a melting pot of cultures, traditions, and artistic expressions waiting to be discovered.

For art lovers, a curated walking tour around the city's hidden gems provides a unique opportunity to explore both contemporary and traditional art while immersing yourself in its lively atmosphere.

Explore Kuala Lumpur's vibrant art scene in just one day!

Start in the lively Bukit Bintang area and uncover the city's most captivating art destinations.

Don't miss out—let's dive into the creativity of KL!

Check out KL The Guide's Instagram

 

Starting Point: MRT to Bukit Bintang

Begin your adventure by hopping on the MRT to Bukit Bintang, an area known for its high-energy vibe and diverse attractions.

Located in the heart of the city, Bukit Bintang is your gateway to a day filled with art, culture, and creativity.

As you exit the station, the urban landscape around you buzzes with excitement, with trendy cafes, shops, and street performances setting the stage for what lies ahead.

 

MinNature: A Miniature Paradise

Your first stop is MinNature, only a 6-minute walk from the MRT station.

This incredible miniature model exhibition celebrates the rich cultural heritage of Malaysia and Southeast Asia.

Here, you'll be captivated by intricately crafted dioramas that recreate iconic landmarks, traditional villages, and cultural scenes.

Each miniature tells a story, highlighting the diversity of the region through its architecture, clothing, and daily life.

As you wander through the exhibits, take the time to appreciate the meticulous craftsmanship and the narratives behind each piece.

MinNature offers a unique introduction to Malaysia's art scene, combining elements of art, history, and storytelling.

Credit by MinNature Malaysia

Ur-Mu @ Bukit Bintang: An Urban Gallery Experience

Next, make your way to Ur-Mu, which is just a 10-minute walk from MinNature.

This contemporary gallery focuses on showcasing emerging artists and pushing the boundaries of traditional art forms.

As you step inside, you’ll be greeted by rotating exhibitions that feature thought-provoking installations, interactive art, and multimedia presentations.

Each visit promises a new experience, making Ur-Mu a must-visit for art aficionados seeking fresh perspectives in a dynamic setting.

Credit by Ur-Mu

Alor Backspace Street Art: An Urban Canvas

As you continue your journey, make your way to Alor Backspace, a 4-minute walk from Ur-Mu.

This hidden gem is known for its outdoor street art, adorned with stunning murals and graffiti that showcase the talents of local artists.

Each artwork tells a story or makes a social commentary, and the vibrant colors and intricate designs come together to create an urban canvas that is nothing short of inspiring.

Take your time to roam the streets, capture some snapshots, and engage with the local art community.

 

REXPERIENCE: Engaging Art and Events

From Alor Backspace, embark on a 20-minute walk to REXPERIENCE, a creative space that hosts a diverse range of art-related events, from workshops to exhibitions.

Often featuring local artists, this vibrant venue provides a platform for community engagement and artistic expression.

Check the schedule to see if any events align with your visit—whether it's a painting workshop or a live performance, participating can deepen your appreciation for the local art scene.


Illusion 3D Art Museum: A Fun Artistic Experience

To conclude your artistic exploration, head over to the Illusion 3D Art Museum, which is a 9-minute walk from REXPERIENCE.

This whimsical space offers interactive 3D artworks that encourage you to pose and create fun, memorable photos with incredible backgrounds.

It's an ideal spot for those looking to blend art with entertainment, and it guarantees a few laughs along the way as you become part of the artwork itself.


Wrapping Up: MRT to Bukit Bintang

After a day filled with creativity and discovery, making your way back to the MRT station in Bukit Bintang wraps up an enriching experience.

The return journey is approximately 30 minutes, giving you time to reflect on the day’s artistic adventures.

Kuala Lumpur’s art scene is as diverse and dynamic as its cultural landscape, offering endless opportunities for exploration.

Whether you’re a seasoned art lover or a casual observer, this one-day walking tour is designed to unveil the hidden gems that make the city a true artistic hub.

Embrace the rich tapestry of artistic expression that Kuala Lumpur has to offer, and leave inspired by the creativity that thrives in every corner of this incredible city.

items.title: EXPERIENCE THE FLAVOURS OF INDIA AT JAIPUR MAHAL RESTAURANT
items.content:
If you’re searching for an authentic Indian dining experience that tantalizes your taste buds with vibrant flavours and spices, look no further than Jaipur Mahal Restaurant. 

Renowned for its exquisite cuisine and warm ambience, this culinary gem promises to transport you straight to the heart of India with every bite. 


A Culinary Journey Through India

Jaipur Mahal Restaurant prides itself on offering a menu celebrating India's rich culinary heritage. 

From the aromatic curries of the north to the fiery delicacies of the south, every dish is crafted with precision and passion by chefs who understand the art of authentic Indian cooking.

Credit to Jaipur Mahal

A Feast for Every Plate

Whether you’re a seasoned lover of Indian food or a curious first-timer, the extensive menu at Jaipur Mahal has something for everyone:

Credit to Jaipur Mahal 

  • Tandoori Specialties: Savor the smoky, char-grilled flavours of tender meats and vegetables cooked to perfection in a traditional clay oven. 
  • Rich Curries: Dive into bowls of creamy Butter Chicken, flavorful rogan josh, or spicy Vindaloo, which pair perfectly with fluffy naan or fragrant basmati rice.

Adorned with vibrant colours, intricate patterns, and traditional Indian art, the setting exudes a regal charm that enhances your dining experience. 

Credit to Jaipur Mahal

Whether you’re planning a romantic dinner, a family gathering, or a celebration with friends, Jaipur Mahal provides the perfect backdrop.

Why you should visit the Jaipur Mahal?

What sets Jaipur Mahal apart is its commitment to authenticity and quality.

From the carefully sourced ingredients to the meticulous preparation of each dish, every aspect of your meal is crafted to provide an unforgettable culinary experience.

Whether you’re a fan of bold, spicy flavours or prefer milder options, Jaipur Mahal caters to all taste preferences. 

It’s a place where the rich traditions of Indian cuisine come alive, making every visit a celebration of food, culture, and hospitality.

items.title: CELEBRATING RONA RAYA: A VIBRANT FESTIVITY AWAITS
items.content:
Credit by Sungei Wang Plaza

As the holy month of Ramadan draws near, the festive spirit of Hari Raya is set to be celebrated in full swing with the much-anticipated Rona Raya Campaign.

From March 14 to April 13, 2025, visitors can dive into a world bursting with cultural richness, dazzling displays, and heartwarming traditions.

This campaign invites Malaysians and visitors alike to immerse themselves in the vibrancy of Raya through stunning batik décor, mesmerizing fashion shows, and interactive workshops that showcase the country’s artistic heritage.

The Grand Launch of Rona Raya was held on March 19, 2025, generating significant excitement.

Distinguished guests included Yang Berbahagia Dato’ Rohaizi Bahari, represented by Mohd Afandi Mohd Isa, and Encik Ahmad Fadhullah Fauzi, President of the Association of Malaysian Optometrists, along with media representatives and members of Sungei Wang Plaza’s Management Committee.

The event featured vibrant cultural performances, the official launch of the Raya campaign, and a CSR initiative offering Free Eye Checkups.

Attendees enjoyed a spectacular fashion show by Pelita Mice, showcasing collections from The Batik Shop, and the celebration concluded with a Buka Puasa session that included media representatives and underprivileged children, fostering a spirit of giving and togetherness, amplified by a special performance from the 1119 Dance Crew.

Sungei Wang Plaza further demonstrated its community commitment by providing free prescription glasses to underprivileged students, emphasizing the importance of vision for academic success.

Hari Raya Fiesta: The festivities will commence with the enchanting Hari Raya Fiesta at the Main Entrance Foyer and Court A in the Centre Court.

These workshops offer an opportunity to engage with local artisans and embrace the creative spirit of Raya.

 

Rona Raya Happenings

The Rona Raya Happenings will light up the Centre Court with an exciting lineup of events, tailored to entertain and inspire.

On March 29, the day unfolds with the glamour of the Face of Malaysia Audition at 10 AM, leading into the Ramadhan Fashion Show at 4 PM, where designers showcase their latest Raya collections.

Subsequently, children will have the wonderful opportunity to display their musical talents at Tiny Hands, Big Melodies on March 30th at 2 PM.

The celebratory atmosphere peaks on April 1 at 1 PM with the Raya Fashion Showcase, followed by the majestic Glam Raya Fashion Show 2025 at 12 PM on April 5.

Credit by Sungei Wang Plaza

Additionally, indulge in the Rhythm of Ukulele Music on April 6 at 2 PM, and wrap up the celebrations with the Raya Fit Fest on April 12 and 13 at 10 AM, focusing on health, fitness, and holistic well-being as we transition from the festivities of Ramadhan to the joyous celebrations of Raya.

Participating in the Rona Raya campaign is not just about enjoying the festivities; there's also a chance to indulge in exciting redemptions!

Visit the Information Centre on the ground floor and receive a Rona Raya packet with a minimum spend of RM150 (or RM100 for Tonton subscribers).

Credit by Sungei Wang Plaza

Additionally, enjoy complimentary vouchers when you spend RM10 or more at any F&B store (T&Cs apply).

This is the perfect opportunity to explore local culinary delights while enjoying exclusive access to local dramas and content through one week of free access to TontonUp upon scanning their QR code.

The Rona Raya Campaign is brought to life with the support of media partner Tonton and event partners such as JUMPA and The Batik Shop, ensuring a cohesive and culturally rich experience for all festival-goers.

Credit by Sungei Wang Plaza

In summary, the Rona Raya Campaign is more than just a celebration; it is an invitation to experience Malaysia's rich heritage, community spirit, and the joy of coming together as one.

items.title: THE MAGIC OF PLASTIC SURGERY AT THE SOMA PLASTIC SURGERY CLINIC
items.content:
In today's society, individuals seek plastic surgery for various reasons, primarily driven by personal aspirations, psychological factors, and societal influences.

Many people desire to enhance their appearance to boost self-esteem and confidence.

Commonly perceived physical flaws can lead to insecurities, further influenced by societal beauty standards.

Others might opt for plastic surgery for reconstructive purposes following trauma or congenital issues.

Ultimately, the choice is deeply personal, reflecting a complex interplay of individual aspirations and societal expectations.

At the Soma Plastic Surgery Clinic, the focus is on enhancing lives through expert plastic surgery procedures tailored to each individual’s needs. 

They prioritize patient satisfaction and well-being, engaging in detailed consultations to empower our clients in their decision-making process. 

Their commitment combines skill, artistry, and a deep understanding of the emotional nuances of transformation, fostering a supportive environment throughout every patient’s journey.

Let’s have a look at how they perform facelifts.

Facelift

Credit by SJ Clinical

A facelift is a cosmetic surgical procedure designed to rejuvenate the face by addressing visible signs of aging, such as sagging skin, deep creases, and jowls. 

It is a procedure that not only rejuvenates an individual’s physical appearance but also enhances emotional well-being. 

Understanding the process, recognizing the ideal candidates, being aware of the intricacies of recovery, and acknowledging the emotional impacts are crucial for anyone considering this transformative surgery. 

At the Soma Plastic Surgery Clinic, our dedicated team is committed to providing personalized care and exceptional results, ensuring a positive experience throughout every step of the journey.

 

Understanding the procedure

During the initial consultation, a thorough evaluation is conducted, assessing factors like skin elasticity, muscle tone, and facial anatomy to create a personalized treatment plan that aligns with the patient's desires and expectations.

The surgery typically lasts between two to four hours and involves removing excess skin while simultaneously tightening the underlying muscles and connective tissues. 

An incision is done at the hairline near the temple, extending along a natural skin fold down in front of the ear, around the earlobe, and then behind the ear, concluding at the scalp’s hairline. 

The surgeon will then detach the skin from the underlying fat and muscle layers. Afterward, the skin is lifted upwards and backwards, allowing for the removal of any excess skin. 

Credit by SJ Clinical

Who is a candidate for facelifts

Most candidates are generally in their 40s to 80s, but individuals outside this age group may also be eligible, depending on their specific circumstances. 

Good overall health is crucial, as candidates should ideally be non-smokers and free from medical conditions that could complicate the healing process. 

They would have to have good bone structure and whose skin still has some elasticity. 

Finally, they are people who are interested in removing traces of aging on the face and or neck.

 

The recovery process

Patients often experience swelling, bruising, and discomfort initially, but these symptoms typically diminish within 2- 3 weeks. 

At Soma Plastic Surgery Clinic, surgeons provide comprehensive post-operative care instructions, which include recommendations for pain management, activity restrictions, and proper care for the surgical sites. 

Most individuals can return to normal daily activities within approximately two weeks; however, it is advisable to avoid strenuous activities and direct sun exposure during the initial healing phase. 

Regular follow-up appointments with the surgeon are essential to monitor the recovery process and address any concerns, ensuring that patients achieve the best possible outcome.

Credit by SJ Clinical

The emotional impact of facelifts

Many individuals choose this procedure to enhance their self-esteem and confidence. 

The desire for a more youthful and revitalized appearance can significantly improve one’s self-image, leading to positive changes in personal and professional interactions. 

The motivation behind seeking a facelift commonly stems from the concern over aging and the wish to regain a youthful appearance, which can alleviate feelings of self-consciousness that may arise from visible signs of aging.

Credit by SJ Clinical

Reviews and testimonials from satisfied patients can be seen here, offering insight into the exceptional care and personalized attention received at the Soma Plastic Surgery Clinic. 

Many individuals share their transformative experiences, highlighting the professionalism and dedication of the team. 

Facelifts transcend being merely a cosmetic procedure; it is a pathway to achieving aesthetic goals while enhancing overall self-confidence.

If you're considering a facelift, schedule a consultation today to take the first step toward realizing the body you’ve always envisioned.

Credit by SJ Clinical

Taking this step could lead to significant changes and a renewed sense of self.
